No overshoot: the last two points are the highest on the whole track. The chain also accepts this one (is_stm 1), and I agree with it independently.
evidence: 65.7 cm chain entering 0.9 cm from the x face at (339,-253,93) and stopping at (282,-232,103), 57.6 cm from the nearest face - comfortably contained. The dQ/dx is as clean as it gets on this set: the plateau over s=20-65 sits at 4.5-6.5e4 and the band climbs without a break to 8.3e4 at s=11, 9.1-9.8e4 over s=3-6 and 1.00-1.09e5 in the last 2 cm, following the shape of the muon reference curve and topping out just under it. The last points are the highest ones, so there is no terminal collapse and the pin stays on the fit end. Past the stop the negative axis carries forty big points from magnitude 1 to 17 cm at 1.0-5.2e4, i.e. at and below MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at a third of MIP, so this is a second particle, and 15 cm at 35 MeV is the right range for a Michel. All three azimuths show it as one continuous arm leaving the very star at about 83 degrees to the muon body and running ~15 cm with its own two vertex squares, attached rather than bridged, so 86001 and 86003 are both michel. 357004 is a 4-point 1.5 cm speck at 29008 e/cm, 23.6 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.34; in c, d and e it sits just beyond the far end of the Michel arm and on the same side, detached by a clear charge gap, which is the faint-speck-on-the-Michel-side case, so gamma and kind both rather than attached. f_meas shows the arm as real measured charge in all three planes with near-white difference panels, and the nearest dead channels (U 2115, V 5960, W 10220) are all far from the stop at U 2085 / V 5860 / W 10155.

265 cm, enters 10.2 cm from the y face, stops 73.8 cm from the z wall. Bragg to 1.3e5 on the muon curve, MCS amb 0.00. A 14.3 cm arm at 3.9e4 e/cm leaves the stop sideways-back (cos_fwd -0.57) with profile charge to -12 cm; the charge and range are a Michel's, and at 14 cm it is far too long to be a delta from a stopping muon.

notes: No undershoot: the forward-side arm starts at about 6.9e4, i.e. near MIP rather than several times it, and the piece is 11.5 cm not a couple of cm. No overshoot: the last point is the maximum. The chain also accepts this one (is_stm 1) and I agree independently. The only judgement call was the 53-60 cm speck shell, gamma vs delta / other, which does flip the kind between both and attached here; I went delta / other because in two of the three azimuths those pieces lie opposite to the arm.
evidence: 222.2 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face at (261,-112,298) and stopping deep at (155,-92,117), 116.5 cm from the nearest face, so containment is not in question. The outward segment ladder is monotone into the stop - 68008 23679 at 206-211 cm back, 68010 48825, 68011 55128, 68020 91934 over the last 5.4 cm - and the 4x g_dqdx matches it point for point: a 4.5-6e4 plateau from s=40 to s=100, climbing through 6-7e4 at s=15-30 and 7-8.5e4 at s=5-12 to 9.2-9.5e4 at s=1-3 and 1.35e5 at the last point, sitting on the muon reference curve over the last 20 cm. The final point is the highest on the track, so there is no terminal collapse and the pin stays where the fit put it. Past the stop, 68021 is a 20-point 11.5 cm arm leaving the very star: the c-frame zoom shows it as a blue bead chain attached at the stop vertex and separated from the green muon body by a clean charge-free lane, running off at 82 degrees with its own end vertex, carrying 48891 e/cm mean and 2.0-6.9e4 point by point - at and below MIP, which a muon that has just reached 1.35e5 cannot do, and 11.5 cm at 27.4 MeV is the right range for a Michel. So the item is STM_MICHEL and the kind is attached. The five small unassigned pieces (C191, 202019, 200018, 196015, 194014) all sit in a 53-60 cm shell, but they are not on the Michel side: the arm leaves the star to the right and up in d, whereas the specks project down-left in c and d and split into two groups by angle (cos_fwd +0.22 to +0.5 for three of them, -0.40 and -0.41 for the other two), i.e. scattered in unrelated directions around the 60 cm ring rather than along the arm - delta / other, and the kind stays attached rather than both. Note 202019 carries 109385 e/cm in a 0.5 cm two-point speck, but charge is not a criterion for this call and its direction is not the arm direction. f_meas puts the stop at U 2265, V 6000, W 10490 with the nearest dead channels at U 2285, V 6055 and W 10410, and the difference panels are near white.

notes: Hard call two ways. (1) The terminal dip: four points below plateau spanning 2.3 cm looks like the overshoot signature until you notice three of them are at essentially zero charge and there is nothing at dstop 0 for the fit to have bridged to. Pin left at the fit end; if the owner counts near-zero terminal points as a real bridge this item becomes an overshoot with the pin near rr 3.0. (2) The 229006/229007 blob is ~13 MeV of electron-like charge over 6 cm, which is Michel-scale, and if its first centimetres simply were not imaged this becomes STM_MICHEL / attached; I went with gamma because the 11.6 cm gap to the stop is clean and an electron cannot start 11 cm from the muon it came from. The chain body-excluded it, but at 10 cm off the body line that exclusion is not what decided me.
evidence: 33 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the y face and the fit ends 24.9 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. The dQ/dx profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau from s=33 back to s~12, climbs through 7e4 at s~12, 8-8.5e4 at s=5-9 and reaches 0.98-1.17e5 at s=3.4-4.3, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve, so this is a real Bragg rise and the chain's no_bragg/shape_flat rejection is wrong. The last four points then fall away: 3.2e4 at s=2.3 and three points at 0.4-1.2e4 over the last 1.2 cm. I considered moving the pin for a peak-then-collapse but did not, on two grounds. Those three lowest points are at 7-22 percent of the plateau, essentially no measured charge, which is the class the rubric says to ignore as fit points rather than read as a bridge; once they are dropped the only survivor below the plateau is a single 3.2e4 point at 0.58 of MIP, i.e. one partial-charge point at the very end, which is the explicit leave-the-pin-alone case. And there is no destination: the fit bridges a gap to something, and here no object row sits at dstop near zero, with the chain reporting n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0. So the stop stays at the fit's last point. Past/near it the substantial object is the 229006+229007 pair, one blob of 21 points over ~6 cm at 4.9e4 and 1.6e4, centroid 12.6 cm from the fit end, 7.7 cm back along the body but 10.0 cm off the muon body line by direct 3-D projection of the centroid onto the entry-to-stop axis, confirmed by the d and e azimuths where it stands clearly off the amber band. It is detached: d_min 11.6 cm with a clean charge-free gap to the stop, so by the attachment tie-break it is a detached compact piece, gamma, not the Michel. 230008 sits at cos_fwd -1.0, d 15-20 cm, right on the body line: delta / other. The two 3-point survey specks 227004/228005 at 38 and 42 cm are 4.8 cm from each other in the same forward direction at z~62-66, reading as two pieces of one unrelated distant object rather than isolated capture gammas, so delta / other. No dead channel band touches the track at the stop in U, V or W.

notes: Not the ordinary flat-to-the-end THRU: the profile actively collapses over the last 15 cm to a fifth of the plateau. That is not the rubric's overshoot signature either, because there is no peak before the collapse -- the charge just fades from MIP into nothing, which reads as the track leaving through a poorly imaged or dead region rather than stopping. Either way there is no Bragg rise, so THRU.
evidence: 150.8 cm six-segment chain entering in the far corner 1.2 cm from a face and running diagonally to a fit end 19.9 cm from the z wall and 106 cm from the cathode. The dQ/dx profile holds a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in to s~15, then does the opposite of a Bragg: it declines monotonically over the last 15 cm, 3.8e4 at s=13, 3.2e4 at s=10, 2.6e4 at s=7, 2.0e4 at s=5, 1.4e4 at s=3, 0.95e4 at s=2, with only a small 2.85e4 tick on the very last point. Nothing ever climbs above the track's own plateau, let alone follows the muon curve, so there is no Bragg rise at the fit end and by the operative test this is a through-goer. The colour of the 3-D point cloud says the same thing independently of the panel: the spine is green over most of its length and turns cyan then blue over the last 20 cm into the star, in all three azimuths. The c and e frames show a single clean smoothly curving spine with nothing attached at the star and nothing detached anywhere near it, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). In f_meas the last stretch to the stop is nearly all dark in U, V and W, and there is a dead U channel band immediately alongside the track's final channels, which is a plausible reason the charge faded out where it did. The only unassigned row, 55010, is a 3-point 1.5 cm speck 132 cm back at cos_fwd -0.96, sitting on the muon body far from any stop, so delta / other.

notes: This is the most flip-prone call in my twelve. The rubric collides with itself here. The attribution tie-break says a piece with a clean charge-free gap to the stop is a detached dot, gamma, however close it sits, and its worked example is a piece 9.4 cm out -- exactly this d_min. The undershoot section says a short forward piece at or below MIP whose charge falls as it goes out is a real Michel and the ordinary STM_MICHEL case, which also describes this object, though that passage is written about a piece attached at dstop of a couple of cm. I went with the tie-break because the gap is measured, clean, and not a dead region, and because an electron cannot cross 9.4 cm without depositing. If the owner reads it the other way this item is STM_MICHEL / attached with 527006 tagged michel; nothing else in the record changes.
evidence: 103.6 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from a face and ending 15.8 cm from the z wall, contained. The Bragg is real and easily the clearest in my chunk: a 5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to s~15, 7-8e4 at s=10-18, 9.2-9.6e4 at s=6.5-7.5, and a peak of 1.06e5, 1.10e5, 1.20e5 and 1.31e5 at s=4-6, following the shape of the muon curve, with the last point back at 9.4e4. Between s=1 and s=3.5 the points scatter hard (2.35e4, 3.4e4, 3.6e4, 5.2e4, 7.8e4), but that is scatter of a factor of three in both directions, not a sustained collapse, and the very last point is the second-highest of the tail at 9.4e4, so a muon still at 1.7x its own plateau reaches the fit end and the pin stays where it is. Past the stop the display draws exactly one thing: 527006, 5 points over 2.5 cm, mean 2.66e4 e/cm with its own points falling 6.4e4, 2.65e4, 1.25e4, 0.75e4 as they go out, sitting 9.4-11.4 cm from the stop, 8.6 cm forward along the muon direction and 5.6 cm off its axis by direct projection. Charge at half MIP and falling outward is electron-like and this is the chain's own Michel object, but it is separated from the stop by 9.4 cm of empty space, which the chain itself calls a bridge rather than a graph edge. f_meas shows that gap is real and not an imaging hole: in all three planes the blob sits about 30 time slices past the end of the track at the same channels, and no dead band lies between them, so charge would have been recorded if a charged particle had crossed it. A 4.8 MeV electron has a range of about 2.4 cm, which matches the 2.5 cm core exactly and rules out its having travelled 9.4 cm invisibly, so what crossed the gap was neutral. Detached, compact, past the stop and clear of the body line: gamma, and by the rubric an isolated compact capture gamma does not promote the item to STM_MICHEL.

notes: Unambiguous stopper, but with nothing at all past the end, so the interesting content is the chain's rejection rather than the verdict: plateau_off_mip fires because the whole visible track is Bragg, which is a rejection reason that will misfire on every short low-energy entering stopper.
evidence: Short 23.7 cm single-segment track that enters 0.1 cm from the y wall and stops 7.5 cm inside it, moving inward in y the whole way. The dQ/dx is the cleanest Bragg in my twelve: it rides along the muon reference curve for its entire visible length, 8.2-8.3e4 at s=20-23, 9.3-9.5e4 at s=17-19, 1.00-1.05e5 at s=13-16, 1.10-1.15e5 at s=10-12, 1.20-1.28e5 at s=5-8, 1.44e5 at s=2.5 and 1.57-1.66e5 at s=0.5-1.5. The very last point falls back to 1.25e5, about 25 percent below the peak, which is exactly the ordinary-scatter case the rubric says to leave alone rather than a sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit end. This also explains the chain's plateau_off_mip rejection: there is no MIP plateau on this object because the entire 24 cm is inside the Bragg region, which is what a muon entering the wall with 84 MeV of kinetic energy looks like, and the chain's own range estimate of 83.9 MeV agrees with 23.7 cm of argon. The scattered low points at s=19-23 (1.25e4 up to 5.15e4) are at the entry end where the track crosses the wall, not at the stop. Nothing else is drawn: the object table has a single row, the three stop azimuths show a bare spine with nothing attached at the star and nothing detached anywhere around it, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. f_meas confirms the isolation -- one short high-charge streak per plane with no companion blob and no dead band within 45 channels of the stop. Stops inside with a Bragg rise and nothing past the end: STM_ONLY, kind none.

notes: Flat to the last point with no face contact -- THRU on the profile alone. The dead U and W channel bands at the fit end give an independent reason the cluster ended where it did.
evidence: 246.6 cm two-segment chain, straight as a ruler in all three azimuths, entering 0.2 cm from a face in the far corner at z=296, x=-340 and ending in open liquid 147.9 cm from the nearest wall and 150.6 cm from the cathode. This is the rubric's textbook case: containment says nothing, the profile decides. The dQ/dx holds a flat 5.5-6.5e4 plateau over its whole visible length and is still on that plateau at s=2-5; the only departure is a single 3.2e4 point at s=0, one low last point which is ordinary scatter and not a rise. Nothing anywhere climbs off the plateau toward the muon curve, which sits at 1.6e5 at the origin. The scattered 0.8-1.1e5 points at s=30, 74 and 87 are mid-track delta activity, not an end effect. A stopping muon cannot deposit at MIP to its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. f_meas supports that mechanically: the fit end sits at U channel 900 hard against broad dead U bands at 890-900 and 920-930, and the W end coincides with a dead W channel near 8490, so the imaging is exactly where the track disappears. The 3-D frames show a bare spine with no arm, no dot and no blob anywhere near the star, and the chain agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The single unassigned row 26005 is 9 points over 4.8 cm sitting 192-194 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the muon body far from any stop, so delta / other.

notes: Confidence medium, not high. The geometry is degenerate -- constant x and constant z, so the collection plane sees the whole 68 cm in about two channels -- and the absolute dQ/dx is a tenth of MIP everywhere, so the Bragg test is weak on this item. The verdict rests mainly on the forward stub being collinear at cos_fwd +0.94 in all three azimuths and carrying the same charge as the muon body rather than falling away like an electron. The competing reading is STM_MICHEL on the grounds that a Michel topology is sufficient without a Bragg peak and the chain calls 88009 pdg 11; I rejected it because a 20 degree, same-charge continuation is a continuation, not a decay. Process note: I first judged this item on five frames, having read the rubric when it said six PNGs and mis-set the c zoom against d and e; I went back and read d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop before finalising, and they confirmed rather than changed the call.
evidence: 68.3 cm chain running almost purely along y, from (272.6,-259.1,286.4) to (273.2,-190.2,285.8): x and z change by less than a centimetre over the whole length, so both listed d_face numbers, 12.1 at entry and 12.6 at the stop, are the sideways distance to the z wall that the track keeps all the way along, not a face it approached at either end. The dQ/dx profile is flat at 0.5-1.5e4 e/cm from s=68 in to the last point at s=0, an order of magnitude under MIP, with two smooth isolated humps at s=27-35 (3e4) and s=40-50 (6e4) in the middle and nothing at all at the end. There is no rise off its own plateau anywhere near the fit end and nothing that follows the muon curve. What sits past the fit end is 88009: 11 points over 6.0 cm at cos_fwd +0.94, d_min 0.0, carrying 6361 e/cm, which is the same charge as the adjacent muon segment 88010 at 7785. All three stop azimuths agree on its geometry: in the c frame, zoomed 5.5x, it is a short yellow stub carrying straight on from the purple last muon segment with a few more faint image points beyond it, and the d and e frames from their own angles show the same stub collinear with the spine and the same faint points continuing past it, so the collinearity is not a one-view projection effect. That is the rubric's stub carrying straight on past a fit end that is not a stop, and charge continuing past the fit end is itself a THRU, so it is tagged muon and the item is a through-goer despite the chain typing the stub pdg 11 and counting it as a stop arm. 464008 is a 2-point 0.5 cm speck 33 cm away at cos_fwd -0.35, isolated in an unrelated direction with no stop to be past, so delta / other. In f_meas the object collapses into two W channels around 10805 at an essentially constant time slice near 1520, which is the degenerate vertical-track geometry and is why the absolute charge scale here should not be trusted.

notes: Unambiguous: stop 0.1 cm from the y wall, out of the fiducial volume, MIP charge to the last measured point. No object other than the chain is drawn, so michel_kind is none by construction as well as by the THRU rule.
evidence: 64.4 cm single-segment chain entering 5.8 cm from a face and running straight to a fit end 0.1 cm from the y wall, with in_fv 0 and the chain's own stop_near_boundary flag set. The dQ/dx sits on a 4.5-6e4 plateau over the whole length with the usual wobble; the last few centimetres reach 6.4e4 at s=4 and 7.1e4 at s=5-6, but the same track already shows 6.5e4 at s=18 and 6.6e4 at s=51, so that is the top of its own scatter band and not a rise off the plateau, and it does not follow the muon curve, which is at 1.3e5 by s=2. From s=2 in the profile falls, 5.8e4 then 4.85e4 then 2.7-3.0e4 on the last two points, i.e. the charge is still at MIP when the track reaches the wall and then simply stops being measured. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot be at 3e4 on its last point. All three 3-D azimuths show a single bare spine with nothing attached at the star, nothing detached anywhere near it, and the object table has exactly one row, the chain itself, so there is no candidate Michel or gamma to weigh. In f_meas the track runs off the bottom of the drift window and its U channels sit inside a broad dead band around 2400-2440, both consistent with a track leaving the imaged volume rather than stopping. This is a through-goer that exits the y wall.

notes: The chain itself asserts a capture gamma 35 cm past the stop (1.74 MeV, 508014), which would be detached dots if this were a stopper. I am calling THRU on the profile, so by the rubric's THRU rule that row is delta / other and the kind is none. If the verdict were wrong this is the row that would flip the kind, but the profile leaves no room: MIP to the last point with the only high-charge points a third of the way back up the track.
evidence: 74.3 cm four-segment chain entering 1.2 cm from a face and running dead straight in all three azimuths to a fit end 15.4 cm from the y wall. The dQ/dx sits on a broad 4.0-5.5e4 band with an upper envelope around 6-7e4 for its whole length and is still there at the end: the last few centimetres read 5.1e4, 5.3e4, 4.5e4, 3.3e4 and 2.55e4, i.e. flat then slightly falling, with nothing climbing off the plateau and nothing following the muon curve, which is at 1.3e5 by s=2. The genuinely high points on this track, 1.05e5 to 1.25e5, are all at s=34-42, a third of the way back, so they are mid-track delta activity and not an end effect. A stopping muon cannot be at MIP on its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out 15 cm short of the wall. Nothing is attached at the star in any of the three stop azimuths. What the display draws around it is a scatter of ten two-point specks 33-53 cm out at cos_fwd from -0.45 to +0.94, sitting in every direction around the ring in the b and d frames, which is the scattered-in-unrelated-directions case, plus the chain's own capture-gamma candidate 508014 (5 points, 2.6 cm, 8277 e/cm, 35 cm out at cos_fwd +0.34) and 98011, a 5.2 cm pdg-11 shower piece lying on the muon body at cos_fwd -1.0, 26-29 cm back. On a through-goer there is no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so all of these are delta / other and the kind is none. f_meas shows no dead band at the fit end in U or V; the nearest W dead band is about 20 channels away.

notes: Medium, not high, and this is the row in my twelve I would most like a second opinion on. For THRU: no rise that stands out from this track's own scatter, a pronounced dip 10-20 cm before the end, a last point at a fifth of MIP, dead V and W channels one or two channels from the fit end, and the last 20 cm showing two interleaved strands that made the terminal shape harder to read than on any other item I scanned. Against THRU, and stronger than I first credited: the chain's range momentum (1146 MeV/c) and MCS momentum (1166 MeV/c) agree to 2 percent, and that agreement is corroborated by the lowest MCS ambiguity in my chunk, amb 0.05. I originally set this aside as the chain's own number rather than display evidence. Then on 039252_7/34, an item I judged THRU on independent and much harder grounds (exits 8 cm from the anode face, flat profile, no dead band), the same two momenta disagreed by a factor of 1.9 at amb 0.87. So in the two places I can check it in this chunk, the range-vs-MCS ratio behaves exactly as a stopping discriminator should, and here it points at a stopper. I kept THRU because the rubric makes the profile the operative test and the profile has no Bragg, but the owner should treat this as the flip candidate.
evidence: 453.5 cm six-segment chain, dead straight in every azimuth, entering 0.5 cm from a face in the far corner and ending 145.2 cm from the nearest wall. Its dQ/dx band is 5.0-6.0e4 with a wide scatter that reaches 1.0-1.2e5 repeatedly at s=22, 51 and 57 from delta rays. Reading the last 20 cm on a 4x crop: the profile does not build toward a peak, it dips, falling from 4.65e4 at s=20 along a smooth coherent strand to 1.95e4 at s=10, recovering to 4.6-5.8e4 at s=2.4-6.9, touching 7.9-8.6e4 at s=1.4-2.7 and then dropping to 1.2e4 on the last point. The 8.6e4 high is only 1.55x the local band and is well inside the scatter this track shows all along its length, so it is not a rise off the plateau in the shape of the muon curve, which is at 1.35e5 by s=1.5. There is no Bragg. f_meas, zoomed tight on the stop, shows why the charge disappears where it does: the last centimetres are dark blue in all three planes, and the fit end sits immediately against a dead V channel near 5440 and a dead W channel near 9390, one or two channels away in both. A track fading into dead channels in two of three planes is a through-goer that stopped being imaged, not a stopper. Nothing is attached at the star in any azimuth. 32022 is the only thing at the stop: 5 points over 2.4 cm at cos_fwd +0.85 carrying 1.17e4 e/cm, a fifth of MIP, and the chain itself types it pdg 13 and counts it inside the muon, so it is the last low-charge scrap of the fit rather than a decay product: muon. 32009 is 10 points over 5.4 cm sitting 423-426 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the body at the far entry end: delta / other.

notes: Clean THRU: flat to the last point, exiting 8 cm from the anode face, and the range-vs-MCS momentum disagreement (430 vs 806 MeV/c) independently says this muon did not stop. Worth noting as a cross-check the round could use: on my one deeply contained THRU with a strong stopping case against it (039252_7/32) those two momenta agreed to 2 percent, and here they disagree by a factor of 1.9. The MCS-vs-range ratio looks like a usable discriminator, but it is the chain's own number, not display evidence, so I did not let it decide either item.
evidence: 140.2 cm single-segment chain entering exactly at a face (d_face 0.0) at z=298 and running straight, with a gentle curve, to a fit end 8.0 cm from the anode face at x=-331.9. The end view puts the star hard against the x boundary of the drawn volume and f_meas puts the last measured point at time slice 1418, the short-drift end, so the track is heading into the anode plane rather than stopping in open liquid. The dQ/dx holds a 5.5-6.5e4 band along its whole 140 cm and does nothing special at the end: the last few centimetres read 5.35e4, 4.75e4, 4.05e4, 3.85e4 and 2.45e4, at or below the plateau. There is a mild lift at s=4-8 (8.55e4 and one point at 1.02e5) but that point has an exact twin at s=33 (1.015e5) and the track carries 8-9e4 points repeatedly out at s=73-95, so it is delta-ray scatter and not a rise off the plateau following the muon curve, which is at 1.1e5 by s=3. No Bragg rise at the fit end means through-goer. The chain's own kinematics agree with that even though its verdict does not: range gives 337 MeV of kinetic energy and 430 MeV/c, while MCS on the same track gives 707 MeV and 806 MeV/c, a factor of 2.4 in energy, which is what you get when a muon that has not stopped is assigned a range-based energy. All three stop azimuths show one bare spine, nothing attached at the star and nothing detached near it; the object table has a single row, the chain itself, and the chain reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. No dead channel band lies at the fit end in U, V or W, so the track is simply leaving through the anode.

notes: Neither undershoot nor overshoot; the Bragg peak is the fit last point. The only judgement calls were 117015 (michel, on a 0.35 cm gap that is inside the point spacing) and the three forward specks (gamma on the along-the-arm direction rather than delta on the random-ring reading); both are stated in the evidence.
evidence: 177 cm chain entering 9.7 cm inside the z face and stopping in the middle of the liquid - 120.4 cm from the anode, 194 cm from the y wall, 132 cm from the z wall - so containment is not in question and the three projections put the stop nowhere near an edge. The Bragg is textbook: the plateau runs 5.5-7e4 from s=100 in to s=20, lifts to 8-9e4 over s=5-10, reaches 1.09-1.14e5 at s=2-4 and the fit last point itself is a 1.36e5 red point sitting exactly on the muon reference curve, which is why the final chain segment 32009 carries a mean of 109348 over its 4.7 cm against 59557 for the 172.8 cm behind it. The pin needs no move in either direction: the peak is inside the fit, not past it, so the undershoot case does not arise, and there is no terminal collapse. Leaving the stop vertex at a 54 degree kink is a 20-point, 11.6 cm arm (32007) at a mean 41870, i.e. below MIP, with a 5-point 2.3 cm piece (117015) picking up 0.35 cm beyond its tip - contiguous within the point spacing, so michel rather than a detached dot - and the chain measures 30.4 MeV over it, exactly the right length and charge for a Michel; a muon on a 1.36e5 Bragg tip cannot then run 11.6 cm below MIP. Three further specks lie strung out along the same direction as that arm, within about 15 degrees of it: 114013 (4 points, 1.5 cm) at 29.7 cm, 115014 (2 points, 0.3 cm) at 32.2 cm and 113012 (2 points, 0.5 cm) at 58.0 cm, all detached and compact, all forward at cos_fwd 0.57-0.69, so they are gammas on the Michel side rather than randomly scattered ring specks, and the kind is both. 32010 is 6 points over 3.1 cm at only 11370 sitting at cos_fwd -0.96 across the 32009/32011 junction, i.e. squarely on the muon body line, so delta / other whatever the chain pdg 11 label says. f_meas has measured matching predicted along the whole track and no dead band within tens of channels of the stop in any plane.

notes: Flat-to-the-last-point THRU with no visible continuation, which the rubric explicitly allows: the cluster simply ran out where the imaging did, and the stop is 0.7 cm from the z face in any case. Charge and 3-D fit are both degraded because the track runs nearly along a wire direction (240 cm into ~40 W channels), which is why the profile oscillates rather than being smoothly flat; this does not change the verdict since there is no rise anywhere. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.

In c, d and e it reads as a short pale-blue (low dQ/dx) arc leaving the stop, mostly hidden behind the vertex squares. The two remaining rows are body activity: 124014, 3 points at 25 cm, sits 22.7 cm BACK along the muon at cos_fwd -0.90 and on a bearing 110 deg away from the Michel, and 36006 (9 pts, 4.6 cm, 4127 e/cm, chain-typed pdg 11 shower) lies 36 cm back dead on the body line at 3.4 cm transverse, cos_fwd -1.00 - both delta / other, neither past the stop. f_meas confirms a real stop: the dead-channel lines the track crosses are all mid-track (U ~190, V ~4000) and the last points at U 220 / V 4055 / W 7805 are well clear of any of them.

notes: medium for two reasons. First, the terminal two-point dip from 9.8e4 to 4.5e4 over the last 1.3 cm is the weakest form of the overshoot pattern; if it were read as a collapse the verdict would flip to STM_MICHEL with the pin near rr = 1.5, but there is no drawn object past the stop to be the Michel and the dip is too short, so I left it. Second, michel_kind rests entirely on one 2-point speck 20 cm off-axis - same configuration as the one on 039252_9/88, and I tagged it the same way for consistency.
evidence: 62 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and stopping 37.1 cm from the nearest z wall, 125 cm from the anode and 264 cm from the y wall - contained, and the three azimuths show one clean unbroken spine with nothing attached at the end. The profile leaves a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau at about s = 20 and climbs along the muon reference curve: 6.5-7.8e4 at s = 13-19, 8.0-8.5e4 at s = 4-8, 8.4e4 at s = 1.3 and a gold pair at 9.3-9.8e4 at s = 1.8-4.5. The last two points then fall back to 6.2e4 (s = 0.4) and 4.5e4 (s = 0.1). I left the pin where the fit put it: that dip spans about 1.3 cm and two points, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse the pin-move signature requires, and - decisively - there is no object at all past the stop for the fit to have bridged to (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the census lists exactly two rows), so there is no Michel candidate at the far side of any bridge. There is no forward high-charge tip either, so the undershoot does not apply. f_meas shows the track terminating at time slice 1140 in all three planes with the dead-channel bands well clear (nearest is the V band at 6040-6060 against a track end at 6080), so this is a real stop rather than a dead-region exit; a small puff of unfitted pale image points sits at the stop in c and d but carries no measurable charge and is not in the object census. The only other object is 180003, a 2-point 0.6 cm speck: taking the entry-to-stop chord its along-axis component is 0.0 and its transverse offset 19.7 cm, so it sits essentially in the stop plane, 20 cm clear of the muon body line and separated from the stop by a clean gap in all three azimuths - isolated, compact and on one bearing rather than several scattered round the ring, which is the gamma case; the chain calls it gamma body exclusion but off-axis separation outranks that label. A 0.6 cm two-point speck is not an electron, so the item stays STM_ONLY.

notes: medium not because the verdict is in doubt - it is a contained stopper with nothing past the end and michel_kind none is certain - but because the object is almost certainly not a muon: charges of 1.35-1.60e5 over the last 10 cm and a 6-8e4 body level are proton-like, the chain says not_muon_pid, and dQ/dx-vs-range energies disagree by 60 percent. Worth an eye if the round is counting muon stoppers.
evidence: 93 cm chain entering 0.4 cm inside the z face and stopping 63.8 cm from the anode, 67.2 cm from the z wall and 205 cm from the y wall - deeply contained, and b, c, d and e all show one straight unbroken spine with a star at one end, a green entry marker at the other and absolutely nothing attached past the stop. The profile rises hugely: a 6.0-8.5e4 level over s = 40-95, a sagging patch at 3-5e4 around s = 25-40, then a steep climb from s = 25 through 8.3e4 at s = 22, 1.0-1.2e5 at s = 12-22 and a run of points at 1.35-1.60e5 at s = 2-10, with the last points at 1.17-1.42e5. That is far more charge than the muon reference curve carries anywhere (it asymptotes to 1.6e5 only at s = 0), which is why the chain rejects this one not_muon_pid and why its dQ/dx energy, 377 MeV, sits 60 percent above the 236 MeV from range - the object is much more heavily ionizing than a muon and reads as a stopping proton or similar. For the rubric question that does not matter: this is unambiguously a stopping track with a large terminal rise. The peak sits a few centimetres before the fit last point and eases to 1.17e5 at the origin, but that is not the pin-move signature - the pin-move test is a collapse far BELOW the track own plateau, and 1.17e5 is still roughly twice the 6-8e4 this track carries in its body (a fall-off at the very tip is also what recombination does to a heavily ionizing particle), so the pin stays. 98010, the 3-point 1.2 cm piece at 1.23e5 sitting essentially at the stop (0.1 cm along, 0.6 cm transverse), is the muon own final centimetre and is tagged muon; it is not the undershoot tip, which has to lie clearly ahead at cos_fwd around +0.9. The only other objects are 370007 and 371008, at 45.6 and 36.8 cm from the stop but 44.6 and 33.6 cm BACK along the body at cos_fwd -0.97 and -0.91 with transverse offsets of 10.5 and 15.6 cm - body activity behind the stop, not past it, so neither can be a gamma in the ring and both are delta / other. f_meas shows the track crossing dead-channel lines mid-body (U ~3040, V ~6890) but the terminal charge peak is incompatible with a dead-region exit in any case.

notes: Fit end is 132 cm from every face with no visible continuation and no dead region under it, but the plateau runs flat to the last point - THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs.
evidence: A 310.9 cm essentially straight cosmic - the chord from entry to fit end is 283 cm - entering 10.1 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest face, so this is a containment-vs-profile case and the profile decides it. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a broad 4-6.5e4 plateau from s=100 all the way in, and over the last 20 cm they are 6.5e4, 6.9e4, 7.4e4 at s=10-15 then 4.6e4, 5.2e4, 5.5e4 at s=3-8 and 6.4e4, 5.0e4, 4.2e4, 3.8e4 at s=0-3. That is flat-to-slightly-falling into the fit end with no climb along the muon reference curve at all; the chain's own reject list says the same (no_bragg, shape_flat) and the flow summary reports nothing at the stop (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). The three stop azimuths show a pencil-thin uniform track running to the pin star with no arm, no dot and no widening near the end, and the b frame shows it crossing most of the drift volume. f_meas has the last hits clear of the dead-channel lines in U (bands at 1055-1075, 1140 and 1305-1330 are all well away from the track end) and V, so I cannot point to a dead-region exit - by the rubric a flat profile is enough on its own, and this cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. The three unassigned rows 25015, 25018 and 25021 are all 173-212 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1.00 and only 1-5 cm off the chord line, at 0.5-1.6e4 - body activity far from the end, so delta / other; no gamma tag, since a through-goer has no stop to define one.

notes: Competing reading was overshoot with the true stop at the s=11-13 spike; rejected because the spike is ~2 cm wide with plateau charge on both sides and the profile recovers to plateau afterwards instead of staying collapsed.
evidence: 165.9 cm of chain running almost parallel to the top y wall - it enters 2.4 cm from that face and the fit end is still only 13.2 cm below it, so an exit through the wall it has been hugging the whole way is entirely available. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 5-6.5e4 plateau from s=15 back to s=60, and coming in from s=20 they go 6.2e4, 6.3e4 at s=15-20, then 4.3-4.5e4 at s=6, 4.4-4.7e4 at s=2, 5.8-6.0e4 at s=3 and 3.6e4 at s=1: at or below plateau to the last point, no climb along the muon reference curve. What made this one medium rather than high is a narrow spike at s=11-13 - four points at 8.1e4, 9.2e4, 1.2e5 and 1.37e5 - which at first reading looks like a peak several cm before the fit end. I rejected the overshoot for two reasons: it is only about 2 cm wide with plateau values at 6.3e4 immediately outside it on the far side, which is a localised delta or blob rather than the gradual last-10-to-20-cm climb the rubric asks for; and the charge after it does not stay collapsed, it recovers to 4.4-6.0e4 by s=1-3, whereas the low-dQ/dx bridge the overshoot mechanism describes stays low all the way to the fit end. The same picture appears far back at s=60-100 where the chain carries 0.9-1.65e5 in patches, and f_meas shows why to distrust those: in U the track sits among hatched dead-channel bands at 1390-1420 and the brightest orange hits are right on them. The stop azimuths show a pencil track running to the pin star with no arm and no widening. The chain itself rejects with no_bragg and shape_flat and reports nothing at the stop. 124013 is a 2-point 0.1 cm speck the chain calls a capture gamma 26 cm out and 121012 a 2-point speck 10.6 cm out, but a through-goer has no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so both are delta / other, as are 35003 and 35008, which lie 106-126 cm back essentially on the body line.

notes: Hardest part was the 1.47e5 hump 8.5 cm before the fit end; rejected as a delta because it is more than twice the muon reference curve at that residual range and the profile returns to plateau behind it.
evidence: 243.4 cm of chain, entering 14.7 cm from the z face and ending 101.1 cm from the nearest wall, so again the profile has to decide. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 4.5-6.5e4 plateau all the way in from s=100. Coming into the end there is a hump: 6.6e4 at s=12, 8.1e4 and 1.03e5 at s=10, then 9.4e4, 1.33e5 and 1.47e5 at s=8.5, then straight back down to 7.5e4 at s=7 and 5.2-6.0e4 - i.e. plateau - through s=3 to s=5, before the last two centimetres tail off through 4.3e4, 3.4e4, 2.7e4, 2.1e4 to 1.55e4 at the fit's last point. I read the hump as a delta ray, not a Bragg peak, on the rubric's own scale argument: the overlaid muon curve is only about 6.8e4 at 8.5 cm of residual range, real stoppers top out at 1.2-1.35e5 and only in their last centimetre, and these points sit at more than twice the curve where they are - a stopping muon cannot be at 1.47e5 with 8.5 cm still to run. The profile also recovers to full plateau for two centimetres after the hump, which the low-charge bridge in the overshoot mechanism does not do. So there is no rise above the plateau in the last 10-20 cm and the item is a through-goer; the final 2 cm tail is where the imaging ran out, and f_meas supports that - in W the track's terminal hit at channel ~11995 sits directly on a grey dead-channel line, while U and V show it running clean off the panel. The three stop azimuths show a straight pencil track to the pin star with no arm, no fan and no dot. The chain agrees on the reject (no_bragg, shape_flat) and reports nothing at the stop. Both unassigned rows are small specks back along the body - 342014 is 5 points 20 cm out at chord cos +0.97 and 4.9 cm off the line, 343015 is 6 points 38 cm out at chord cos +0.96 - so delta / other, and no gamma tag since a through-goer has no stop.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 1). Bragg climbs on the reference curve to 1.14e5 at s=1-3; nothing past the stop, so STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL.
evidence: 311.4 cm of chain entering 0.9 cm from the +y face and stopping 55.0 cm from the nearest wall, comfortably contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: on the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 4-6e4 plateau from s=100 in to about s=20, then climb steadily - 6.4-6.7e4 at s=15, 7.7-8.4e4 at s=13, 6.8e4 at s=7, 7.9-9.2e4 at s=5, and 9.2e4, 1.02e5, 1.09e5, 1.13e5 and 1.14e5 clustered at s=1-3 - sitting right on the drawn muon reference curve through the whole climb and topping out at 1.14e5, exactly the 1.2-1.35e5 band the rubric says real stoppers reach. The rise is ragged in places (two points back at 3.5-4.0e4 around s=10) but it is unmistakably a rise, and the single 3.3e4 point at the fit's very last position is one partial-charge point, the ordinary end-of-track scatter the rubric tells me to leave alone rather than a sustained collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. Past the stop there is nothing at all: the three stop azimuths show the track terminating cleanly at the pin star with no arm, no dot, no fan and no second particle in any direction, and the flow summary agrees (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring). I also checked for the undershoot - there is no short forward high-charge piece, no row here has positive cos_fwd or a small dstop. All three non-muon rows sit far back along the body: 106011 is 13 points 46-53 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 and 3.4 cm off the chord line, 378022 a 2-point speck 40 cm back and 4.1 cm off the line, and 106008 is 21 points at only 3.2e3 e/cm some 259-267 cm back, up near the entry. All body activity, so delta / other, and with no michel and no gamma the kind is none. One caveat noted but not decisive: in V the stop neighbourhood sits beside the hatched dead-channel band at 7290-7345, so some terminal charge could be missing - it does not change a peak that already reaches 1.14e5.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 1). Undershoot checked and rejected on charge: the forward arm is at MIP, not several times MIP, and the muon's own peak already reaches 1.19e5 at the fit's last point.
evidence: A short stopper: 40.0 cm of chain entering right on the x face (d_face 0.0) and ending 34.0 cm from it. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the chain points hold a 5-6e4 plateau from s=40 in to s=15 and then climb along the drawn muon reference curve - 7.9-8.5e4 at s=8-10, 6.6-7.3e4 at s=6, 8.5-8.6e4 at s=4, 8.7-9.1e4 at s=2-3, 1.10e5 at s=1 and 1.19e5 at the fit's own last point. The peak is reached AT the fit end, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach, so the muon's tip is fully accounted for inside the fit and the pin does not move. I explicitly checked the undershoot, because the shape here is the one that manufactures false Michels - a short forward piece the chain types pdg 11 - and it fails on the load-bearing clause: 116008 carries 5.77e4 mean over 13 points, essentially the muon's own MIP plateau, with its points spread 2.05e4 to 8.7e4, nowhere near the 0.9-1.2e5 (four to six times MIP) that would mark it as the muon's last centimetres. So it is the ordinary case: a 7.4 cm arm attached at the shared stop vertex, leaving at a 44 degree kink (cos_fwd +0.69, 2.3 cm off the body line at 3.2 cm out) at MIP where the muon has just been at more than twice MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP - and 7.4 cm at 20.9 MeV is a sensible Michel. The three stop azimuths show it plainly as a distinct blue low-charge arm branching off the amber muon tip. 447009 is a 2-point 0.2 cm dot 22.0 cm out, 21.7 cm clear of the muon body line and 57 degrees from the Michel arm's direction against 133 degrees for the body - isolated, past the stop, on the decay's side of the ring, so gamma; charge is not a criterion here and I did not use its 5.1e4. C448 is a separate 11-point cluster 58.9 cm out, 54.8 cm off the body line and 129 degrees round from the Michel arm - the opposite side of the ring, an unrelated object with no PR segment, so delta / other. With one michel and one gamma the kind is both.

notes: Fit end 3.5 cm from the x face with a flat-to-falling profile - a genuine wall exit, the least ambiguous kind of THRU.
evidence: 132.3 cm of chain in the far -x/-y corner of the detector: it enters 0.6 cm from the z face and the fit end is 3.5 cm from the x face, so it leaves through the wall it is pointed at. The projections confirm it - in the top and end views the pin star sits right on the dashed detector boundary. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points sit on a 4.5-6.5e4 plateau across the whole displayed range with the usual delta spikes to 1.0-1.3e5, and coming into the end they are 6.3e4 and 8.3e4 at s=15, 6.6e4 at s=12, 8.1-8.4e4 at s=8, 5.8-6.6e4 at s=5-7, 3.0-4.6e4 at s=3-4 and 1.0-2.15e4 over the last two centimetres. That is flat to falling, never a rise off the plateau along the muon reference curve; the terminal drop to a fifth of plateau in the last 2 cm is the track running out of active volume, not a Bragg peak, and a Bragg peak would have to be at 1.2e5 there, not 1e4. f_meas shows the same thing directly: in all three planes the measured hits run in an unbroken diagonal straight off the top of the panel with no terminal blob and no dead-channel band under the end (the hatched bands in U at 20-30 and 90-100 and in V at 3810-3830 are far from the track). The three stop azimuths show a single smooth pencil track with nothing at the pin - no arm, no dot, no fan. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) and reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0. There is only one drawn object, the muon chain itself, so no attribution question arises.

notes: Wall exit at 11.8 cm plus a flat profile with a 2 cm terminal die-off; the terminal hits also sit on a dead-channel band in U.
evidence: 101.5 cm of chain low in the -x/-y corner: it enters 0.5 cm from the z face and the fit end is 11.8 cm from the x face, and in the end and top projections the pin star sits essentially on the dashed boundary, so a wall exit is right there. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 5-6.5e4 plateau over the whole displayed range with delta spikes to 1.0-1.4e5 scattered along it, and coming into the end they read 7.5-8.3e4 at s=15, 6.1-6.5e4 at s=12-14, 5.6e4 at s=10, 5.7-6.5e4 at s=8, 5.4-6.3e4 at s=5-7, 5.3-5.5e4 at s=3-4 and then 3.6e4, 2.5e4, 1.3e4 and 0.4e4 over the last two centimetres. Flat all the way in and then a two-centimetre die-off - no climb along the muon reference curve, which at 5 cm of residual range would already be near 9e4 and is nowhere approached. The chain's own reject list is shape_flat plus profile_sparse and it reports nothing at the stop. f_meas is consistent with an exit rather than a stop: the measured hits run in an unbroken line off the top of all three panels, the terminal hit in U sits right against the hatched dead-channel band at channels 700-712, and there is no terminal charge blob in any plane. The three stop azimuths show a straight pencil track ending at the pin with no arm, no dot and no widening. The single unassigned row 166008 is a 2-point speck with no measured dQ/dx 49.9 cm away and 46 cm off the muon line - an unrelated object, and in any case a through-goer has no stop against which gamma or michel could be defined, so it is delta / other.

notes: Flat profile at the fit end with no face and no visible continuation; I suspect this 33 cm stub is a piece of a longer track but no parent object is drawn, so THRU rather than FRAG_THRU.
evidence: A short object: only 33.0 cm of chain in 56 points, entering 12.9 cm from the z face and ending 41.4 cm from it, so both ends are interior. On the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the non-zero chain points hold a 6.5-8e4 band across the whole 33 cm with spikes to 9-1.1e5 around s=13-22 and dips to 2.2e4 and 0.75e4 at s=3-4; at the fit end itself the points are 6.8e4, 6.5e4 and 5.5e4, i.e. sitting on the same band the rest of the track sits on. There is no climb off that plateau over the last 10-20 cm and nothing approaching the muon reference curve, which would be near 9e4 at 5 cm and 1.6e5 at the stop, so by the operative test this is a through-goer even though the fit end is 41 cm from the nearest face - the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. The three stop azimuths show a uniform pencil stub running to the pin with nothing at either end - no arm, no dot, no fan and no widening - and f_meas shows a clean unbroken diagonal in all three planes with no terminal blob; the hatched dead-channel bands in U at 2480-2550 and V at 6390-6440 are beside the track but not under either end. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). What keeps this at medium: 33 cm of flat MIP-level track with both ends interior looks like a piece of something longer rather than a whole object, but no larger parent is drawn in any frame - only 27 thinned context points, none of them forming a continuation - so I cannot call it a fragment on the evidence in front of me and I have used the plain THRU. There is only one drawn object, the muon chain itself.

notes: Flat-to-falling profile on a badly imaged 97 cm chain with a near-empty stretch at s=60-75; no face, no continuation, THRU on the profile.
evidence: 96.7 cm of chain entering 1.0 cm from the z face and ending 51.8 cm from it. This is a poorly imaged object - the chain mean is only 3.4e4 and on the 4x-upscaled g_dqdx the points scatter between 2e4 and 5e4 for most of their length with a long nearly charge-free stretch at s=60-75 where they drop to 0.3-2e4, which is why the chain also flags profile quality. Coming into the fit end the non-zero points read 7.3-7.9e4 at s=13-18, 5.2-5.8e4 at s=10-12, 4.4-5.2e4 at s=2-8 and then 3.7e4, 2.3e4 and 0.75e4 over the last centimetre and a half: no climb off the band, and the muon reference curve would demand roughly 9e4 at 5 cm and 1.6e5 at the stop. So there is no Bragg rise at the fit end and the item is a through-goer whose cluster ran out of imaged charge - there is no face within 50 cm and no visible continuation, and the rubric says to say so rather than reach for UNCLEAR. f_meas shows only a short orange stub of the track inside the stop window with no terminal blob and no dead-channel band under it. Everything else drawn here is a ring of 2-point specks: 252003 (32.4 cm out, 26 cm off the muon line), 251002 (32.5 cm, 32 cm off), 250001 (39 cm, 37 cm off), 257006 (40 cm, 34 cm off), 253004 (53 cm, 53 cm off), 255005 and 258007 (57 cm, 20-35 cm off), pointing in unrelated directions all round the 60 cm ring. The chain calls 252003 a capture gamma at 0.52 MeV, but a through-goer has no stop against which a gamma can be defined, so by the rubric's THRU rule every non-chain row here is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Verdict is high-confidence: contained stop, unambiguous Bragg rise, attached MIP arm. The uncertain part is only the far-speck attribution (119008 at 51 cm, 121010 at 54 cm): kind is 'both' regardless because 120009 at 15 cm is already a detached dot. No undershoot - the forward attached piece is at MIP (5.07e4 against a 5.4e4 plateau), not the several-times-MIP tip the undershoot signature requires. No overshoot - no sustained collapse before the fit end.
evidence: 205.8 cm chain, enters 14.9 cm from the z face and stops 114.0 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained, so containment is not in question. On the 4x-upscaled dQ/dx panel the chain sits on a 5.4e4 plateau all the way in and then climbs off it over the last ~15 cm: 6.8e4 near s=10, 7.6-8.4e4 at s=5-8, 9.4e4 at s=4, 1.04e5, 1.10e5 and 1.15e5 in the last two cm, following the shape of the solid muon curve (which asymptotes to 1.6e5 and is never crossed, as expected). The peak is at the fit's own last point with no collapse before it, so the pin stays. Attached at the stop is a 7.9 cm 14-point segment 35005 at 5.07e4 e/cm (d_min 0.0, cos_fwd 0.37) continued by a 2.6 cm piece 35007 out to 8.96 cm at 4.46e4 - an arm leaving the Bragg peak at MIP and falling, which a muon at its own peak cannot do, and 9 cm is the right range for a ~25 MeV electron; the three azimuths show it as a distinct blue arm breaking off the amber muon band at a large angle, well clear of the body line. A 0.4 cm 2-point speck 120009 at 15.1 cm sits along the continuation of that arm direction (12 deg from it) but across a clean ~6 cm charge-free gap, so by the attachment tie-break it is a detached dot, gamma, not part of the electron. Two faint far specks, 119008 at 51 cm (2.4e4 e/cm, 12 deg off the arm axis) and 121010 at 54 cm (4.8e4, 27 deg off), are on the Michel's side of the stop and read as gammas; 125012 at 52.8 cm has cos_fwd -0.96, i.e. sits on the muon body line, and 122011 at 13.7 cm is backward at 81 deg from the arm in an unrelated direction and body-excluded by the chain, so both are delta / other. f_meas shows no dead-channel band at the stop in U, V or W, and the measured-predicted panels leave no residual charge past the end.

notes: Medium, not high, for two reasons. (1) The highest charge on the chain is not at the stop but in a 5 cm blob 20-26 cm before it, peaking at 1.26e5 against 9.8e4 at the end; I read that as a local delta or nuclear interaction rather than the true Bragg peak, because the charge recovers to a 5.5-6.6e4 MIP band after it instead of collapsing to the 0.15-0.5-of-MIP level the overshoot signature requires, and because an electron does not then climb again at its own far end. The pin is therefore left alone, but this is the item in my chunk where an overshoot pin is most arguable. (2) MESSY is a live competing reading - 19 of 27 drawn objects are shower-typed and MCS gives 84.8 MeV against 172.4 by range with ambiguity 0.84 - and I ruled it out only on the spine visible in d_3d_stop/e_3d_stop. No undershoot: no forward high-charge tip past the fit end (the only forward speck is 44 cm out with no measured charge).
evidence: A short, heavily fragmented object: 63 cm of chain broken into 8 muon segments with 19 further pieces the chain types 'pdg 11, shower', all of them at cos_fwd -0.96 to -1.0 and 20-53 cm from the stop, i.e. lying on the muon body line. It enters 1.5 cm from the z face and the fit ends 22.0 cm from the nearest face, so the end is inside the volume but not deeply. b_3d_wide is a formless clump, but d_3d_stop and e_3d_stop resolve a genuine continuous spine from the stop star running the full 50 cm chord with the shower pieces bundled around its back half and sprayed at the entry end - so there is a coherent spine and this is not MESSY. The dQ/dx profile is bimodal and ugly: from the entry end the segment averages sit at 8e3-1.6e4 out beyond 40 cm, 3.2e4 at 35-40, 4.7e4 at 26-35, then a 5 cm blob at 20-26 cm whose points run up to 1.26e5 (segment 41044, mean 8.2e4), then back down to a 5.5-6.6e4 band over 5-20 cm, and finally a climb over the last ~5 cm through 8.0-8.4e4 to 9.4, 9.7 and 9.8e4 in the last two centimetres, tracking the shape of the solid muon curve without crossing it. That final climb off the local band is a ragged but real Bragg rise, so the verdict is not THRU. notes: Medium, and this is the weakest call in my chunk - stated so a re-scan disagreement is expected rather than surprising. THRU rests on the rubric's operative test: no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the last 11 cm sitting at MIP when a stopper's last 11 cm must be roughly twice that. The competing reading is a pattern I only saw after scanning several items: across my chunk, MCS-versus-range separates my own verdicts 9 for 9 - the six items where MCS agrees with range (12/35, 13/39, 13/73, 13/103, 15/45, 15/77) I called stopping, and the three where MCS exceeds range by 1.3x to 6x (12/88, 14/47, 15/30) I called THRU. 14/84 is the single item that breaks that split: MCS 330.9 MeV at ambiguity 0.27 against 344.1 by range and 299.6 by dQ/dx, all agreeing, and the chain itself accepts the item (is_stm 1). I still went THRU for two reasons. First, the charge contradiction is direct and large, while MCS-range agreement is coincidence-prone at this length: a 143.5 cm segment has a range-equivalent momentum of about 437 MeV/c, and an ordinary through-going cosmic in that momentum band would reproduce the agreement without stopping - the test only bites when the track is long enough for the two to separate, which is why it is convincing on 14/47 (817 by range against 1737 by MCS over 312 cm) and not here. Second, f_meas rules out a dead region at the end, so there is no mechanism to hide a Bragg peak. If a re-scan calls this STM_ONLY, the MCS split is the reason. No undershoot: nothing is drawn forward of the fit end.
