The four unassigned pieces 34007, 34010, 34013 and 34016 that the chain types pdg 11 shower all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 at 17.8, 26.0, 37.2 and 157.2 cm along the body - they are the orange points on the negative axis at magnitudes 18 to 38 - so they hug the muon line and are delta / other by the on-the-body rule, which on a THRU is where everything non-chain goes anyway.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence - the Bragg climb over 20 cm is unambiguous. The medium is entirely for michel_kind: it rests on calling the two forward survey specks gamma rather than delta / other, which is what moves the kind from none to detached dots. I went gamma because they are detached, compact, inside 60 cm, off the body line and on one side of the stop rather than scattered, which is the rubric's stated test; the competing reading is that two 3-4 point survey specks that neither stage was offered are just unrelated activity in a busy region that also contains a 120 cm crossing track. Note 173008 is the same object id that appears in item 039253_6/31, seen from a different stop. No overshoot and no undershoot signature.
evidence: 83.9 cm chain in four fitted segments, entering at (-195.4, -4.6, 1.9) just 1.1 cm from the z face and ending at (-256.1, 25.4, 27.4), 26.6 cm from the nearest z wall, so the far end is inside the volume. The Bragg is the cleanest thing in this item: reading in from the plateau the points go 5.5-6.5e4 beyond s=25, 6.9-7.1e4 at s=14-16, 7.1-7.8e4 at s=12-14, 9.3-9.5e4 at s=8-12, 8.6-9.2e4 at s=6-8, 1.03-1.09e5 at s=3-6, 1.25e5 at s=1.5, 1.45e5 at s=0.7 and 1.19e5 at the last point - a monotone climb over the last 20 cm hugging the shape of the black muon curve, and segment 41001's own mean of 88180 against 60030 for the segment behind it says the same thing in one number. The final point being 18 per cent under the peak just before it is ordinary end scatter, well inside the rubric's leave-the-pin-alone band, and there is no sustained collapse, so the pin stays. Nothing is attached at the stop: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the nearest drawn object is 175019 at 18.6 cm with cos_fwd -0.95, a 15-point 8.2 cm piece lying back along the muon body that the chain itself body-excluded - delta / other on the on-the-body rule, and past the 10 cm radius where direction stops discriminating. Two survey-only specks sit past the stop on its forward side: 174009 (3 points, 1.2 cm, 18743 e/cm) at 36.5 cm with cos_fwd 0.57, and 173008 (4 points, 0.0 cm, 24104 e/cm) at 40.0 cm with cos_fwd 0.89. On the e azimuth they are the two isolated brown squares beyond the star, and scaling off the 18.6 cm orange segment (5.6 px/cm) puts the nearer one about 37 cm out - they are detached across a charge-free gap, compact, well clear of the body line and inside 60 cm, and they lie on the same side of the stop rather than scattered around the ring, so both are gamma and the kind is detached dots. Charge is not a criterion for that call. C42 is a 574-point 120 cm cluster with no PR segment crossing the field diagonally in every 3-D frame - a different object entirely - and 41007 is a 3.3 cm 5184 e/cm shower speck 59 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99; both are delta / other. f_meas: V is unusable at the stop, the track sitting inside the wide dead band at 4760-4820, but U and W both show measured matching predicted and the charge ending at the pin, with the two specks appearing as separate markers at time slices 2113 and 2177 against the track's 2250-2400.

notes: Cleanest THRU in the chunk: face to face, anode-parallel geometry, and a profile that collapses rather than rises. The MCS estimate is pegged at 4000 MeV with ambiguity 1.00, which is what a straight non-stopping track does to that fit. No overshoot and no undershoot signature.
evidence: 79.6 cm chain, one drawn object, and the geometry decides it before the charge does: it enters at (335.1, -230.9, 297.4), 1.0 cm from the z face, and the fit ends at (337.4, -178.5, 253.3), 2.6 cm from the anode face - a face at each end. x runs 335.1 to 337.4 over the whole 80 cm, so the track lies essentially parallel to and 2-3 cm off the anode, which is exactly why the 3-D frames show a broad diffuse smear of image points either side of the orange chain rather than a clean spine, and why f_meas has the track compressed into time slices 2450-2470 in all three planes (isochronous). The profile does the opposite of a Bragg: taking the upper envelope it runs 6.0-7.6e4 at s=17-25, 5.2e4 at s=15, 4.6e4 at s=8, and then over the last 8 cm the points collapse into a dense band at 0.3-0.8e4 from s=0 to s=7 with a few at 1.2-2.4e4 at s=7-12 - fading to nothing, with no peak anywhere before the collapse to make it the overshoot signature and the segment's own mean only 36167 to begin with. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any azimuth, the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma, and measured matches predicted with no dead band at the fit end in any plane (U's nearest are at 2490-2540, V's at 6390-6430, W's at 10800-10820). Charge fading to zero as the track runs into the anode 2.6 cm away is an exit, not a stop. Single chain segment, so muon, and the kind is none.

notes: Cleanest STM_MICHEL in the chunk. Pin left alone: no peak-then-collapse, the profile is still climbing at the last fit point. Explicitly checked the undershoot and it does not apply - the forward piece is at 0.58 MIP, not the four-to-six times MIP that would make it the muon's own tip.
evidence: 77.2 cm chain entering at (339.6, -233.4, 150.3) 0.3 cm from the anode face and ending at (307.2, -287.0, 189.7), 32.7 cm from the nearest face, so the stop is comfortably inside. The Bragg is textbook: a 5.2-5.5e4 plateau from s=80 in to s=15, then 6.0-6.6e4 at s=10-18, 7.3-7.8e4 at s=5-8, 8.0-8.4e4 at s=2-5, 1.06e5 at s=0.8, 1.12e5 at s=0.3 and a 1.285e5 point at s=1.5 - a smooth monotone climb over the last 15 cm that tracks the black muon curve's shape and tops out where the rubric says real stoppers do. Attached at that stop, at the shared vertex 79002, is 79001: 6 points over 3.0 cm carrying 31160 e/cm, which is 0.58 of this track's own MIP plateau, leaving at a 97 degree kink (cos_fwd -0.14). It is the ordinary Michel case and explicitly NOT the undershoot - the undershoot needs a 2 cm tip at several times MIP, and this piece is below MIP, so the tip is not the muon's own last centimetres. A muon sitting at its Bragg peak has no energy left to throw a 5.7 MeV delta, and at 97 degrees the piece is well clear of the body line and attached at the vertex, so both halves of the tie-break rule give michel. Its points are the blue circles on the negative axis at magnitudes 1 to 3 carrying 3.0-3.6e4, which is minus their 3-D distance from the origin and not a claim about which side they are on; the 3-D azimuths put the small blue blob right at the star, transverse to the spine. The only other object, 79004, is a 2-point 0.4 cm piece the chain types pdg 2212, sitting 74 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99 hard on the muon body at the far end of the track - delta / other. f_meas shows measured matching predicted in all three planes with the charge and the low-charge Michel points both ending at the pin near time slice 1220, and the dead bands in U at 2380-2450 and in V at 6180-6200 are nowhere near the stop. One michel piece and no gamma, so the kind is attached.

notes: Medium, not high, because the object is nearly isochronous and the per-segment means run from 2230 to 45650 e/cm - charge reconstruction is visibly unreliable over much of it, so the flat profile is weaker evidence here than it would be on a normal-angle track. Two things pull the other way and are worth recording: the chain rejected on shape_flat ALONE, not no_bragg, so its own Bragg metric keyed on that single last point; and range KE 967.9 MeV against MCS 802.6 MeV at ambiguity 0.08 are closer than one usually sees on a through-goer. I still read it THRU because the human test is a rise over the last 10-20 cm and there is none. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: A 418.6 cm chain in twelve fitted segments with ten more unassigned pieces hung along it, entering at (267.7, -295.0, 290.1) 8.3 cm from the z face and ending at (276.6, -0.8, 93.2), 63.3 cm from the anode face and 92.4 cm from the z face, so the fit end is deeply inside. Geometry first, because it colours everything else: the end view puts the whole object at x between 267 and 277 over its full 418 cm, i.e. essentially isochronous, and f_meas confirms it - the entire object occupies time slices 20 to 50 across U channels 2280-2490. On the 6x crop the last 20 cm are flat and low: 0.44-0.49e5 at s=0.6-3.9, 0.53e5 and 0.63e5 at s=2.7-3.5, 0.38-0.42e5 at s=4.5-5.1, 0.28-0.35e5 at s=6-8, 0.47-0.49e5 at s=9-10, with one zero-charge point at s=1.2 to ignore, against a muon reference curve that is at 1.3e5 by s=0.6 and 0.78e5 at s=6. The only elevated point in the whole terminal region is the single last one at 1.044e5, 2.3x the near-stop segment's own 40427 mean - one point, no climb behind it, the same fit-end charge-sweep artefact as in 039253_5/121 rather than a Bragg. Nothing is drawn past the fit end in any azimuth and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma. Every unassigned piece sits on the muon body: 217044 is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 33.7 cm out at cos_fwd -0.95 that the chain body-excluded, and 82001, 82013, 82017, 82020, 82023, 82027, 82029, 82035 and 82036 are all at cos_fwd -0.98 to -1.0 between 55 and 342 cm back - body activity, delta / other, which is also where a THRU sends everything non-chain. It is not MESSY: all three azimuths show one continuous coherent spine with the side activity as a halo around it, not an EM blob with no spine.

notes: OVERSHOOT: real stop is about 9.2 cm back up the fit from its last point, at the 0.83-1.02e5 group at s=9.4-13.4; pin-rr 9.2 recorded. Medium, not high, and here is the competing reading: the track is drift-dominated (dx -130 against dy 34, dz 42) so it crosses only about 15 U channels over its whole length, and U carries a thin dead band at channel 3040 which is exactly where the last stretch of the track sits, while V (6820, dead bands at 6770 and 6890) and W (11310, dead band at 11400) are clear. A dead U channel eating charge along the last stretch would depress the same nine centimetres without any Michel. What kept me on the overshoot is that charge loss cannot manufacture the RISE from 0.5e5 at s=20 to 1.02e5 at s=10 that precedes the collapse. Note also the two points at 0.78-0.81e5 at s=1.8-2.0, which sit inside the region I am calling Michel; I read them as a brem or shower point on the electron. Verdict and kind are robust to the pin question - leaving the pin alone gives STM_MICHEL / attached as well, with 80009 tagged muon instead - so only the pin and that one tag are at stake.
evidence: 152.1 cm chain in two fitted segments, entering at (339.9, 72.9, 56.5) right on the anode face (d_face 0.0) and ending at (209.6, 106.8, 98.3), 97.5 cm from the nearest z face - deeply contained. On the 7x crop the profile does something none of the through-goers in this chunk do: it climbs off its own plateau and then collapses well before the fit's last point. Reading in, s=20-100 sits at 0.45-0.55e5, s=18.4 is 0.578e5, s=17.2 is 0.60-0.70e5, s=16-17 is 0.70-0.75e5, s=13.7 is 0.79e5, then a coherent group of about eight points at 0.83-0.90e5 across s=9.4-13.4 topped by 1.021e5 at s=10.1 - a climb to twice plateau that is far steeper than the muon curve's own slope over that span (0.60e5 to 0.66e5). Immediately inside it the charge falls away and stays down for nine centimetres: 0.558e5 at s=9.1, 0.31e5 at s=8.2, 0.549e5 at s=8.0, 0.466e5 at s=6.8, 0.53e5 at s=6.3, 0.545e5 at s=5.6, 0.57e5 at s=4.8, 0.47e5 at s=3.9, 0.372e5 at s=3.2, 0.418e5 at s=2.9, and 0.437e5 at s=1.3, with two points at 0.78-0.81e5 at s=1.8-2.0. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot then continue at MIP for nine centimetres, so I moved the pin to rr 9.2, the junction between the 0.83e5 point at s=9.4 and the 0.558e5 point at s=9.1. That makes the last 9.2 cm of fit plus the attached piece the Michel: about 11 cm of electron, which is the right range for a 25-35 MeV Michel and far more plausible than the 1.8 cm / 3.1 MeV object the chain offers. The tag alphabet cannot split a row, so segment 80009 (d 0 to 6.8 cm) lies wholly past the moved pin and is tagged michel, and 80006 (d 6.8 to 140.9 cm) is tagged muon for what most of it is - its first 2.4 cm, from 6.8 to 9.2, are Michel and the row is therefore split. 80001, the four oversized circles on the negative axis at magnitudes 0.4 to 1.9 carrying 0.41e5, 0.345e5, 0.256e5 and 0.204e5, is attached at the shared stop vertex 80002 at a 63 degree kink and is michel too - well below MIP and falling as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature and explicitly not the undershoot. One michel, no gamma, so kind attached. f_meas shows measured matching predicted, with the markers turning dark blue near the pin exactly as the collapse says they should.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test, corroborated by the 3.5 cm wall proximity. Containment ambiguity worth flagging: the rubric gives no d_face threshold for ends inside the volume, and this stop at 3.5 cm sits in that hole - but the verdict does not turn on it, since the profile is flat either way. Terminal 4 cm of near-zero points judged zero-charge fit points, not an overshoot collapse, because the same sprays recur mid-track and nothing lies past the fit end.
evidence: 84 cm of chain, entering 23.9 cm from the nearest y face and ending 3.5 cm from the top y wall (in_fv 0). The dQ/dx profile is flat: the bulk sits on a 4.3-5.0e4 plateau continuously from s=85 all the way in to the last measured point at s~0.5, which is itself at 4.8e4, i.e. plateau level. A handful of green/yellow points at 7.1-9.0e4 appear at s=5-25 and look at first like a ragged Bragg rise, but the identical excursion recurs at s=72-74 (7.6, 6.9, 6.8e4) far from the stop, so it is scatter in the upper envelope, not a terminal rise; the median never leaves the plateau and never approaches the muon reference curve, which climbs from 5.5e4 at s=30 to 1.6e5 at s=0. A cluster of near-zero points (0.6-2.2e4) occupies the last 4 cm, but the same near-zero sprays recur at s=34-36 and s=67-80, straddling the 92001/92002 junction at 68 cm, so they are fit points with no measured charge rather than the Michel-gap collapse - and there is nothing on the far side for the fit to have bridged to (n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted clusters). f_meas shows the charge terminating cleanly in all three planes with the only dead V band crossed 15 cm upstream, not at the end. The 3-D azimuths d and e show a single straight amber band with a shallow jog and no arm; the apparent downward spur at the stop in frame c is the near-end-on projection. The only other object is a 2-point 0.6 cm survey speck 48 cm away, unrelated: delta / other. Flat to the last point plus a stop 3.5 cm from the wall reads as an exiting muon.

notes: Undershoot explicitly considered and rejected: 28005 mean 1.35x this items plateau and a 51 deg kink. Medium rather than high because the arms peak points reach 2.5x MIP, which is higher than a typical electron start, and because the detached-dot call on 126014 is what sets kind=both rather than attached.
evidence: 197.8 cm over two chain segments, entering 0.9 cm from the z face and stopping 13.0 cm from the anode face, comfortably inside. The profile is a textbook rise: a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s=90 in to s=20, lifting to 7-8e4 by s=12, 8.4-9.5e4 at s=5-10, and peaking at 1.145e5 at s=3.5 with 9.9e4 at s=2 and 8.2e4 at s=1 - about 1.9x its own plateau and following the muon curve shape, so the Bragg rise is complete inside the fit. A single 5.2e4 point sits at s=0.3; that is one partial-charge point at the very end, not a sustained collapse, so the pin stays. I checked this hard against the undershoot case because 28005 is a short forward piece the chain calls the Michel with individual points at 1.49e5 and 1.135e5. It fails the undershoot test on the load-bearing clause: its mean is 80580 against this items own 5.5-6.5e4 plateau, i.e. 1.35x MIP, not the four-to-six times the rubric requires, and it leaves at a 51 deg kink (cos_fwd 0.66), not straight ahead. It is a 6-point 3.2 cm arm carrying 18.3 MeV that the display draws in all three azimuths as a distinct blue limb standing clear of the muon body from the stop vertex - that is the ordinary Michel case. 126014 is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 12.3-12.5 cm out at cos_fwd 0.58, essentially along the extension of the Michel arms direction; frames c and e both show ~9 cm of clean white between the end of the arm and it, and f_meas confirms it as an isolated brown dot separated from the track end in all three planes. A 0.2 cm two-point speck across a 9 cm gap is a detached dot, so gamma rather than a piece of the electron, which makes the kind both. No dead channels at the stop in any plane.

notes: THRU with no visible continuation, no face within 51 cm and no dead-region exit - the rubric case where a flat profile alone carries the verdict. Medium rather than high because the drift-parallel geometry gives factor-three point-to-point scatter, so the Bragg test is weaker here than on a normal-angle track; the call rests on there being no rise at all and on the terminal points being the lowest on the plot.
evidence: 247.3 cm over four chain segments, entering 0.4 cm from the anode face and ending 51.0 cm from the nearest wall, deep inside the volume. No object of any kind is drawn near the stop - the table has four rows and all four are muon chain segments - and frame d shows the amber band terminating cleanly at the pin star with nothing past it. The profile never rises: a very scattered 2.5-5.5e4 band runs the whole length, and the last centimetre and a half sits at 1.5-3.0e4, the lowest values on the plot, i.e. the profile falls rather than climbs into the fit end. The 5.5-7.35e4 points at s=4-6 looked briefly like a peak-then-collapse, but the same 7-7.7e4 excursions recur at s=25-30, 54, 62-66 and 81 far from the stop, they are only about 1.5x the local band, and there is nothing past the fit end for a bridge to reach, so this is scatter and the pin stays. The terminal segment 40001 averages 35237 against 43650 and 45278 upstream, confirming the fall numerically. f_meas explains the noise rather than the end: in all three planes the track is nearly vertical in the channel-time plane, spanning 145 time slices over about ten channels, so it runs almost parallel to the drift and its per-point dQ/dx is poorly defined; the charge simply stops at time slice 2475 with the dead U, V and W bands sitting beside the track channels rather than across the end, so this is not a dead-region exit either. Flat-to-falling with no Bragg rise makes it a through-goer whose cluster ended where the imaging ran out.

notes: The competing reading was THRU on a flat shape, and the tags and kind would be identical. I went MESSY because the plateau is five times below MIP with a six-fold range-versus-dQ/dx energy disagreement, which makes the shape test denominator-less rather than merely flat, and because the drawn scene is a shower cloud plus fragments rather than one track. Medium confidence: if the owner reads the low plateau as a calibration or attribution defect on a real through-going track, this becomes THRU with 53005, 53007 and 53017 as muon.
evidence: There is no credible stopping muon here, and no coherent ionisation track either. The object is a 37.8 cm patch lying almost flat against the anode plane, with the fits first point 5.1 cm and its last point 4.7 cm from that same face; f_meas shows the whole thing as a compact horizontal blob spanning only about thirty time slices in all three planes, so it sits at nearly fixed drift. Every point on the dQ/dx panel is below 3e4 and the body sits at 0.5-1.5e4, about a fifth of MIP, and the chains own two energy estimates disagree six-fold (range 116.9 MeV against dQ/dx 20.5 MeV) - the plateau_off_mip reject. No real minimum-ionising particle reads a fifth of MIP over 38 cm, so the charge here cannot support a Bragg test at all: there is no trustworthy plateau to measure a rise against. The topology matches that. Eight of the eleven rows are pdg 11 shower or michel fragments; 53003 (49 points, 29.0 cm) runs parallel to and overlapping the 53005 muon segment over almost the same 3-25 cm span, and five more shower specks are strung along 20-29 cm. Frames d and e show a broad, sparse stream of image points running alongside the amber tube and spreading ten to twenty centimetres transversely, which is shower-like rather than track-like, and the HEAD line confirms these are this clusters own points because the seven blobs from the other flash are hidden. The apparently coherent spine is the particle-flow tube drawn over the fit, not resolved ionisation underneath it. This is an EM blob broken into many pieces, so MESSY, and under the MESSY convention every row is tagged delta / other with kind none.

281 cm, enters 1.4 cm from the anode face, stops 105 cm from the y wall. Bragg to 1.15e5 on the muon curve. A 9.8 cm arm at 5.1e4 e/cm leaves the stop forward (cos_fwd 0.61) with profile charge to -11 cm, and a further 0.5 cm piece the chain also calls Michel sits 16 cm out on the same side. Two dots at 40 and 51 cm, perpendicular and forward, clear of the body: gamma. 59005 lies 45-50 cm back ON the body line at 0.1 MIP: delta / other.

275 cm, enters 1.1 cm from the z face, stops 70.9 cm from the anode face. Bragg to 1.07e5 on the muon curve, MCS amb 0.02. A short two-piece arm covers 0-4.1 cm past the stop (6.6e4 and 2.5e4 e/cm) with profile charge to -3 cm -- a low-energy Michel. Three dots at 22.5, 30.6 and 31.2 cm, clear of the body: gamma. Five further objects lie 38-220 cm back along the body line (cos_fwd -0.96 to -1.0), including a 59 cm pdg-4 piece: delta / other.

notes: Medium. The Bragg case rests on the upper envelope and on one terminal point at 2.8x the body median, against a genuinely noisy profile with near-zero fit points a few centimetres earlier; the containment (35 cm) and the clean empty stop in three azimuths are what tipped it away from THRU. Single-row item, so the tag and kind follow mechanically once the verdict is fixed.
evidence: 76.5 cm on a single chain segment in the top corner, entering 0.5 cm from the z face and ending 35.0 cm from the nearest wall. The object table has exactly one row: nothing at all is drawn near the stop, and frames b, c and e confirm it - the amber band terminates at the pin star with clean space beyond, the only other points in view being the pale thinned-context cloud from neighbouring clusters. The profile is scattered but its upper envelope climbs onto the muon curve: the bulk sits at 4.0-5.4e4 from s=75 in to s=40, the envelope reaches 8.0e4 at s=18, 8.85e4 and 9.1e4 at s=7-8, 7.85e4 at s=1, and the last point at s=0.3 is 1.265e5, about 2.8 times the body median and sitting essentially on the reference curve, which nothing else on the track does. f_meas shows a dark-red maximum-scale hit at one end of the track in W, which I read as the same terminal point; that is a consistency check rather than independent evidence, since identifying which f_meas end is the stop relies on the drift-to-time mapping. The competing reading was scatter, because a comparable 1.245e5 outlier sits at s=76 and because a handful of near-zero points (0.75-1.95e4) fall at s=3-5. But the s=76 outlier is the fits first point right at the z entry face, where a partial path length inflates dQ/dx, and the low points at s=3-5 are the usual charge-less fit points that the rubric says to ignore; they are a dip before the last point, not a sustained collapse after a peak, so there is no overshoot and the pin stays. Dead channels are clear of the stop in U and V; W has a band five to fifteen channels short of the end, which could thin the charge just before the stop but does not touch the terminal hit, and no charge continues past the end in any plane.

notes: High confidence on the verdict: attached 12.8 cm 42.7 MeV arm at MIP off a stop whose muon points are 1.5x plateau, with the chain agreeing (is_stm 1). The attached-versus-both call rests on 456015 and 457016; both are forward of the stop, clear of the body line and separated from the Michels end by a visible gap in f_meas, so I read them as detached dots rather than outlying pieces of the electron. Several dead V and W channels cross this track, which is likely why the muons terminal rise is only 1.5x.
evidence: 71.8 cm on one chain segment, entering 0.2 cm from the z face and stopping 13.9 cm from the nearest wall, inside the volume. The muon rises modestly but genuinely: a 5.0-6.5e4 plateau from s=70 in to s=20, 6.5-7.4e4 through s=2-15, and the last two chain points at 8.5e4 and 9.0e4, about 1.5 times its own plateau. That alone would be borderline, but the decay topology is unambiguous and the rubric makes it sufficient. 111010 and 111001 form a single 12.8 cm two-piece arm leaving the stop vertex at cos_fwd 0.86 - about 31 deg forward - carrying 42.7 MeV, and frames b, c and e all show it as a blue limb attached at the pin star and running clean away from the amber muon band, which continues in the opposite direction. Its charge is the load-bearing check against the undershoot: 41267 e/cm over the first 8.2 cm and 55153 over the next 4.6 cm, i.e. 0.75 to 1.0 of the muons own plateau, nowhere near the several-times-MIP a mis-fitted muon tip would show, and 12.8 cm is far too long for a muon tip in any case. A muon whose last point is at 9e4 cannot continue at MIP for thirteen centimetres, so this is a second particle - a textbook attached Michel. Of the three remaining rows, 455014 sits 16.3-18.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.91, on the muon body line and chain-excluded as Michel body, and f_meas puts its dots at time slice 773 on the muon side of the stop: delta / other. 456015 (5 points, 2.3 cm, 27.0-28.5 cm, cos_fwd 0.42) and 457016 (2 points, 0.1 cm, 43.8 cm, cos_fwd 0.94) are both in the forward hemisphere on the Michels side - 457016 lies almost exactly along the arms direction - and f_meas shows them as isolated dots at time slices 887 and 948, separated from the end of the Michel at 870 by clean gaps in all three planes. Detached compact dots past the stop, so gamma, which makes the kind both.

notes: Medium because the rise is sharper than a textbook Bragg ramp - the profile is still on plateau at s=4-16 and then jumps within a centimetre - and because delta spikes of similar height recur along this body. The deep containment (127 cm from any face) and the four-point consecutive climb are what decided it for STM_ONLY over THRU. 175016 tagged gamma on the plain gamma rule; if the owner requires a speck to be associated with a reconstructed decay to count, this becomes kind none.
evidence: 269.3 cm over four chain segments, entering 0.9 cm from the bottom y face and ending 127.2 cm from every face - the most deeply contained stop in my chunk, which matters because it rules out an exit. The body sits on a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to s=4, and then the last three centimetres carry the highest charges on the plot: 1.125e5 at s=2, 1.26e5, 1.35e5 and 1.41e5 at s=1-3, with the final point at 9.15e4, so the terminal group is 1.5 to 2.3 times the plateau and lands on the muon reference curve, which nothing else on this track does. Frame e shows that as a real red stretch of points immediately before the stop vertex, not a single hot pixel. I weighed it against the delta-ray reading, because comparable spikes recur at s=30 (1.25e5), s=63-66 (1.20-1.26e5) and s=92 (1.13e5) and are visible in frame e as orange patches partway down the body - but those are one to three isolated points on an otherwise flat local band, whereas the terminal group is four consecutive points climbing into the origin. The 9.15e4 last point and a single 2.9e4 stray at s=0.3 are a 35 per cent dip and one partial-charge point, which the rubric calls ordinary scatter, so the pin stays and there is no collapse - and nothing lies past the stop for a bridged fit to reach. f_meas shows the charge terminating cleanly at time slice 2170 in all three planes with every dead band well clear of the track channels. Nothing at the stop reads as an electron: the object table has only the four muon segments plus 175016, a two-point 0.3 cm survey speck 45.4 cm out at cos_fwd 0.33, past the stop and tens of centimetres off the muon body line, separated from the star by visible empty space in a_proj, b and f_meas - an isolated compact dot in the forward hemisphere, which the rubric calls an uncertain gamma rather than a delta, so the kind is detached dots.

notes: High confidence. Monotone four-fold rise over the last 30 cm onto the muon curve, a 129.5 cm containment margin, and a completely empty stop. The chain also accepts this one (is_stm 1). Sub-MIP plateau is a dead-U-plane artefact, not a physics feature, and does not affect the shape test.
evidence: 153.0 cm over five chain segments, entering 0.2 cm from the anode face and stopping 129.5 cm from every wall, so the stop cannot be an exit. This is the cleanest Bragg profile in my chunk and it is monotone rather than ragged: the body sits at 2-4e4 from s=100 back to s=50, lifts to about 4e4 at s=30-50, 5-6e4 at s=15-25, 6.1-6.4e4 at s=13-14, 7.5e4 at s=6, 9.25-9.3e4 at s=7-8, then 1.04e5 at s=0.5 and 1.35e5 at the last point at s=0.3. That is a factor of four climb over the last thirty centimetres, it follows the shape of the muon reference curve the whole way and lands on the curve at the origin, and it is the only structure of its kind on the plot - no comparable spike occurs anywhere along the body. The plateau sits below the reference asymptote, which f_meas explains: a wide dead U band covers this tracks channels over the full drift, so the charge is carried by V and W. There is no collapse and no partial-charge tail at the end, so the pin stays. Nothing is past the stop at all: frames b and d show the amber-yellow band terminating at the pin star with clean white space beyond, the flow reports zero stop arms, zero dots, no unfitted clusters and no capture gamma in the ring, and f_meas shows charge stopping at time slice 2410 with V and W both clear of dead bands there. The single non-chain row, 75008, is 34 cm back up the body at cos_fwd -1.00 - seven points at 2362 e/cm, under a tenth of MIP - visible in frames c and e as a faint green dotted spur off the segment junction 34-39 cm behind the stop, which puts it squarely on the muon body line: delta / other, and the kind is none.

notes: Terminal 3 cm dip after a 1.39e5 peak considered as the overshoot/bridged-gap signature and rejected because the dip stays at the track own plateau, not far below it; pin left alone.
evidence: 81 cm chain, enters 0.2 cm from the anode x-face and stops 30.6 cm from the nearest (z) wall, in_fv, so containment is a numbers call and it passes. Profile sits on a 4-5e4 MIP plateau from s=80 in to s=25, lifts to 6-8e4 over s=25-10 and reaches 1.07-1.11e5 at s=5-6 with a 1.39e5 point at s=3.5, following the shape of the muon reference curve; the rise is ragged but it is a rise, so the chain reject no_bragg / shape_flat is wrong here. The last ~3 cm dip back to 3.8-7.2e4 (five points), which I looked at hard as the overshoot signature and rejected: the dip lands at or above the track own MIP plateau rather than far below it, f_meas shows measured = predicted at the stop with the dead bands tens of channels away so there is no charge-poor gap for the fit to bridge, and the arm leaves the fit end at a 58 deg kink rather than collinear with those last points. Pin left on the fit last point. Past the stop the only object is 52002, a 4-point 1.8 cm arm attached at the stop vertex, cos_fwd 0.44, whose charge falls 9.7e4 -> 6.5e4 -> 5.9e4 -> 4.85e4 going out: ~1.4x MIP and falling, which is the ordinary Michel case and not the undershoot tip (that needs several times MIP), so michel. Hardest part was the terminal dip; the three azimuths show nothing else within the 60 cm ring.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation, no face and no dead region at the end - recorded per the rubric rule that a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own. The two survey specks are 40-48 cm out and would have been a gamma call had there been a stop.
evidence: 321 cm chain in four fitted segments, enters 1.3 cm from the anode x-face and the fit ends at (53.6, 210.6, 240.3), 58.2 cm from the nearest z wall, 50.6 cm from the cathode and 125.8 cm from the y wall, so it is nowhere near a face. The profile decides it anyway: dQ/dx sits on a 3-5e4 MIP band from s=100 all the way in and the last 10 cm are 4.4e4, 4.9e4, 4.7e4, 3.1e4, 3.6e4 with no lift at all, where the muon reference curve is climbing through 6e4 at s=20 and 1.6e5 at s=0. A stopping muon cannot run flat into its own endpoint, so this is a through-goer that simply ended where the imaging ran out. The three azimuths show a bare star at the fit end with no arm, no stub and no dot attached, and f_meas has measured matching predicted with the dead-channel bands 20-40 channels clear of the track in U, V and W, so it is not a dead-region exit either. The only other drawn objects are two 4-point 1.8 cm survey specks 40.1 and 48.1 cm from the end at cos_fwd -0.70 and -0.64, sitting together off to one side; on a THRU there is no stop for gamma or michel to be defined against, so both are delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: MESSY: EM-like blob broken into many pieces plus a fabricated 30 cm zero-charge fit bridge. The chain offers 215041 as a Michel bridged across 7 cm of empty space, but with no identified stop that offer cannot be checked.
evidence: This is not one track. f_meas settles it: in all three planes the measured charge is a scatter of two dozen disconnected blobs spread over roughly 150 time slices and 60 channels, with the fit line drawn as a thin grey thread through part of the cloud; there is no continuous ionisation trail anywhere in U, V or W, and measured minus predicted repeats the same scattered blobs. The object table matches that picture: 28 drawn objects, nine of them fitted muon segments whose dQ/dx runs 1607, 5777, 6675, 12859, 24796, 27575, 27601, 37563, 74598 e/cm over 2.6-36.5 cm pieces, four segments the chain itself types pdg 11 / shower, and fourteen 2-5 point specks scattered in every direction out to 56 cm, most of them labelled gamma or Michel body exclusion. The 3-D azimuths show a dozen and a half brown vertex squares strewn across the frame with a long bare orange fit line bridging about 30 cm of near-empty space between the pin and the jumble, and the dQ/dx panel shows that bridge for what it is: whole stretches of chain points at or near zero charge from s=25-55 and s=60-85. There is no MIP plateau and no Bragg rise to read; the chain own KE estimates disagree by a factor of three (range 220.9, dQ/dx 71.6, MCS 65.6 MeV, ambiguity 0.94). With no coherent spine there is no stop to define gamma or michel against, so every row is delta / other and the kind is none, per the MESSY convention.

notes: OVERSHOOT: peak 1.05e5 at s=11-16, collapse to 0.4 of plateau over the last 9 cm inside segment 58001; pin moved back to 9.65 cm. Competing reading is STM_ONLY / none if the faint bridged stretch is fit points on a sparse tail rather than a Michel.
evidence: 172.6 cm chain in four segments, enters 5.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends deep inside the volume, 64.2 cm from the nearest (x) face and 133 cm from the z wall, so containment is not in doubt. The profile is the overshoot case. It sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to s=20, then climbs along the shape of the muon curve to 8.2-8.5e4 at s=10-13 and 9.4e4, 9.9e4, 1.01e5 and 1.05e5 at s=11-16 - a clean factor-two Bragg rise - and then collapses: 7.4e4 at s=9, 6.1e4 at s=7, 2.7e4 at s=6, a run of near-zero fit points from s=1-5 that I ignore as unmeasured, and 1.85e4 and 2.15e4 at the last point. That is a sustained fall to about 0.4 of the track own MIP plateau over the final 9 cm, exactly where a muon at its Bragg peak should be highest, and it coincides with a whole fitted segment: 58001 is 19 points over 10.9 cm at a mean 18555 e/cm against 48831, 42323 and 44642 for the other three. The three azimuths show why - past the black end-of-cloud marker the amber fit band runs on alone for about 10 cm to the star with no point-cloud halo beside it, and the cropped U panels of f_meas show the measured charge stopping where that band starts, with measured matching predicted and the dead bands far away. So I moved the pin to the 58001 / 58003 junction at 9.65 cm and tagged 58001 michel per the overshoot rule; the true stop is at the peak. The only other object is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck 50 cm out, delta / other. What makes this medium rather than high: the bridged stretch is faint enough that it could equally be read as the fit running past the muon end into a sparse tail with no decay electron at all, which would make it STM_ONLY with kind none.

notes: Pin left alone: a 2 cm terminal drop to 0.4 of plateau after the peak looks like the overshoot, but U has dead bands at the fit end (V and W clean), so the collapse is not cleanly attributable. If it is real the pin belongs at the 19005 / 19009 junction, rr = 1.98 cm.
evidence: 48.8 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from the z face, curves through about 40 degrees and stops 27.3 cm from the nearest z wall with 82 cm of x and 273 cm of y to spare, so it is contained. The profile sits on a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s=48 in to s=20, lifts to 7.5-9.2e4 over s=8-18 and reaches 1.06-1.08e5 at s=4, following the shape of the muon curve - a genuine ragged Bragg rise, so the chain reject no_bragg / shape_flat is wrong. Past the stop sit three chain-typed pdg 11 shower pieces, 14-16 points each, 7.6-9.3 cm long, at 1.0-1.6e4 e/cm, with d_min 0.0, 1.58 and 1.71 cm and d_max out to 6.8 cm and cos_fwd -0.08, -0.49, -0.44; all three are attached at the stop and inside the 10 cm radius where the rubric says direction does not discriminate, and the three azimuths show them as a spray leaving the stop nearly transverse to the muon and well clear of its body line, so all three are michel. That is decay activity past a contained end, which settles STM_MICHEL on its own. The last 2.0 cm of chain (segment 19009, 4 points, 29059 e/cm) does drop to 0.35-0.55 of the plateau after the 1.07e5 peak at s=4, which is the shape of the overshoot, but I left the pin alone: the drop is only 2 cm rather than the sustained several-cm collapse the rubric asks for, and f_meas shows three dead-channel bands in U running straight through the track last few centimetres while V and W are clean, so a terminal charge deficit there has an innocent explanation.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation and no face or dead region at the end; recorded per the rubric rule that a flat profile to the last point suffices. The two 1.0-1.1e5 points near s=0 are matched by identical excursions all along the track, so they are scatter, not a Bragg rise.
evidence: 314 cm single-segment chain, enters 0.3 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends at (-78.6, 37.3, 64.6), 63.8 cm from the nearest z wall, 75.6 cm from the cathode and 261 cm from the x face, so it is nowhere near an exit. The dQ/dx is the whole argument: the track scatters in a 5-9e4 band with occasional 1.0-1.1e5 excursions along its entire length - there are such excursions at s=13, 27, 65 and 90 as well as the two at s=0 and s=3 - and the last 20 cm are 5.8e4, 5.9e4, 6.0e4, 5.5e4, 7.7e4 with no systematic climb above that band and nothing resembling the muon curve shape. The chain own mean is 56881 e/cm and the terminal points sit right on it. A stopping muon cannot run into its own endpoint at plateau charge, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out; the range and MCS momenta disagree by a factor of two (823 vs 1755 MeV/c) which is what an unterminated track does. The three azimuths show a bare star at the end with no arm, stub or dot, b_3d_wide puts the end in open space well inside the box, and f_meas has the dead bands 20-80 channels to the left of the track in U and V and clear in W, so it is not a dead-region exit either. Only one object is drawn, the chain itself, so it is muon and the kind is none.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test with no visible continuation and no face at the end. Considered and rejected an overshoot reading in which the 1.31e5 burst at s=13-21 is the true stop: the charge after it returns to the plateau instead of collapsing, and normal-charge points coexist with the burst at the same arc lengths.
evidence: Short 34 cm single-segment chain, enters 0.2 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 25.4 cm from the x face and 25.4 cm from the z wall, so containment is marginal but not decisive either way. The profile has no terminal rise: from s=34 in to s=25 it scatters 3.5-7.5e4, and the last 12 cm are 6.5e4, 5.7e4, 5.4e4, 5.2e4, 4.8e4, 4.6e4, 5.1e4 with two 2.0e4 partial-charge points at the very last point - flat on the same band the far end sits on, where the muon curve is asking for 1.6e5. The one feature is a burst of 9.7e4, 1.02e5, 1.04e5, 1.14e5 and 1.31e5 at s=13-21, but that is not a Bragg peak: normal 3.5-7.5e4 points sit at the same arc lengths alongside the high ones, so it is extra charge deposited locally, a delta ray or a crossing, not the whole profile lifting. A Bragg peak lifts every point near the end and this one does not, and the charge after the burst returns to exactly the plateau rather than collapsing below it, which also rules out the overshoot reading in which the burst would be the true stop. The three azimuths show a clean straight track ending in a bare star with nothing past it - no arm, no stub, no dot - and f_meas shows the charge ending at the same place in U, V and W with the dead bands 20-30 channels to the side. Only the chain is drawn, so it is muon and the kind is none.

notes: Sub-MIP everywhere (mean 13573 e/cm) and buried in a wire-degeneracy ghost fan, so the charge scale is untrustworthy; the call rests on the profile falling rather than rising into the end. Dead bands sit immediately beyond the stop end in U, V and W, so this may well be a dead-region exit rather than a plain imaging truncation.
evidence: 53 cm single-segment chain lying almost entirely at one drift time - in f_meas it runs horizontally across time slice 990-1000 in all three planes - entering 9.7 cm from the y face and ending 17.9 cm from the y wall. There is no Bragg rise anywhere: the whole object sits at 0.5-3.3e4 e/cm, a fifth to a half of MIP, and the last 12 cm actually decline, 2.0e4, 1.7e4, 1.2e4, 0.9e4, 0.7e4, 0.5e4 into the last point, with two dips to zero at s=20 and s=35. A stopping muon runs into its endpoint climbing, not falling, so this is not an STM. The reason the charge is so low is visible in the 3-D frames: the fit line is buried in a wide fan of ghost points 15-20 cm across, with the diagonal streaks of wire-degeneracy plainly drawn in the e azimuth, so the 699 image points are a smeared reconstruction of a track running nearly parallel to a plane and the per-point dQ/dx is diluted. That is also why I put this at medium rather than high - every charge number on this object is suspect - but the verdict does not turn on the absolute scale, only on there being no relative rise at the end, and there is none. f_meas additionally shows a dead-channel band immediately outside the stop end in all three planes (a wide hatched block at U 2415-2445 against the track end at 2450, and narrower bands just left of the V and W ends), so a dead-region exit is the natural reading of where it went. Only the chain is drawn, so muon and kind none.

notes: Fit-stops-short reading considered and rejected on 46025: cos_fwd 0.88 and a 2.3 cm forward tip, but the charge falls outward from 9.2e4 to 6.2e4 instead of rising, which the rubric names as the ordinary Michel case. NOT an undershoot item. The attached-vs-both call rests on both far specks lying on the decay side of the stop.
evidence: 87.7 cm chain, enters 0.2 cm from the anode x face and stops deep inside - 80.2 cm from the x face, 107 cm from z, 173 cm from y. The Bragg rise is the cleanest in my chunk: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=90 in to s=40, 6-7e4 through s=10-25, 7.3-8.5e4 over s=2-8 and 9.1-9.2e4 at the last point, tracking the shape of the muon curve the whole way, and the terminal segment 46026 averages 65548 e/cm against 45322 for the segment behind it. Past the stop there is a six-piece structure spanning 0-9 cm: the core 46025 (3.0 cm, cos_fwd 0.88, d 0-2.33 cm) and then 46021, 46016, 46018, 46017 and 46011 out to 9.03 cm at 2.7-4.2e4 e/cm, i.e. at or below the muon own MIP plateau. I checked the fit-stops-short reading hard, because 46025 is short, forward and high - its first points are 9.2e4, matching the muon own last centimetres, and the chain types it pdg 11 - but it fails the load-bearing clause: its charge falls monotonically outward, 9.2e4, 9.1e4, 8.9e4, 8.4e4, 7.6e4, 6.2e4 over 2.3 cm and then 3e4 in the pieces beyond, where a muon running into its own Bragg peak would rise. A falling short forward piece is the ordinary Michel, and the high first centimetre is the decay vertex where the muon last points and the electron first points share the same charge. So all six pieces are michel, 44 MeV worth. 46015 sits 22 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0 dead on the muon body line, so delta / other whatever the chain pdg 11 says. The two survey specks 39 and 44 cm out I made gamma: the decay spray is not one axis - the core points forward at cos_fwd 0.88 while the outermost piece 46011 is at -0.47, about 90 degrees apart - so I used the second clause of the speck rule, same side of the stop as the decay, rather than along the arm. Both specks are on that side (118023 has a dot product of 0.99 with the stop-to-46011 direction, 119024 about 0.71) and neither is scattered off in an unrelated direction round the ring. That is the call that makes this both rather than attached and it is why I put the item at medium.

notes: Flat-profile THRU, ends in open space with no continuation and no dead region. The chain also flags vertex_hadron; nothing in the pictures past the fit end supports any vertex there.
evidence: 309 cm chain in nine fitted segments, enters 0.1 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends at (78.2, -44.7, 74.3), 73.5 cm from the nearest z wall, 75.2 cm from the cathode and 262 cm from the x face - deep inside, so containment is not the question. The profile is flat: 4-6e4 from s=100 all the way in, and the last 15 cm read 6.0e4, 5.5e4, 5.3e4, 5.0e4, 4.8e4, 5.6e4 with a single 7.8e4 at the very last point, which is inside the same band the track shows everywhere and nothing like the muon curve climbing to 1.6e5. The terminal segment 47020 averages 47772 e/cm against 47919 and 50332 for the two behind it - the profile does not move at all. There are two big excursions at s=45-50 (1.03e5 and 1.28e5) but they sit mid-track among normal points, so they are delta rays on the body, not a Bragg peak. The three azimuths show a straight thin track running to a bare star with no arm, stub or dot past it, and f_meas has the charge ending at the same time slice in U, V and W with the dead bands 20-100 channels away, so it is not a dead-region exit. Every other drawn object sits at cos_fwd -1.0 on the muon body line - five shower-typed pieces 137-299 cm back and 47021 16 cm back - so on a THRU they are all delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Flat-profile THRU; the last two points are the lowest of the whole track, the opposite of a Bragg rise. Range and MCS momenta disagree by a factor 2.5 (627 vs 1555 MeV/c), consistent with an unterminated track.
evidence: 228.8 cm chain in three fitted segments, enters 5.3 cm from the z face and the fit ends at (-182.3, -201.6, 32.0), 31.2 cm from the nearest z wall, 135 cm from y and 158 cm from the x face. The profile never lifts: the track sits in a 5-7e4 band from s=100 in, and the last 10 cm read 7.6e4, 6.1e4, 5.9e4, 5.5e4, 5.6e4, 4.5e4, 4.3e4 - the lowest points on the whole profile are the last two - against a muon curve asking for 1.6e5 at the origin. The terminal segment 19001 averages 56565 e/cm against 59227 for the 218 cm segment behind it, so nothing changes at the end. There are several 1.3-1.5e5 excursions at s=18, 40-45, 60-65 and 90, all mid-track among normal points, i.e. delta rays on the body rather than any terminal feature. The three azimuths show the track running to a bare star with nothing past it, b_3d_wide puts the end in open space inside the box, and f_meas has the charge stopping at the same time slice in U, V and W with the nearest dead band 35 channels away in U and about 10 in V, neither of them across the track. The only non-chain object is 19003, a 13-point 7.4 cm shower-typed piece 9-10 cm back at cos_fwd -0.97, which is on the muon body line and in any case on a THRU there is no stop to define anything against, so it is delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Flat-to-falling profile into the fit end with no continuation, no face and no dead region; THRU on the rubric operative test.
evidence: 302 cm chain in seven fitted segments, enters 60.7 cm from the z face and the fit ends at (-272.4, -254.7, 211.2), 67.6 cm from the nearest x face, 81.7 cm from y and 87.3 cm from z, so it ends in open volume. The profile falls into the end rather than rising: the plateau over s=10-50 is 4-7e4, and the last centimetres read 5.7e4, 5.2e4, 4.6e4, 4.4e4, 4.0e4, 3.6e4, 3.0e4, 3.0e4, with the two lowest points of the near region sitting at the origin itself, where the muon reference curve is at 1.6e5. The terminal segment 24022 averages 48813 e/cm, in line with 35304 and 34836 for the long segments behind it, so nothing lifts at the end at all. The 1.0-1.2e5 points at s=35-50 sit among normal points mid-track and are delta rays on the body. The three azimuths show the track running out to a bare star with no arm, stub or dot past it; the two brown squares in the frames are 52-54 cm back on the body. f_meas has the charge ending at the same time slice in U, V and W with the nearest dead bands 30-50 channels to the side, so it is not a dead-region exit, and the large diffuse grey cloud visible in b_3d_wide is a separate shower well away from this track (3490 thinned context points), not a continuation. The only non-chain object is 24020, a 15-point 8.4 cm shower-typed piece 52 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0 on the muon body line, which is delta / other; on a THRU there is no stop, so the kind is none.

notes: No visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the fit end; called THRU on the flat/declining profile alone, per the rubric. The last 10 cm decline below the plateau rather than staying flat, which is the one thing that kept this off high confidence.
evidence: 26.9 cm chain, enters 1.3 cm from the +y face and the fit ends 23.7 cm from that same face (232.6 cm from the anode/x wall, 45 cm in z), so containment by the numbers is fine but the profile is not. At 4x the dQ/dx panel shows the chain sitting on the muon reference's own asymptote, about 5.5-6e4, from s=27 down to s=15 with a couple of points at 8-8.6e4 near the entry end, then falling steadily through 4.5e4 at s=13, 3-4e4 at s=3-8 and 1.1e4 at the last point. There is no rise off the plateau anywhere in the last 10-20 cm and nothing approaches the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches; the highest point on the whole track is 22-24 cm back from the fit end, which is the entry, not a Bragg peak. I weighed the overshoot reading (peak then collapse, move the pin) and rejected it: the collapse is there but there is no peak in front of it, the last putatively real muon charge is at or below the plateau, so this is a fit running out of imaged charge, not a bridge across a muon-to-Michel gap. Nothing sits past the fit end at all: the two unassigned rows 86002/86003 share dstop 21.7 cm at cos_fwd -0.54/-0.68 and the three 3-D azimuths put them well off the muon line as a separate short piece below the track, so they are a different object; 87004 is a 0.3 cm two-point survey speck 55 cm out. No dead channel touches the fit end in U, V or W: the nearest hatched band in U starts just past the track's upper end and the W bands are clear of it, so it is not a dead-region exit either. Flat-to-below-plateau with no rise is the operative THRU test, and the chain's own no_bragg/shape_flat agrees.

notes: Segment 44005 (285 points, dqdx 3117 e/cm) is an essentially uncharged fit extension, tagged muon because it is a chain segment. No undershoot candidate: there is no object past the fit end to mistake for a Michel.
evidence: 403.8 cm chain in four segments, entering 5.1 cm from a z face and ending 38.4 cm from the nearest z wall (93.3 cm from the anode, 208.9 cm in y), so the stop is deep. The dQ/dx panel at 4x is the textbook case: the profile sits on the muon reference's asymptote at 5.4-6e4 from s=60 back to s=20, lifts to 6.5-8.2e4 by s=10-18, 8.5-9.8e4 at s=3-8, and the last four real points climb 1.22, 1.26, 1.38 and 1.52e5 within 2 cm of the fit end, tracking the shape of the solid muon curve the whole way. Two low outliers at s=4 (2.6e4, 4.85e4) and the string of near-zero points at s=60-64 are the uncharged fit points of segment 44005, whose mean dqdx is 3117 e/cm, and I ignored them per the rubric. The fit's very last point is 1.09e5, about 28 percent below the 1.52e5 peak one point earlier: that is a single partial-charge point at the end, not a sustained multi-centimetre collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. Past the stop there is no object at all: the table lists only the four muon chain rows, all at cos_fwd -0.86 to -1.00 and 57-212 cm back along the body. The three azimuths show a fan of pale image points spreading a few centimetres beyond the star, which is what made me look twice, but the W measured panel shows the drawn points ending cleanly at the track tip with nothing beyond, and the chain reports no stop arms, no dots and no unfitted clusters, so I read that fan as the terminal Bragg blob and diffusion, not decay charge. The U tip does abut a wide dead band and the V and W tips each sit on a thin dead channel, but a track leaving through a dead region cannot produce a peak at three times its own plateau, so that does not compete.

notes: No continuation and no face at the fit end (21 cm from the z wall); called THRU on the flat MIP profile alone, per the rubric. No undershoot candidate - nothing forward of the fit end at any charge.
evidence: 186.3 cm chain in three segments, entering 0.7 cm from the anode face in x and ending 21.0 cm from the nearest z wall, so the fit end is short of a face but not far from one. The 4x dQ/dx panel shows a MIP band the whole way: from s=100 in to s=5 the chain points scatter between 4.0e4 and 5.5e4, straddling the muon reference's 5.4e4 asymptote and sitting mostly under the electron dashed line, with no organised lift anywhere in the last 10-20 cm. The only high charge on the plot is a knot of six points at 1.0-1.43e5 sitting 60-67 cm back from the fit end, which is a mid-track delta or a segment overlap, not the stop. The last three centimetres go the wrong way entirely, dropping through 3.1e4, 2.2e4, 1.6e4 to 1.25e4 before a single 4.3e4 point at the fit end; that is a terminal dip with no peak in front of it, so it is not the peak-then-collapse signature and I left the pin alone. Nothing sits past the fit end: the only non-chain row, 102018, is a 0.4 cm two-point survey speck 40.4 cm away at cos_fwd -1.00, i.e. lying on the muon body line well back, so it is body activity. The measured panels show the track as one clean stripe in all three planes with a couple of brown points at the far entry end and no charge continuing past the star, and no dead band touches the fit end. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot run at MIP to its last point, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out; the chain's own no_bragg and shape_flat rejections agree.

notes: Bragg evidence is a shallow but 15 cm wide lift (1.3-1.4x plateau from s=2 to s=18) topped by a terminal point at 2.8x. evidence: 45 cm single-segment chain that enters 0.2 cm from the anode face in x and ends 42.9 cm back from it, 78 cm from the nearest z wall and 118.9 cm in y, so the fit end is comfortably inside. The fit's last point then sits at 1.405e5, about three times the far-end plateau and on the shoulder of the solid muon curve, which is well outside the factor-of-two scatter the rubric allows, so I read it as the Bragg peak rather than a hot point. The width of the rise is what carries this call, and it is worth stating explicitly because I used the same criterion to reject two other items in this chunk: a real stopper should be elevated over its whole last ten to twenty centimetres, not only at its final point. This item satisfies that weakly (1.3-1.4x from s=2 to s=18) where 039349_15/17 fails it outright (dead flat at plateau from s=3 to s=45 with only the last 1.1 cm hot) and 039349_13/60 satisfies it strongly (1.6-1.9x at s=3-6). Nothing at all is drawn past the stop: the object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and the three azimuths show only the faint image cloud hugging the body with no arm, dot or speck beyond the star. notes: Downgraded to medium: the last 13 cm of profile, which is the stretch the flat-to-the-end THRU test rests on, is partly suppressed by a dead W band at channel 11550 and a nearby V dead line. evidence: 172.6 cm chain in three segments, entering 0.3 cm from the +y face and ending 59.8 cm from the nearest z wall, 87.5 cm in y and 202 cm from the anode, so containment is not the issue. The last four points are 5.6e4, 4.6e4, 3.8e4 and 4.2e4, at or below the track's own plateau, so there is no rise off the plateau and nothing following the muon curve's shape; the highest charge on the plot sits 60-80 cm back. On peak location: the profile's maximum is nowhere near the fit end, so neither the overshoot (peak several cm early then a sustained collapse) nor the undershoot (peak sitting at or just past the last point) applies. I did test the s=6 pair as an overshoot candidate, since 8.8e4 is 1.8 times plateau, and it fails: what follows it runs at MIP rather than the 0.15-0.5 of MIP a bridged gap segment carries, and the charge before it is no higher than the charge after. The 15 cm past the vertex square is drawn as a thin teal segment rather than fat beads, which is 54009 and 54010, but the chain types both muon and their charge is ordinary MIP, so it is not a second particle leaving a stop. Nothing else is drawn: only the three muon chain rows, all cos_fwd -1.00, and no arm, dot or speck past the star in any azimuth. What keeps this off high confidence is the dead-channel picture: in the measured panels the track darkens at exactly the hatched W band near channel 11550, with the V dead line at 7000 also close, so the very stretch of profile I used for the flat-to-the-end test is partly suppressed by dead channels. A dead region can hide a rise as well as flatten one, and I cannot exclude that here; against that, a dead region suppresses charge rather than manufacturing a plateau, and there is no hint of a climb in the 20 cm before it either, which is why the call stays THRU.

notes: THRU on a fit end 118.7 cm from every face, purely on the flat profile, exactly the case the rubric anticipates. evidence: 325.7 cm chain in four segments, entering 13.3 cm from a z face and ending 118.7 cm from the nearest wall in z, 121.8 in y and 228 from the anode, so by the numbers this is as deeply contained a fit end as anything in the set. notes: Hardest item so far and the one place the undershoot geometry appeared: 56018 is forward (cos_fwd +0.95), attached (d_min 0.0), 3.6 cm and typed pdg 11, but at 1.45x plateau its charge sits between the undershoot band (0.9-1.2e5) and the at-or-below-MIP Michel case, so I invoked neither and read it as the muon continuing into the anode face 3 cm beyond. evidence: Short 26.1 cm two-segment chain in a corner of the volume: it enters 5.2 cm from a z face and the fit ends 6.7 cm from the anode face in x and 13.1 cm from a z wall, travelling toward the anode the whole way. It fails the load-bearing charge clause in both directions - 78525 e/cm is 1.45 times this track's own plateau, below the 0.9-1.2e5 the undershoot requires and above the at-or-below-MIP that marks a real Michel - and the tight azimuth crops show it as a short pale trail from the star to a second vertex square, collinear with the muon, not an off-axis arm. notes: Overrides the chain: its michel-group row 139001 is a 2-point 0.3 cm dot across a 12.2 cm charge-free gap, which the rubric classes as a detached dot (gamma), not an attached Michel. Peak-location check: peak at the fit end, single low last point only, so no overshoot and no undershoot.
evidence: 91.8 cm single-segment chain entering 0.2 cm from the anode face in x and ending 85.0 cm from that face, 142 cm from the z wall and 234 cm in y, so this stop is deep. The hot pair at s=25-26 (1.16 and 1.08e5) with 9.6e4 at s=19 is an isolated mid-track delta, well away from the stop. The fit's very last point is 7.0e4, roughly a third below the 1.09e5 half a centimetre earlier, but it is one point rather than a sustained multi-centimetre collapse, so the pin stays put; peak location is at the fit end, so neither failure mode applies. Past the stop the chain offers 139001 as the Michel, and I disagree: it is two points, 0.3 cm long, 1.3 MeV, sitting 12.2 cm out with the chain's own flow text admitting it was bridged across 12.22 cm of empty space. The two survey specks 142002 and 143003 are the same size, 0.6-0.7 cm and 1.3-1.4e4 e/cm, at 38.5 and 41.6 cm; in all three azimuths the three brown squares lie along one common direction out of the stop, with the near one about a third of the way to the far pair, so they are on the decay's side rather than scattered around the 60 cm ring, and I called them gamma too. All three planes show one clean stripe ending where the fit ends with no dead band at the stop.

notes: Medium: the fit ends on 8.2e4 then 1.215e5, which is in the band real stoppers reach, but the preceding 10 cm are flat at plateau where a stopper should already be 1.3-1.7x, so I read a 1.1 cm hot blob rather than a Bragg peak. evidence: 120.7 cm chain in four segments, entering 9.6 cm from a z face and ending 22.8 cm from the z wall, 195 cm from the anode, so the fit end is inside. The chain itself is a suspicious assembly: segment 17011 is 36.4 cm at a mean 5921 e/cm, essentially an uncharged bridge, the three azimuths show the object zig-zagging with a long dotted grey gap between two charged stretches, and range, dQ/dx and MCS give 295, 184 and 91 MeV, a factor of three apart. At 4x the profile from s=45 in to s=3 is flat at 4.0-5.5e4, straddling the muon reference's 4.8e4 plateau, with a single 8.9e4 delta point at s=26; the near-zero strings beyond s=50 and s=85 are 17011's uncharged points. The only Bragg-like feature is the last centimetre: 8.2e4 at s=2 and 1.215e5 at s=0.5, which is 1.7 and 2.5 times plateau and lands close to the muon curve at those residual ranges. A real stopper is elevated over its whole last ten centimetres - the muon curve wants 6.5e4 at s=8, 7.3e4 at s=6 and 8.0e4 at s=4 - and here s=3 to s=10 sits at 4.0-5.5e4, indistinguishable from the plateau 40 cm back, so the rise occupies about 1.1 cm, two points at 0.56 cm spacing. notes: THRU on the operative test: no Bragg rise at the fit end, charge declining to well below MIP at the last point. Deliberately NOT the overshoot case - the rubric requires a peak several cm before the fit end followed by a collapse, and here there is no peak at all before the collapse, only a monotone decline from the entry wall inward, so I left the pin alone rather than promote the low tail to a michel. Competing reading recorded: the only Bragg-shaped charge in this item is at the OTHER end, 1.1 cm from the y face, which would make the fit direction-reversed with the true stop on the wall - still not a contained stopper either way. Confidence medium and not high because two of three planes are dead at the fit end, so the last few centimetres are genuinely unmeasurable rather than measured flat.
evidence: 43.6 cm chain: the fit enters 1.1 cm from the y face and its last point sits 24.4 cm from the nearest face (in_fv 1), so containment is not the issue here. The profile is the issue. So there is no rise above the plateau anywhere before the collapse - the profile falls toward the fit end, the opposite of a Bragg peak, and the chain agrees (reject no_bragg, shape_flat). f_meas puts the stop end squarely on hatched dead-channel bands in BOTH U (~1850-1890) and V (~5630-5650), so those last centimetres are under-measured: this reads as the imaging running out / a dead-region exit, not as a stop. All three drawn objects are fitted chain segments and are tagged muon.

notes: Flat to the last point with the stop 12.4 cm short of the y wall - the rubric case where no continuation is visible and the cluster just ends where the imaging ran out. Dead channels are present but at the entry end, so they do not explain the flat tail.

notes: Flat to the last point, no continuation drawn and no face reached - the rubric case where the cluster ends where the imaging ran out. Neither failure mode applies: nothing exists past the fit end to be an undershoot tip, and the terminal charge neither peaks nor collapses.

There is no rise off the plateau at any point near the end; the only excursions above it are isolated hot points at s = 8, 18-31 and 85-95 (up to 1.26e5) which sit on the body and read as delta activity, and a handful of low points at s = 28 and 85-92 which are ordinary scatter. 254 cm whose fit ends 112 cm from every face, dQ/dx flat at 4-6e4 to the last point with no rise, and MCS returning its 4000 MeV ceiling at amb 1.00 against 586 MeV from range. The display draws ONE object and nothing at all past the end. No Bragg and no decay activity is the owner's TGM case.

notes: Flat at MIP to the last point; the fit end coincides with a U dead band, which is the leave-through-a-dead-region case f_meas is there to catch. Neither failure mode: no peak-then-collapse, and nothing sits past the fit end to be an undershoot tip.
evidence: 130.3 cm chain in seven fitted segments, entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 35.9 cm from that same wall and 40.0 cm from the anode face - not at a wall, but not deep either. The dQ/dx is noisy (this track carries a lot of associated activity: four unassigned pdg 11 shower pieces strung along its body, all at cos_fwd -1.0) yet its centre of mass is a 4-5e4 band from s = 130 all the way in, and the last points are 4.9e4 and 4.8e4 - dead on that same band, with the terminal segment 51001 (3 pts, 1.5 cm) averaging 48428 against 46867 for the 46.6 cm segment behind it.
