notes: UNDERSHOOT: the fit stops about 2.2 cm short. The real stop is at the far end of 39009, the vertex square one segment past the star. 39009 is tagged muon rather than michel despite the chain offering it as the Michel core, because its points reach 1.03-1.115e5, above the muon chain own last point and squarely in the rubric 0.9-1.2e5 band, and it is collinear with the incoming track. Confidence medium, not high, because the median of 39009 is 7.4e4, only about 1.4 times MIP, so the rubric several-times-MIP phrasing is not met even though its explicit numeric band is; the two top points, the collinearity and the sharp ninety-degree kink into sub-MIP falling charge at 39007 are what carry the call. Pin not moved: --pin-rr cannot move past the fit last point.
evidence: Short object: a 47 cm chain of 137.6 MeV that enters in the corner, 0.2 cm from the z face and 2.1 cm from the anode x face, and whose fit ends 28.9 cm from the z wall. The Bragg rise is unambiguous and clean: 4.0-5.5e4 at s=40-47, 4.5-7.0e4 at s=20-35, 6.5-8.3e4 at s=10-20, 7.8-9.4e4 at s=2.5-5, and 7.6e4 and 1.01e5 at the last two fitted points, tracking the solid muon curve the whole way. The interest is what sits past the fit end. Object 39009 is five points over 2.4 cm with d_min 0.00, d_max 2.18 and cos_fwd +0.92, and on the dQ/dx panel its points include 1.03e5 and 1.115e5 about one centimetre out, the highest charge anywhere on this object and higher than the muon chain reaches at its own last point. The chain calls it the Michel core, pdg 11, with a 21 degree kink. That is the undershoot signature: a two-centimetre piece straight ahead in the 0.9-1.2e5 band cannot be an electron first centimetre, which should be at or below MIP, and the 6x zoom on c_3d_stop and e_3d_stop confirms it is essentially collinear, running on from the star to the next vertex square along the incoming direction with only a slight bend. So 39009 is the muon tip and the true stop is at its far vertex, about 2.2 cm past the fit end. Past that true stop, object 39007, ten points over 2.4 cm spanning d 2.16-4.59 at cos_fwd +0.23, turns roughly ninety degrees out of the muon line in both zoomed azimuths and its charge falls from 6.4e4 to 2.0e4, below MIP and dropping as it goes out, which is the ordinary Michel signature. So there is decay activity past the corrected stop and this is STM_MICHEL, not STM_ONLY. f_meas has measured and predicted matching with no dead band on the stop in U or V, the nearest in W being about 15 channels beyond the end. The remaining object 39006, five points over 2.5 cm at 37-39 cm back with cos_fwd -1.00 and 0.69e4 e/cm, is body activity on the muon line: delta / other.

notes: Flat, low, drift-aligned profile with no terminal rise, so THRU even though the fit end is 45.5 cm from the nearest face. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). Charge quality is poor throughout because the track is nearly parallel to the drift axis and hugs a W dead channel, but the test is a relative rise and there is none. No pin move: no peak, so nothing to collapse from.
evidence: 194.7 cm chain, enters 1.7 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 45.5 cm from the z wall. The track runs almost entirely along the drift direction, from x 338 to x 161 with only 17 cm of z travel, and f_meas shows the consequence: in all three planes it is a near-vertical band covering hundreds of time ticks over about ten channels, and in W it hugs a dead channel at 10030 along its whole length. That is why every charge number here is low, with segment medians of 3.05e4, 2.45e4, 2.12e4 and 3.38e4 against a 5.4e4 reference asymptote, and why the chain quotes 455 MeV from range but only 265 MeV from dQ/dx. Even so the Bragg test is answerable, because a real peak would still show as a factor of two or three relative rise over the last 10-20 cm. There is none. The profile is a broad 0.5-4e4 scatter with periodic dips almost to zero at s=5, 50, 65 and 83, and over the last five centimetres it reads 6.4e4 and 4.1e4 right at the fit end, then 3.1e4, 2.7e4 and 0.3e4 going back, indistinguishable from the band it carries at s=20, 40 and 90. Nothing tracks the solid muon curve, which is at 1.6e5 by s=1 and 8.5e4 by s=10, and the terminal 70 cm segment averages 3.05e4 against 3.38e4 for the 87 cm behind it, that is flat or slightly falling. All three azimuths show a bare amber-banded spine that simply ends at the star with no arm, fan or dot past it, and the object table lists only the four fitted chain segments and nothing else. f_meas has measured and predicted agreeing and the charge stopping cleanly at time slice 1590, with no dead band crossing the end in U or V. Flat to the last point is enough on its own, so THRU, and all four rows are fitted chain segments and take muon.

notes: THRU on both legs: no Bragg rise, and a faint collinear trail of image points carrying about six centimetres past the fit end in all three azimuths. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat). The five-point 1.0-1.14e5 cluster at s=10-12 is a hot spot, matched by two more like it further up the same track, not a terminal peak, so no pin move.
evidence: 324 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the z face and the fit ends 37.6 cm from the z wall. No Bragg rise. The bulk of the profile over the last 9 cm reads 2.55e4, 2.8e4, 3.4e4, 3.5e4, 3.6e4, 4.15e4, 4.3e4, 4.3e4, 4.45e4, 5.1e4, 5.55e4 and 5.67e4, which is at or slightly below the 5.0-5.5e4 plateau the track carries from s=40 out to s=100, so it is flat to falling into the fit end. The tempting feature is a cluster of five points at 1.00e5 to 1.14e5 around s=10-12, but that is not a Bragg peak: the identical thing happens twice more on the same track, at s=23-24 with 9.87e4 and 1.216e5 and at s=69-71 with 9.0-9.5e4, and the band between s=15 and s=22 sits back at 6-7e4 rather than collapsing. These are localized hot spots, deltas or crossings, not a terminal rise, and the bulk never leaves the plateau. That also rules out the overshoot reading, because the region between that cluster and the fit end never falls far below the plateau, only to about half of it with green points at 5.5-5.7e4 interleaved, so there is no sustained collapse to bridge and the pin stays. What does show up is a continuation. Zoomed 6x on both c_3d_stop and e_3d_stop, the thin pale halo line that runs alongside the fitted track for its whole length carries straight on past the star, collinear with the incoming direction, for roughly six centimetres before it runs out; d_3d_stop shows the same faint points above the star. Charge continuing past the fit end is itself the THRU test. f_meas has measured and predicted agreeing, and while the track crosses several dead bands in U along its body, the stop end at U 2615 has clear channels on both sides, so the fit end is not a dead-region exit. The two unassigned pdg-11 shower pieces 52004 and 52007 sit 103-120 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00 carrying 0.84e4 and 2.09e4, hugging the muon body: delta / other.

notes: Hardest item of my twelve. THRU because the last six centimetres of the fit sit on the track own MIP plateau with a dozen points at 4.9-6.75e4 and no rise, which the rubric makes the operative test. Competing reading, which the owner should look at: the seven-point 9.7e4-1.25e5 block at s=10-14 is the Bragg peak, the pin belongs at about s=10, and the three forward dots at 10.6, 18.5 and 24.4 cm are capture gammas, giving STM_ONLY with kind detached dots. I rejected it because the block has normal and low charge on both sides so it is not monotone in residual range, and because there is no charge-free gap along the fit for a bridge to cross. The dots being collinear with the extrapolated direction inside a 35 degree cone also argues continuation rather than isotropic capture gammas. Chain agrees with THRU (no_bragg, shape_flat).
evidence: 205 cm chain, enters 0.3 cm from the anode x face and the fit ends 91.5 cm from the z wall, deeply contained. This is the hardest item in my chunk and I put it at medium. The plateau runs 4.5-6.0e4 from s=100 in to about s=20, and the profile at the fit end is still on that plateau: read at 5.5x, the last six centimetres carry about a dozen points at 4.9-6.75e4 with a single 8.26e4 at s=3.5 and a single 1.13e5 at s=0. Twelve points at MIP over the last six centimetres is what a through-goer looks like, and a stopping muon cannot do it, so by the operative test this is THRU and I leave the pin alone. The competing reading is a block of seven points at 9.74e4, 1.00e5, 1.02e5, 1.028e5, 1.076e5, 1.195e5 and 1.254e5 spread over s=10 to s=14, sitting above the muon curve there, with 7.4-7.8e4 just outside it at s=15-18: taken alone that has a Bragg shape and would put the true stop near s=10. I rejected it for two reasons. First, it is a four-centimetre block with ordinary or low charge on both sides, 2.3e4 at s=9.4 and 4.3e4 at s=7-8 immediately inside it, and a muon dQ/dx is monotone in residual range, so a peak that goes away again is a localized deposit, a delta or a crossing, not a Bragg peak. Second, the overshoot mechanism needs the fit past the true stop to be a low-charge bridge across a gap, and there is no gap: f_meas shows continuous amber measured charge along the fit right to its tip in U, V and W, at the same level as the rest of the body. Past the fit end there is a genuinely empty 10.6 cm with no dead channel in any plane, then three tiny detached pieces, 130004 at 10.6 cm with 2 points, 131005 at 18.5 cm with 2 points and 132006 at 24.4 cm with 3 points, at cos_fwd +0.98, +0.84 and +0.81. The chain offers 130004 as a Michel of 0.7 MeV bridged across 10.62 cm of empty space, which by the attachment rule is a detached dot and not a 35 MeV electron. Those three dots are also very nearly collinear with each other and with the extrapolated track direction in b, c and e, all inside a forward cone of about 35 degrees, which is what a sparsely imaged continuation looks like and not what isotropic muon-capture gammas look like. So they read as fragments of the continuing track. On a THRU the tag alphabet has no stop to define gamma or michel against, so all three take delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit at the end - the cluster simply ran out of imaging 123 cm inside the volume. Per the rubric a flat profile is enough on its own for THRU, so I did not reach for UNCLEAR. THRU tag convention applied: the 11 group=muon fitted chain segments are muon, the 6 group=unassigned rows (143031 plus fitted-but-off-chain 58013/58019/58026/58028/58030) are delta / other, kind none.
evidence: 265 cm chain, enters 6.8 cm from the y face and the fit end sits 123 cm from the nearest (z) wall, so containment is not the question here. The profile is a flat 4.5-5.5e4 MIP plateau from s=100 all the way in to s=5, never leaving it and never taking the shape of the muon reference curve, which asymptotes to 1.6e5 at s=0; the last ~4 cm then fall to 1.2-4.0e4. I considered the overshoot reading (peak then collapse) and rejected it: the only points above 1e5 are isolated singles at s~15, 26, 60 and 82, i.e. they occur all along the body, not as a sustained rise in the last 10-20 cm, so they are the factor-two point-to-point scatter the rubric warns about, not a Bragg peak. With no peak preceding it the terminal dip is just partial-charge end points. The 3-D azimuths show the spine ending abruptly with nothing attached or detached past the star, and the chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The one non-body object, 143031, is 2 points / 0.8 cm at dstop 30.7 and is the grey cross at s=-30, y=5.5e4 on the dQ/dx panel - the negative s is only its 3-D distance, not a side. f_meas shows dead bands in V near 6890 and in W near 11655 but both cross the track mid-body, not at the fit end, so this is not a dead-region exit either.

notes: Not an undershoot: the Bragg maximum is reached at the fit last point, not 1-3 cm past it. 68002 tagged muon as an unfitted tip stub.
evidence: 180 cm chain, enters 2.8 cm from a z face and the fit end sits 69.5 cm from the nearest (z) wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg on my chunk: the profile leaves the electron reference at about 6.7e4 near s=13 and climbs monotonically along the shape of the muon curve through 8e4, 9.5e4, 1.1e5 to 1.35e5 at the fit last point, a factor 2.6 above the bodys own 5.1e4 plateau. I checked the undershoot explicitly because 68002 is exactly the shape that fakes it - 4 points, 1.8 cm, 9.6e4 e/cm, straight ahead at cos_fwd 0.76 - but the diagnostic fails: the peak is AT the fit last point, not past it, and 68002 sits BELOW the peak, so it is simply the muons own unfitted last 1.7 cm and I tagged it muon (the chain calls it pdg 2212, not a Michel, so nothing is being manufactured here either way). Past the stop there are only two specks, 204003 (2 pts, 0.3 cm, 1.8e4) at 20.5 cm and 205004 (3 pts, 1.2 cm, 8.9e3) at 15.3 cm. Computing them against the local forward direction they sit 20.2 cm and 14.4 cm OFF the muon line at azimuth -142 and -143 deg, i.e. the same side of the stop as each other and nowhere near the body, so the chains gamma/Michel body-exclusion labels are wrong about the geometry and the rubrics off-axis rule outranks them. Both are detached with a clean gap and far too small to be a 35 MeV electron - 5 points between them - so they are capture-gamma dots, which does not promote the item past STM_ONLY. f_meas shows the two dots as isolated real charge in all three planes below the track end; the U plane has a dense dead-channel forest but the track and the stop are on live channels.

notes: michel_kind hangs entirely on one 2-point speck: I read 106001 as gamma because the tag tables gamma rule is met literally (isolated, past the stop, 35 cm clear of the body line, inside 60 cm) and charge is explicitly not a criterion. The live competing reading is that a lone speck 36 cm out in no particular direction, with no decay arm anywhere to define a Michel side, is unrelated charge - that would make this STM_ONLY / none. Hence medium.
evidence: 194 cm curving chain, enters 12.8 cm from the lower y face and the fit end is 72.1 cm from the nearest wall, well contained; the 3-D azimuths show a clean single spine ending at the star with nothing attached. The Bragg is unambiguous: the profile sits on a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau out at s=20-40, lifts through 6.7e4 at s=9-11, 9.5e4 at s=7, 1.06-1.13e5 at s=4-6, 1.21e5 at s=2 and 1.45e5 at s=1, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve, about 2.5 times its own plateau. Exactly two points sit at s=0 itself, at roughly 6.5e4 and 3.5e4. I considered moving the pin back 1-2 cm for those, and did not: the rubric calls a partial-charge point or two at the very end ordinary scatter and reserves the pin move for a sustained collapse over several cm, which this is not - the fall is one point wide right against the peak. The only other drawn object is 106001, a 2-point 0.4 cm survey speck the chain never offered to either stage. Against the local forward direction it lies 36.4 cm from the stop, 35.1 cm OFF the muon line and on the forward side, so it is nowhere near the body and cannot be delta by the body rule; f_meas shows it as isolated real charge in all three planes, about 67 time slices and a few channels away from the track end, with no dead band at the stop in any plane.

notes: The kind call is the soft part. 227030/227031 meet every stated clause of the gamma rule (isolated, clear of the body line by 50 cm, inside the 60 cm ring, detached with a clean charge-free gap confirmed on the full azimuths), and the rubric says charge is explicitly not a criterion, so I tagged them gamma and the item is detached dots. The competing reading is the delta rules last clause, belongs to a different object entirely: 25 points over ~14 cm at MIP charge is more than a capture-gamma speck, and it sits 50 cm off-axis in no particular direction with no Michel anywhere to define a decay side. The full frames weakened that reading - the piece is a short compact arc rather than a through-going fragment - but did not kill it, so this stays medium. Under the other reading the record would be STM_ONLY / none.
evidence: 341 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the anode x face, fit end 47.1 cm from the y wall and in_fv. Textbook Bragg: the profile leaves the electron reference near 6.0-6.4e4 at s=10-12 and climbs along the shape of the muon curve through 7.6e4 at s=7, 8.2e4 at s=5, 9.4e4 at s=3, 1.04e5 at s=2, 1.17e5 at s=1 and 1.31e5 at the last point, about 2.8 times the 4.4-4.7e4 body plateau and monotone enough that no pin question arises. The three stop azimuths at full extent show the spine simply ending at the star with nothing attached and no arm, matching n_stop_arms 0. 58025 (9.6 cm, 1.6e4) and 58027 (12.1 cm, 1.7e4) sit at d 11.5-25 cm with transverse offsets of 0.1 and 3.8 cm from the muon line, i.e. they hug the body, so they are delta / other whatever the chains pdg 11 shower label says. The only thing off the body is the pair 227030 + 227031, 13 and 12 points over 7.3 and 6.6 cm at 3.9e4 and 5.3e4 e/cm: computed against the local forward direction they lie 50.5 and 54.7 cm OFF the muon line, about 14-15 cm behind the stop plane, at essentially one azimuth (125 and 129 deg), so they are one structure sitting in the 60 cm ring beside the stop. On the uncropped azimuths that structure reads as a short curved arc of a dozen or so points, separated from the spine by a wide charge-free gap in all three views - detached and compact, not a track running alongside. f_meas shows it as a clean isolated blob in all three planes, ~50 time slices from the track end, real charge and not a fit artefact. No dead band at the stop in U or W; V has a hatched band at 7540-7565 that the track skirts, but the Bragg peak is intact so it costs nothing here.
The track did not go to the end of the track ... which seems to have a Michel ...

notes: THRU on both routes: no Bragg rise AND the fit end is 1.1 cm from the y wall. THRU tag convention applied - the 7 group=muon fitted chain segments are muon and all 32 unassigned rows (including the 783-point C49) are delta / other, kind none; several of those rows would otherwise have argued for gamma on distance alone, which is exactly the case the THRU convention exists to prevent.
evidence: 574 cm chain, enters 2.9 cm from a z face and the fit end sits 1.1 cm from the y wall and 3.9 cm from the z wall - a corner exit, and in_fv is 0. The side projection shows the spine running from Y=+95 straight down to Y=-330 against the bottom of the box, so this one does reach a face, but the operative test agrees independently: the profile has no rise. The plateau out at s=20-45 is 4-5e4 and over the last 20 cm it stays at 3-5e4, nowhere near the shape of the muon curve; the only excursion is a single 8.7e4 point at s=0, which is one point of the ordinary factor-two scatter and not a sustained climb, and the two neighbouring points at s=1-2 are 5.5e4 and 2.2e4. The chain rejects on all three of no_bragg, shape_flat and stop_near_boundary. There is a great deal of other charge drawn here - 32 unassigned rows including C49, 783 points over 152 cm with no PR segment - but computing them against the local forward direction they form one population at azimuth -70 to -102 deg, 30-67 cm off the muon line and 40-70 cm from the stop, i.e. a separate shower/track sitting to one side and visible as its own long ribbon of segments in the second stop azimuth. It is not decay charge from this fit end and it is not on the muon body either; it belongs to a different object. f_meas shows that population as its own cluster of blobs 50-150 time slices off the track in all three planes.

notes: Single-row item; no gamma/michel judgement needed, kind none follows.
evidence: Short, clean 76 cm muon: enters 0.8 cm from the y face and the fit end sits 29.7 cm from the nearest (z) wall, comfortably inside. The profile is the cleanest kind of Bragg on a short track - about 5-6e4 out at s=25-40, lifting through 6.5-7.5e4 at s=10-15, 8.5e4 at s=7-9, 9.5e4 at s=4-5, 1.02e5 at s=2-3 and 1.13-1.15e5 at the last centimetre, hugging the shape of the muon reference curve the whole way and finishing about 2.2 times its own plateau. Nothing to argue about on the pin: the peak is at the fit end and there is no collapse. Nothing sits past the stop either - the object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and the three stop azimuths show the spine terminating at the star with clean empty space beyond it; the only points in that space are the faint thinned context dots and the header explicitly says the 7 nearby blobs belong to another flash, not this stop. So no arm, no dot, no gamma candidate, and n_stop_arms 0 / n_dots 0 agrees. f_meas has a dense dead-channel forest in U at 2350-2450 but the track sits at 2480-2510 and the stop end is on live channels in all three planes, so the Bragg rise is measured charge and not an artefact.

notes: Ordinary STM_MICHEL, the case the rubric contrasts with the undershoot: the forward piece is at or below MIP and long, so it is the electron and not the muons last centimetres.
evidence: Short low-energy stopper: 29 cm of chain, KE 97 MeV by range, entering 1.5 cm from the z face and stopping 21.5 cm from the nearest z wall, so both ends are accounted for and this is not a fragment. The Bragg is emphatic for such a short track - the chain points climb from about 5e4 at s=25-30 through 6-7e4 at s=10-20 and 8.5-9.5e4 at s=5-8 to 1.2-1.55e5 in the last 3 cm, roughly three times the plateau and right on the shape of the muon curve. The very last point or two come back to about 1.15e5 from the 1.55e5 peak 1.5 cm earlier; that is a 25 percent dip one point wide, which the rubric calls ordinary scatter, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse that would move the pin, so I left the pin at the fit end. Past the stop there is a single arm, 46012: 13 points over 7.2 cm attached at the very vertex where the chain ends, and on the dQ/dx panel its points (plotted on the negative axis at |s| 0-7, which is only their 3-D distance and says nothing about side) run 2.4e4 to 6.6e4, i.e. straddling MIP and mostly below it. A muon at a 1.5e5 Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle, and 7 cm of sub-MIP charge leaving the stop at a 31 deg kink is exactly a ~17 MeV Michel. I checked the undershoot case and it does not apply: the tip here is 7.2 cm at MIP, not a 2 cm piece at several times MIP. No dead band anywhere near the stop in any plane; the three azimuths show the amber muon, the vertex square and the blue arm as one clean Y.

notes: THRU on the flat-profile test with no visible continuation, no face and no clean dead-region exit at the end - the cluster ended 30 cm inside the volume where the imaging ran out, which the rubric says is enough on its own; I did not use UNCLEAR. Competing reading, and why this is medium not high: the last 2-3 cm do reach 1.0e5 against a 6.5-7.0e4 plateau, and if that pair is read as a genuine weak Bragg the item becomes STM_ONLY / none. I rejected it because the same size excursion appears at s=19-20 and a much bigger one at s=38, and because there is no rise over the preceding 10-20 cm. Note the track runs nearly along the drift, so it spans only ~25 channels over 145 time slices and its dQ/dx is poorly sampled in any case.
evidence: 109 cm track running almost along the drift direction: enters 12.7 cm from a z face and the fit end is 30.0 cm from the nearest z wall, in_fv, and the 3-D azimuths show it simply terminating at the star with nothing attached or detached beyond it (only two rows in the table, both muon chain segments, and n_stop_arms 0 / n_dots 0). The profile does not rise. Its upper envelope is about 6.5-7.0e4 from s=100 all the way in to s=5, and the excursions above that are not localised at the end: 8.4-9.3e4 at s=19-20, 9.9-10.2e4 at s=0-3, and a spike of 1.09-1.41e5 at s=37-39, which is 39 cm back from the fit end and can only be a delta ray or an overlap. That last one is the useful control - it shows this track produces 1.4e5 points mid-body, so the 1.0e5 pair in the last 3 cm is the same population, not a Bragg peak. There is also no gradient over the last 10-20 cm, which is the interval the test is defined on: s=20, 15, 10 and 5 all sit at 6.5-7.0e4 with sub-MIP points down to 3.1e4 mixed in. The chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) and its momentum fit is internally inconsistent - MCS 481 MeV against 272 MeV by range with amb 0.76, i.e. the track is straighter than a 272 MeV muon should be. f_meas shows the U plane is a dead-channel forest here, with bands at 1440-1450 and 1470-1490 flanking the track at 1445-1470, which is a plausible reason for the cluster to end where it does.

220 cm, enters 1.2 cm from the anode face, stops 79.8 cm from the nearest wall. Clean Bragg: 5e4 plateau rising to 9e4 in the last 3 cm along the muon curve. A three-piece 9.6 cm arm leaves the stop roughly perpendicular to the muon (cos_fwd -0.11 to -0.26) at 2.7-6.4e4 e/cm. Sideways rather than forward, which is what a Michel does and what a broken continuation does not.

notes: 1.52e5 terminal point is above the rubric's stated 1.2-1.35e5 band for real stoppers here and essentially touches the muon reference curve; judged on shape as the rubric directs. No undershoot, no overshoot.
evidence: A 555 cm cosmic muon (chain KE 1259 MeV) entering 0.5 cm from the anode x face and stopping 72.1 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1, so containment is a comfortable numbers call. Upscaled 4x, g_dqdx sits on a 5.0-5.5e4 MIP plateau for 100 cm and then climbs smoothly along the shape of the muon reference curve over the last ~10 cm, 6e4 at s=10, 8e4 at s=5, 1.05e5 at s=2 and a terminal 1.52e5 at s=0 - the cleanest possible Bragg, and it peaks AT the fit's last point with no peak-then-collapse, so the pin stays where the fit put it. The blue near-zero points at s=45-47 are mid-track fit points with no measured charge, not a terminal collapse. Nothing sits forward of the stop at all: every drawn row has negative cos_fwd and the nearest non-body object is 47.6 cm away, so the undershoot signature (a high-charge 1e5 tip a couple of cm straight ahead) cannot apply here either. 75005/75009/75012/75013 are the four fitted chain segments running 0-526 cm back up the body, transverse offsets 0-39 cm on a 555 cm chord, all muon. 75011 is a 3 cm 6-point pdg-11 shower speck 210 cm back at cos_fwd -0.97 and 10 cm off the body line: body activity, delta / other. The call I had to weigh is the three 2-point survey specks 189014/190015/192016 at 47.6/49.8/52.4 cm, dqdx 1.8-5.7e4: they are well clear of the muon line (transverse 30/43/49 cm) which pulls towards gamma, but projecting them onto the muon axis puts all three 19-37 cm BEHIND the plane through the stop, so they are not past the stop and the gamma rule does not reach them; they are also three isolated blips with 11 and 23 cm charge-free gaps between them, not a radial trail from the stop, and with no Michel there is no decay side for the faint-far-speck rule to key on. Called delta / other, hence kind none. f_meas shows the track terminating cleanly at time slice ~930 in all three planes with the hatched dead bands (U 1320-1340, V 5130, W 9280) alongside but not at the end, so this is not a dead-region exit.

notes: Flat profile is the operative test and it is met, so THRU even though the fit end is 87.9 cm from every face with no visible continuation and no dead-region exit - the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. No undershoot (no forward object exists at all), no overshoot (no peak-then-collapse; the last 2 cm sit above, not below, the plateau).

The 4x profile is dead flat: a ~5.2e4 plateau with the usual factor-two scatter runs the whole 100 cm and is still 4.5-5.5e4 at s = 1-12 cm, with no hint of a climb toward the muon reference curve; the only sub-plateau points are the last two, 3.9e4 and 1.9e4 at s = 0-1, which is the ordinary terminal-scatter case the rubric tells me to leave alone, not a sustained collapse off a peak -- there is no peak above plateau anywhere to collapse from. That is the operative THRU test and it settles the item. f_meas explains where it went: at the fit end (time slice ~1595) the track sits a few channels from a dead band in ALL THREE planes -- U 3450 with the band at 3425-3435, V 7205 with the band at 7195, W 11915 with the band at 11890 -- and the track is running toward decreasing channel in every plane, so it walks straight into dead material. The chain Michel object 164007 is a 2-point 0.9 cm dot at 9.1e4 e/cm sitting 8.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.08, bridged by the chain across 7.99 cm of empty space by proximity alone, and 53004 is a 5 cm pdg-11 shower blob at cos_fwd -1.0 hugging the body 18-21 cm back; 163006 is a faint 1.5e4 pair 50.5 cm out. notes: Awkward item, medium. The fit overshoots the charge by ~45 cm through a near-empty region, so the terminal collapse is a fit artefact, not the rubrics peak-then-collapse: there is no peak above plateau anywhere to collapse FROM, so I did not move the pin -- and moving it would not help, because at the real end of the charge (s ~ 45) the profile is still flat plateau with no Bragg. Competing reading is UNCLEAR, on the grounds that the last 45 cm of fit is not measuring anything; I rejected it because the 215 cm of real track that IS measured answers the question on its own. evidence: 260 cm chain in 12 fitted segments, enters 0.4 cm from the z face and the fit ends 133.8 cm from the nearest wall. From s = 100 cm down to s = 45 cm the profile is an ordinary 5.5-7e4 MIP plateau with no trend. Below s = 45 cm it does not rise -- it falls, smoothly and over 45 cm, into a low arch that tops out at 2.5e4 near s = 18 and sits at 0.5-1.5e4 (effectively zero-charge fit points) at s = 0-8 and s = 28-40. The 3-D azimuths say what that is: the dense spine ends in a knot of vertices about 45 cm short of the pin and the fit then runs on as a thin, almost charge-free dotted trail to the star, which is exactly the chains own profile_sparse rejection. So the real end of the charge is at s ~ 45, and THERE the profile is flat on its own plateau at 5.5e4 with no climb toward the muon reference curve -- no Bragg rise at either candidate end, which is the operative through-goer test. Nothing here can be a Michel: 45 cm of tail is twice the range of the most energetic Michel possible, and the chains own Michel object 222048 is a 2-point 0.4 cm dot at 8.5e4 sitting 13.1 cm out, bridged across 13.07 cm of empty space by proximity. Under the THRU tag convention all twelve fitted segments are muon and every other row -- 222048, the gamma-body-exclusion speck 223049 at 17.9 cm cos_fwd -0.98, the survey specks 224050 (42.4 cm) and 225051 (35.6 cm), and the six pdg-11 shower blobs at cos_fwd -0.98 to -1.0 hugging the body between 26 and 108 cm -- is delta / other, kind none. notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit; called THRU on the profile alone as the rubric directs. notes: Medium, and the reason is worth recording: this items last 39 cm is not measured, not flat -- the fit interpolates 12 points across it at 0.2 MIP and there is a 29 cm stretch with literally no plotted point. notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence on its own; the medium is for michel_kind. All three near specks are detached compact pieces 33-42 cm out and 15-36 cm off the muon line, clustered within ~50 deg of each other on one side of the ring, which is the rubrics gamma reading; if the owner instead reads three specks 30 cm apart from each other as scattered, or lets 282052s cos_fwd -0.9 keep it on the body line, the kind falls back to none while the verdict does not move. evidence: 772 cm cosmic, enters 0.1 cm from the x (anode) face at [339.8, 158.0, 230.5] and stops at [-307.7, -103.8, 76.3], 32.2 cm from the anode face and comfortably inside. It is monotone, not ragged, and there is no terminal collapse and no forward high-charge tip past the fit end, so neither fit-failure mode applies and I left the pin alone. Nothing is attached at the stop -- n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 -- so there is no Michel and the verdict is STM_ONLY. What IS there are three faint specks: 278050 (3 points, 1.1 cm, 1.2e4 e/cm) at 33.4 cm, 282052 (4 points, 1.7 cm, 3.5e4) at 35.3 cm and 281051 (2 points, 0.1 cm, 2.9e4) at 41.6 cm. The chain labels two of them gamma body exclusion, which the rubric tells me the off-axis judgement outranks; 282052 is the one that tests it, since its cos_fwd -0.9 formally trips the on-the-body clause while it actually sits 15 cm off the line. Three capture gammas past the stop and no michel piece give michel_kind detached dots without promoting the verdict. The four pdg-11 shower blobs 75034, 75040, 75043 and 75049 are 4.7-5.7 METRES back along the body at cos_fwd -0.97: delta / other. Range KE 1715.0 MeV against MCS 1613.4 MeV with amb 0.00 -- a consistent stopper.

notes: Cleanest item in my chunk: monotone Bragg on the reference curve, no object of any kind past the stop, no dead band downstream. Pin unmoved; neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies.
evidence: 80.2 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from the z face at [254.3, 179.2, 297.9] and stops at [208.9, 184.3, 234.6], 63.9 cm from the nearest wall and well inside the volume. Neither fit-failure mode is present: the highest points are the LAST points, so there is no peak-then-collapse to move the pin back for, and there is no forward object at all past the fit end, so nothing to invoke the undershoot on. The pin is left where the fit put it. Nothing is past the stop either: the object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, 0 unfitted dot clusters and no capture gamma in the ring. notes: Flat profile to the last point with no visible continuation to a face or dead region -- THRU on the profile test alone, per the rubric. Deeply contained (58.6 cm) which is the only uncomfortable part of the call. Chain agrees (reject no_bragg, shape_flat) but the call was made from the plot first.
evidence: 294 cm chain, enters 0.6 cm from the x (anode) face and the fit ends 58.6 cm from the nearest wall, so containment alone would suggest a stopper. The dQ/dx panel says otherwise. At 6x the band from s=0 to s=20 sits on a 3.5-7.5e4 scatter with its top envelope about 7.5e4 at s=5-7 -- and the same envelope reaches 9e4 at s=45 and 1.05-1.26e5 at s=33-62, i.e. the charge is HIGHER further back up the muon than it is at the fit end. There is no rise off the plateau following the solid muon curve anywhere in the last 10-20 cm; the profile is flat-to-falling into the origin. The only structure at the end is four dark points at about 2e4 inside the last 1.5 cm, but low points of exactly that depth recur all along the track (a 1.2e4 cluster at s=8-11 and another at s=38-40), so they are this track s ordinary scatter and not a localised collapse. I considered the overshoot reading (peak at s=5-7 then collapse to 0.4 MIP) and rejected it: 7.5e4 is only 1.4x this track s own MIP and is matched at four other arc lengths, so it is not a Bragg peak, and the low stretch is 1.5 cm not several cm. f_meas shows a faint cyan trace continuing below the amber selection band past the fit end in both U and V, consistent with the cluster simply running out of image. No object row has d_min under 33 cm, so there is nothing attached at or past the stop to be a Michel; the three unassigned pdg-11 rows sit 35, 102 and 137 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00, hugging the muon body, and are absent from the dQ/dx panel entirely. Body activity, tagged delta / other.

notes: The only judgement call was the two survey-only clusters: 20-26 cm off the chord would make them gammas if they were past the stop, but they are 40-51 cm back up the muon and on the far side from the Michel arm, so delta / other and kind stays attached rather than both.
evidence: 98 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the z face and the fit ends 15.9 cm from the anode face, deep enough to be a real stop. The dQ/dx panel is a textbook Bragg: a 5.4e4 plateau beyond s=40 climbing smoothly through 6.5e4 at s=15, 8e4 at s=6, 1.0e5 at s=3 and 1.20-1.26e5 in the last centimetre, tracking the solid muon curve point for point with almost no scatter -- the cleanest rise I could ask for. Past the stop the Michel row 31007 plots as large markers on the negative axis at magnitude 2-5 cm carrying 3.5-5.9e4 e/cm, i.e. at or a little below this track s own MIP, and a muon sitting at 1.26e5 cannot continue at 4e4, so the arm is a second particle; 5.4 cm and 12.7 MeV is the right scale for a low-energy Michel. Frames d and e show it plainly: a short blue arm leaving the amber band at the star vertex at a wide angle (chain kink 56 deg), attached, no gap. I computed off-axis distances against the entry-stop chord (93.2 cm, and the chord length matches d_max 93.7 so the track is straight in 3-D even though frame b looks bent): the Michel is 2.0 cm off and 1.4 cm past the stop. The two survey-only clusters sit 50.7 and 39.8 cm BACK along the muon at 19.7 and 25.6 cm off the chord. They are well clear of the body line, so I weighed gamma, but the gamma rule needs the piece to be past the stop and these are behind it, on the opposite side from the Michel arm, in unrelated directions, and neither stage was ever offered them -- separate objects, so delta / other. Neither appears on the dQ/dx panel at s = -47 or -54, which is the known census gap, not evidence of absence. No dead channel at the stop in any plane; f_meas shows the track simply ending.

notes: Chain also calls it STM with no daughter; I reached STM_ONLY from the profile and the empty negative axis before reading that. The peak at s=3.8 rather than s=0 was the one thing worth a second look and the 9x re-read settled it against the overshoot. MCS 40 MeV vs range 604 MeV is flagged amb 1.00 in the status line and I ignored it.
evidence: 262 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends 30.2 cm from the nearest wall, comfortably inside. The dQ/dx panel shows an unambiguous Bragg: the plateau beyond s=20 sits at 4.0-4.7e4 with the usual scatter down to 2e4, and from s=15 inward the profile lifts off it and follows the solid muon curve -- 6.0e4 at s=10.6, 7.4-7.9e4 at s=5-10, 8.5e4 at s=2.3-9, 9.3e4 at s=2.9, 9.95-1.02e5 at s=4.4-9.6 and a 1.12e5 point at s=3.8, right at the 1.2-1.35e5 ceiling real stoppers reach here. That is a rise of about 2.5x over the track s own MIP in the last 15 cm. Because the peak sits a few cm short of the origin I re-read the last 20 cm at 9x and read the values off the gridlines rather than eyeballing them: the six points inside s=0-2 come in at 9.67e4 (twice), 7.66e4 (three times) and 6.41e4. Every one of them is well ABOVE the 4.0-4.7e4 plateau -- 1.4 to 2.1 times it -- where a bridged Michel segment would be at 0.15-0.5 of MIP, and the dip spans about 2 cm rather than several. So this is near-peak scatter, not the overshoot signature, and the pin stays on the fit s last point. Nothing at all is plotted on the negative axis and nothing leaves the star in frames c, d or e -- the point cloud simply terminates in a yellow high-charge tip. The object table agrees: every row is on the muon side, all five fitted segments at cos_fwd -1.00, and the single unassigned row 57011 is a 2-point 0.9 cm speck 147.5 cm back sitting 2.6 cm off the entry-stop chord, i.e. on the muon body, so delta / other. notes: Flat to the last point with no visible continuation, no face and no dead region -- the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. The 98 cm containment is the only thing arguing the other way and the rubric explicitly says the profile test governs.
evidence: 156 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the z face, and the fit ends 98.2 cm from the nearest wall and 26 cm from the cathode -- about as deeply contained as an end can be, which is why I looked hard at the profile before calling this. The profile refuses to cooperate: it is a flat 4.4-5.5e4 band from s=3 all the way out to s=100, sitting on the solid muon curve s own asymptote, with a mild bump to 6.5-7e4 at s=12-15 that is not a peak because the same envelope reaches 8.1e4 at s=40, 8.2e4 at s=52 and 1.0-1.33e5 at s=24 and s=76-88. notes: Confidence medium for the kind, not the verdict: STM_ONLY is solid, but 208004 sits 13.7 cm past the stop and 48 cm off the body and would be a gamma by the letter of the gamma rule, which would make this detached dots. evidence: 112 cm chain, enters 0.1 cm from the x face and the fit ends 71.8 cm from the nearest wall, well inside. The dQ/dx panel is one of the cleanest Braggs in my chunk: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau beyond s=30 lifting to 6-7e4 at s=10-20, 8-9e4 at s=4-8, 9.5-10.4e4 at s=1-3 and a single 1.37e5 point sitting exactly on the origin, the whole rise hugging the solid muon curve. notes: Judged end is a 0.3 cm wall exit with in_fv 0 and a flat profile, so THRU is not in doubt. The drawn cluster is the x<0 half of a cathode-split cosmic; I record that in the evidence rather than as FRAG_THRU because the continuation is at the far end, not the end being judged.
evidence: 235 cm drawn cluster running almost horizontally along the floor of the detector, and the fit end sits 0.3 cm from the y wall with in_fv 0 -- it leaves through the bottom face. The profile confirms it independently: a flat 4.5-5.5e4 band from s=3 out to s=100 with the usual scatter, no lift off the plateau anywhere in the last 10-20 cm, and the five centimetres just before the end actually sag to 3.0-4.0e4. The far end of the drawn cluster is a separate matter: it sits at x = -3.1, on the cathode plane, and the 3-D wide frame zoomed 4x shows a faint thinned trail continuing from the orange entry marker in nearly the same direction for about the same length again, with the end view showing it running on along the floor to x = +240. Michel electrons did not get accessed

notes: The W plane has dead-channel bands adjacent to the track in f_meas but the U and V measured panels carry the stop cleanly, so the Bragg is not a dead-region artefact. evidence: 265 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.3e4 plateau beyond s=40 climbing smoothly along the solid muon curve through 6.0e4 at s=20, 6.7-7.5e4 at s=10-18, 8.7-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.5-1.02e5 at s=3-4, 1.14-1.22e5 at s=1.5-2.5 and 1.39e5 at s=0.5, with the row mean for the last segment 58015 quoted at 1.05e5 over its 7.8 cm. Two gammas and no michel gives detached dots.

notes: Flat to the last point. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat) but the call came from the plot. Not a fragment: only 1 thinned context point in the whole event and no continuation past either end.

notes: Nothing borderline here. The only judgement was gamma versus michel for 137001, and the 60-slice charge-free gap in f_meas plus its two-point zero-extent size settles it as a detached dot.

notes: THRU on a flat/scattered profile alone: no continuation is visible past the fit end, but the last points sit inside the entry islands own charge spread and the profile falls into the fit end rather than rising. notes: The four michel rows are absent from g_dqdx entirely (77 points and 16 cm of charge missing from the panel), so the michel evidence is the object table plus the three azimuths, not the dQ/dx plot. evidence: 423 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and stopping 35.0 cm from the nearest wall, in_fv 1; the projections show one clean spine with no companion, so containment is not in doubt. Past the stop the display draws four forward pieces that my own decomposition places 1.4 to 7.9 cm ahead of the stop and only 1.9-7.1 cm off the muon line: 64011 (10 pts, 5.2 cm, dqdx 13979, attached at d_min 0), then 64008 (14 pts, 8.0 cm, 27935), 64004 (26 pts, 14.9 cm, 11007) and 64003 (27 pts, 15.7 cm, 18041), all starting 4.0-4.7 cm out and reaching 15-16 cm. notes: THRU on a flat profile alone, as the rubric allows: there is no visible continuation past the fit end, no face within 53 cm, and no dead-region exit at the star itself - the cluster just ends. notes: Medium, not high: the competing reading is a very ragged STM_ONLY built on the 1.03e5 point at s=0.7 and the 8.4e4 at s=4. evidence: 84.3 cm chain running almost parallel to the z wall, entering 0.5 cm from it and ending 9.2 cm from the same z face and 13.9 cm from the anode face - a corner stop, so the geometry already argues for an exit, and in_fv 1 only just. notes: Not counted as an overshoot. notes: High confidence: this is not a marginal flat profile, it actually DECLINES into the fit end, so both the STM_ONLY and the pin-move readings fail at the first step. notes: High: the profile does not merely fail to rise, it falls into the fit end, so neither STM_ONLY nor a pin move is on the table. notes: High confidence and nothing marginal about it: one object, a flat profile that declines rather than rises into the fit end, and no candidate decay charge anywhere. The orange entry circle is drawn right at the fit end rather than at the far end here, which is the known display trap - I read the ends from ends.entry / ends.stop, not from the circle.

notes: Not counted as an overshoot, but the fit does over-run: the profile peaks about 8 cm inside the fit end and the muon almost certainly stopped near rr 7.5. The hardest part of this item was telling the s=7-13 lift from a delta cluster; the rubric gives no test for that, so I used point-by-point coherence (every point lifted, monotone over 6 cm) plus a predicted-versus-observed comparison against the reference curve under the two stop hypotheses. Medium: if the owner reads the lift as a long delta, this becomes THRU / none with every non-chain row delta / other; if the owner reads the MIP stretch as a short Michel, it becomes STM_MICHEL / both with the pin at 7.5 and 21009 tagged michel.
evidence: 92.4 cm curved chain entering 2.1 cm from the z face and ending 22.4 cm from that same z wall, in_fv 1; a_proj_full and b_3d_wide show one isolated spine, so not a fragment. Plateau is 5.4e4 out at s=40-90. Past the stop, 85010 is a 5-point 2.1 cm piece 29 cm forward at cos_fwd 0.96 and only 7.0 cm off the muon line, detached across a clean charge-free gap and far too faint at 9370 e/cm to be a 35 MeV electron - a capture gamma, which does not promote the verdict, so the kind is detached dots. 86011 is a 2-point speck 34.7 cm out and 34.6 cm off the line, with its transverse direction cos -1.00 against the gamma, i.e. the exact opposite side of the ring in an unrelated direction: delta / other. The 4.2 cm 8-point stub 84-88 cm back at 13982 e/cm is body activity on the muon side.

This is the textbook Bragg of the twelve: at 4x the profile leaves a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau at s = 45-55, climbs to 7e4 by s = 25, 8-9e4 by s = 8-12, 1.05e5 at s = 5-7, and then 1.14 / 1.29 / 1.44 / 1.56e5 at s = 3.5, 2.5, 1.8, 1.0, riding the muon reference curve the whole way up. The two points at s < 0.5 fall back to 8.8-9.5e4; that is still 1.6x the plateau, nothing like the 0.15-0.5-of-MIP sustained collapse that would mean the fit bridged a gap, so it is last-point scatter and the pin stays at the fit end. Nothing leaves the stop: n_stop_arms 0, and the three azimuths show a bare track end with only the usual thin image-point halo. The one other drawn object, 99007, is a 2-point speck 21.4 cm away at cos_fwd 0.20, which puts it forward of the stop with a 21 cm transverse offset from the muon line - isolated, past the stop, clear of the body, well inside 60 cm, and separated from the end by a completely charge-free gap: gamma, so detached dots, and per the rubric an isolated capture-gamma-like piece does not promote this to STM_MICHEL. Worth flagging for a re-auditor: the U plane has dead bands and the stop end sits at U channel ~1145 next to a dashed dead line at ~1140, but V and W image the end cleanly and a muon leaving through a dead region could not produce a 1.56e5 peak first, so the containment call stands.

311.2 cm chain entering 0.5 cm from the z wall and ending 46.9 cm from the nearest wall - contained by the numbers, and irrelevant, because the profile settles it. At 4x the dQ/dx is flat on a 5.5-6.5e4 plateau from s = 100 all the way in to the last point: the points inside s = 10 read 7.5, 6.5, 6.4, 6.2, 5.9, 5.1, 4.9, 4.85, 4.1, 2.5, 2.4 e4, i.e. the same band as the body with a little low-side scatter, while the muon reference curve over that same stretch climbs from 6.5e4 at s = 10 to 1.15e5 at s = 2. There is no rise off the plateau in any shape, ragged or otherwise. Two isolated single points at 1.18e5 (s = 6) and 1.41e5 (s = 8.5) are the only high values anywhere near the end; single points with the neighbours on either side back at 6e4 are delta-ray hits, not a Bragg shape, and a stopping muon cannot show 1.4e5 at s = 8.5 and then 2.4e4 at s = 2. The three azimuths show a straight uniform spine running into the star with nothing attached, nothing past it, and no widening. Per the rubric a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out; worth noting for the record that it may not even be a mystery, since in f_meas the V plane has a hatched dead band at channels ~6810-6825 and the fit end sits at V ~6812 right inside it, while U (2965, bands at 2850/2870/2900/3040) and W (11210, band at 11070) are clear there. THRU tagging convention applied: the four fitted chain rows 59006, 59001, 59003, 59005 are muon and the one unassigned pdg-11 shower piece 59007 sits 195-199 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, dead on the muon body, so delta / other; kind none because gamma and michel are only defined relative to a stop.

notes: Medium, not high, for one reason: the michel side of this is small - a 4.2 cm fitted tail plus a 2.4 cm unfitted piece, all at 0.25-0.5 of MIP, and the very last fit points measure essentially zero charge in U. The competing reading is STM_ONLY with the pin still moved to 6.5: that the fit simply ran on into nothing past the muon stop and 36013 is a stray fragment rather than an electron. I went with STM_MICHEL because 36013 is real reconstructed charge attached at the stop, forward, off the body line, which the tag alphabet calls michel, and because the collapsed tail carries 2.5-5e4 over five centimetres, too much to be nothing.
evidence: OVERSHOOT item. 201.3 cm, whole object (the wide view shows one curved spine from the anode to the star, the only other charge in the frame being faint thinned context points from other tracks), entering 0.2 cm through the anode face and ending 49.1 cm from the nearest wall. Undershoot screen first: the only forward piece at the stop is 36013 at 2.4 cm and 2.4e4 e/cm, i.e. a third of MIP, nowhere near the 0.9-1.2e5 tip that would mean the fit stopped short - so not that case. The profile at 4x rises off a 5.5e4 plateau in a clean curve-shaped run, not a single-point excursion: 7.6e4 at s = 15, 7.9, 8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6 through s = 14 to 10, then 9.2, 9.3, 9.1 e4 at s = 9-8 and 1.00e5 at s = 7, sitting just above the muon reference curve the whole way. That run of ten consecutive elevated points is quite distinct from this tracks ordinary scatter, whose isolated highs elsewhere (9.5e4 at s = 19, 8.8e4 at s = 51, 8.2e4 at s = 38) are single points with 5-6e4 neighbours on both sides. From s = 6 the profile then collapses and stays collapsed: 5.1, 4.6, 4.5, 4.4, 3.85, 3.4, 3.0, 2.55, 1.7 e4 and finally three points under 1e4 which I discount as no-measured-charge. Falling to a quarter of MIP over five to six centimetres where a muon at its own Bragg peak would be far above it is the fit-bridges-a-gap signature, so the real stop is about 6.5 cm back and the pin goes there. The chains own segmentation agrees: it broke the chain at 3.84 cm, and that whole terminal row 36014 (4.2 cm, 2.79e4) lies inside the collapsed region, so it gets tagged michel; 36010 keeps muon because 195 of its 198 cm are muon, with the last ~2.7 cm belonging to the electron and no row to say so. Also at the stop is 36013, an unfitted 5-point 2.4 cm cluster the chain types pdg 11 at 2.4e4 and then declines to accept (n_stop_arms 1 but no daughter) - attached, forward, well off the body line, so michel. The three azimuths back this: the orange high-charge chain markers stop several cm short of the star and the last stretch to it is drawn in low-dQ/dx teal with a small kink, and in f_meas the U plane, which is live there (its dead band is at 2170-2180, the end at 2205), shows a bright orange body ending in near-black points at the vertex, so the terminal collapse is measured, not a V-plane artefact - though I note the V plane does have a hatched band at ~6040-6055 right where the track ends. Two more objects, 96011 (2 points, 20.0 cm) and 98012 (5 points, 36.4 cm), lie in almost exactly the same direction from the stop (their unit vectors agree to 0.996), forward and well clear of the muon line: a collinear pair of detached dots on the decay side, so gamma for both.

Short one, 38.9 cm, and a whole object - the wide and stop views show a single continuous spine from the entry circle to the star with no companion cluster and nothing that reads as a broken-off piece. It enters 0.4 cm through the anode face and stops 34.5 cm from that same anode face, contained by the numbers. Undershoot screen: no forward piece at the stop at all (n_stop_arms 0), so that failure mode is not in play. The profile is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.5-6.0e4 plateau at s = 25-38, then 6.5-7.5e4 at s = 10-15, 8.4e4 at s = 8, 9.3-9.8e4 at s = 5-6, 1.15-1.20e5 at s = 3-4, 1.27e5 at s = 2 and 1.42e5 at s = 0.8, riding the muon reference curve point for point. The single last point at s = 0.1 sits at 1.08e5, a quarter below the peak - one terminal point low is ordinary scatter, not the sustained several-centimetre collapse that would mean the fit bridged a gap, so the pin stays where it is. Nothing is attached at or leaves the stop in any of the three azimuths: the star sits on a bare track end. Two drawn specks remain, both 2-point and 0.6 cm, and both roughly perpendicular to the muon at the stop. 164001 is 30.5 cm out at cos_fwd 0.04, isolated, compact, entirely clear of the muon body line, with a clean charge-free gap back to the stop, and it is what the chain calls its 3.3 MeV capture gamma - detached dot past the stop, so gamma, which makes the kind detached dots (per the rubric an isolated capture-gamma piece does not promote the verdict to STM_MICHEL). 165002 is 50.3 cm out at cos_fwd -0.01, and I computed the two specks directions from the stop: they point almost opposite ways (their unit vectors dot to -0.49), so this one is not part of any coherent decay-side family, it is a lone survey speck in an unrelated direction at the outer edge of the ring, which the rubrics faint-far-speck rule sends to delta / other. That is the one judgement call here and it does not change the kind either way. No dead band at the stop in any plane (U bands at 3360 and 3425 with the end at 3460, V at 7200/7290/7315 with the end at 7265, W at 11720/11780/11895 with the end at 11850).

120.5 cm, entering 0.5 cm through the anode face and stopping 77.1 cm from the nearest wall. The drawn muon is a whole object - one continuous spine from the entry circle to the star - although it shares the frame with C54, a 622-point 164 cm unfitted cloud whose diffuse blue points spray across and alongside the muon body; C54 has d_min 50 cm and lies at cos_fwd -0.99, i.e. back along the body, so it is a different object crossing the scene and not a continuation of this one. Undershoot screen: nothing sits 1-3 cm ahead of the stop at all (n_stop_arms 0), so that mode is out. The profile is a clean Bragg: a 5.0-5.5e4 plateau from s = 30 to 100, 6.0-6.5e4 at s = 10-15, 7.5-8.5e4 at s = 6-9, 9.3-9.6e4 at s = 4-5, 1.02e5 at s = 3 and 1.15e5 at s = 1.8, tracking the reference curve; the two final points at s < 0.5 fall to 8.7e4 and 7.4e4, still 1.4x the plateau, which is terminal scatter rather than the several-centimetre collapse to a fraction of MIP that would move the pin, so the pin stays. The three azimuths show a bare end: no arm, no widening, nothing bridging out of the star. Object attribution. 177014 is the chains 0.88 MeV capture gamma, 2 points 28.9 cm out at cos_fwd 0.56, isolated and clear of the body across a charge-free gap - gamma, which sets the kind to detached dots without promoting the verdict. Three more faint pieces sit in the same forward cone and I checked their directions from the stop rather than trusting cos_fwd on this slightly curved track: 174011 (4 points, 46.4 cm, straight ahead at 0.93), 176013 (2 points, 50.0 cm, 0.48) and 175012 (2 points, 57.4 cm, 0.71), the last two pointing within 35 deg of each other - a coherent forward family inside the 60 cm ring, so gamma rather than random deltas. The odd one out is 173010, 21 cm away perpendicular to the muon in +y, which is the direction C54 occupies and the one piece the chain itself body-excluded; a lone speck in a direction unrelated to the forward family, so delta / other, as is C54 itself. U has a dead line at channel ~3640 right where the track ends and V a hatched band at 7420, but the Bragg peak is measured before that and W is clear there, so the stop is not a dead-region exit.

notes: The end is abrupt: uniform orange charge to the last point in all three measured planes, live channels either side, 45 cm from the nearest wall, and nothing drawn beyond it. That is the rubrics no-continuation-no-face-no-dead-region case, which it says is still THRU on a flat profile.
evidence: 131.2 cm, dead straight, entering 0.1 cm through the anode face and ending 45.3 cm from the nearest wall (z). Undershoot screen: nothing at all sits ahead of the fit end (n_stop_arms 0, no michel-group row), so that mode is out. The profile is flat on its 5.5-6.0e4 plateau right through to the last point - the points inside s = 7 read 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9, 5.4, 5.5 e4 with two low strays at 3.7 and 4.2e4 - while the muon reference curve over the same stretch climbs from 7e4 at s = 7 to 1.15e5 at s = 2. There is no rise of any shape at the fit end. A cluster of elevated points does sit at s = 8-17 (8.4 to 12.7e4) and I checked whether it could be a Bragg peak with the fit overshooting, but this particular track carries excursions of exactly that size all along its length - 1.03e5 at s = 33, 1.06e5 at s = 42, 1.02e5 at s = 43, 1.31e5 at s = 50, 1.15e5 at s = 64, 1.03e5 at s = 81, 1.17e5 at s = 93 - so the s = 8-17 group is this tracks ordinary delta-ray scatter and not distinctive, and, decisively, the charge after it stays exactly ON the plateau instead of collapsing below it, which is the opposite of the bridge signature. The chains own kinematics agree with a through-goer: MCS gives 1157 MeV against 318 MeV from range (amb 0.90), i.e. the track is far too straight for a muon with only 131 cm of range left. Nothing is attached at or past the end in the three azimuths, and it is not a dead-region exit - the end sits at U 150, V 3920, W 7705, all well clear of the hatched bands (U 10-30/90-100/185/290, V 3810-3830/4000). No visible continuation either, so per the rubric this is the plain case of a cluster that simply ended where the imaging ran out; I say that explicitly rather than reaching for UNCLEAR. Whole object as drawn, no sign of a companion fragment. THRU tagging: the fitted chain 20000 is muon and the one 4-point survey speck 67001, 35 cm back at cos_fwd -0.79, is delta / other; kind none, since gamma and michel are only defined relative to a stop.

277.3 cm, one whole object - a single continuous spine from the entry 0.4 cm inside the z face to the star, no companion fragment in the wide view - stopping 77.9 cm from the nearest wall (y). Undershoot screen: the piece at the stop (45010, d_min 0, cos_fwd 0.66) carries 2.8e4 e/cm, about 0.4 of MIP, not the 0.9-1.2e5 muon tip that fakes a Michel, so the fit did not stop short. The profile is a clean Bragg: 5.4e4 plateau from s = 40 to 100, 6.5-7.8e4 at s = 10-18, 8.4-9.7e4 at s = 3-6, then 1.45, 1.51 and 1.57e5 at s = 1.5, 1.0 and 0.5, riding the muon reference curve into the stop with no terminal dip at all - the pin stays exactly where the fit put it. Past the stop the three michel-group segments form one connected arm that leaves the vertex with a 49 deg kink and runs out to 11.6 cm: 45010 (4.2 cm, 2.8e4), then 45012 (4.8 cm, 1.8e4) and 45011 (9.6 cm, 4.5e4). The whole arm sits at or below the muon plateau and a muon at 1.57e5 cannot continue at a third of MIP, so it is a second particle, and 12 cm with a kink is the right size for the chains 34 MeV electron. In all three azimuths the arm is unambiguous: a blue polyline hanging off the star, well clear of the muon body line. Beyond its tip sit the four points of 116014 at 16.4 cm, and I resolved these the way the rubric asks - their direction from the stop agrees with the arms own direction to 0.93, i.e. they lie squarely on the Michels side rather than in a random direction, but the frames show a clean charge-free gap of several centimetres between the arms last point at 11.6 cm and this piece, so attachment breaks the tie the other way: a detached compact dot, hence gamma and kind both. That is the one judgement call in the item; calling it a further piece of the electron would make the kind attached. The chain labels it gamma body exclusion, which is its reason for not counting it as a capture gamma, not a claim that it is muon body activity - at cos_fwd -0.12 and 16 cm out it is nowhere near the body line. Dead channels: U is busy here (bands at 2380-2400, 2420-2450 and one at 2480-2490 adjacent to the track), but V and W are clear at the stop and the 1.57e5 peak is measured, so the stop is real.

notes: Medium because the Bragg here is modest - a 1.5-1.9x lift over the plateau rather than the 2.5-3x of the clean stoppers in this chunk (039349_51/25 reached 1.56e5, 039349_52/50 1.42e5) - and one could read the whole last 10 cm as a run of delta activity on a through-goer. What tips it for me is that the lift is sustained over a dozen consecutive points and peaks at the very last one, that the chains no_bragg flag is absent, and that MCS 536 MeV agrees with the 562 MeV range estimate (amb 0.04), which a much higher-momentum through-goer would not do.
evidence: 242.9 cm in three fitted pieces, one whole gently curved object from an entry 0.3 cm inside the z face to the star, stopping 101.7 cm from the nearest wall. Undershoot screen: the nearest drawn object of any kind is 48.6 cm away, so there is no forward tip at the stop to mistake for a Michel. The profile does rise, though not dramatically: the plateau is 4.5-5.0e4 out at s = 55-100 and 5.5-6.0e4 at s = 15-40, and then over the last 10 cm nearly every point is elevated - 6.5 and 7.5e4 at s = 10, 8.0e4 at s = 8.5, 8.9e4 at s = 8, 9.6e4 at s = 7, 7.9, 7.6 and 7.5e4 at s = 4-6, 7.0-7.2e4 at s = 1.5, 7.4e4 at s = 0.2 and 9.7e4 at the last point, with only two dips (6.05e4 at s = 2 and 4.5e4 at s = 3). That is a factor 1.5-1.9 above the plateau sustained across a dozen consecutive points, and it is distinctive: the isolated highs elsewhere on this track (9.1e4 at s = 50, 8.6e4 at s = 25, 8.3e4 at s = 22) are single points sitting among 4.5-5.5e4 neighbours, whereas here the whole last 10 cm is lifted. It never approaches the reference curve (which is at 1.2e5 by s = 1), but the rubric asks for a rise off the tracks own plateau in the shape of the curve rather than a crossing, and this is one - ragged, with the two-times scatter the rubric calls normal. The chain agrees at least this far: its rejection list here is shape_flat alone, without the no_bragg flag it raises on the four flat-profile items in my chunk. Nothing is attached at the stop and nothing lies past it - all three azimuths show a bare end, and the last stretch of the point cloud is drawn in the yellow-orange of higher dQ/dx, matching the profile. All five other drawn objects are on the muon side: 131010 (10 points, 53 cm, cos_fwd -0.99), 130009 (2 points, 52 cm, -0.83) and 129008 (3 points, 49 cm, -0.59) sit around the body about half a metre before the end, and 51003 and 51006 are pdg-11 shower pieces 177-200 cm back at cos_fwd -0.95. None of them is past the stop, which is what the gamma rule requires, so all five are delta / other and the kind is none.

notes: Flat profile to the last point with no visible continuation, no face contact and no dead region at the stop in any of U/V/W - the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Per the rubric that is still THRU and not UNCLEAR. Chain agrees (reject no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0), and the range/MCS disagreement (129.5 MeV vs 981 MeV, amb 0.96) is consistent with a non-stopper.
evidence: 43.4 cm of chain, entering right on the anode face (entry d_face 0.0) and running inward to a fit end 35.3 cm from that same face, 301.6 cm from the cathode, so containment is not the issue here. Upscaled 4x the dQ/dx profile is flat to falling all the way in: the plateau sits at 4-6e4 over s = 17-43 with excursions to 8.5-9e4 around s = 21-28, then the last 6 cm run 7.6e4, 5.5e4, 5.4e4, 4.2e4, 2.9e4, 1.9e4 - a fall, not a rise, and nothing that follows the muon reference curve, which climbs from 6.7e4 at s = 17 to 1.6e5 at s = 0 while the data goes the other way. The segment means say the same thing: 48664 e/cm over 14-42 cm back, 39126 over 0-14 cm, 21211 over the terminal 1.8 cm. A muon at its own Bragg peak cannot do that. I checked the overshoot reading and rejected it: there is no peak several cm before the last point to move the pin to, only plateau then decay, and the 1.8 cm terminal piece 56010 is 4 points at 21211 e/cm with nothing forward of it (flow reports n_stop_arms 1, n_dots 0). The one unassigned piece of any size, 56003, is 11 points over 6.0 cm at 23852 e/cm sitting 10.9-14.3 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, i.e. right on the muon body line despite the chain calling it pdg 11 shower - body activity. 182009 is a 2-point 2.1 cm speck 51 cm out, off the panel entirely. Under the THRU convention every fitted chain segment is muon and everything else is delta / other.

notes: Hardest part of this one was the s = 3-5 cm group at 7.2-8.4e4, which does track the muon curve and is the competing STM_ONLY reading; I went THRU because the terminal three centimetres then fall to 0.76 of MIP with nothing past the end for a fit to have bridged to, so the overshoot/pin-move story has no Michel to explain it, and because this tracks own plateau scatters to 1.1e5 at s = 10 and s = 21 which makes 8.4e4 unremarkable. Flat-enough profile with no visible continuation - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). Note a hatched dead band in U sits immediately beside the top end of the track, which is a possible exit route but not one I can confirm.
evidence: 309 cm of chain, entering 1.2 cm from the anode x face and running clear across the volume to a fit end 33.3 cm from the nearest z wall, 86 cm from the y wall, so it is nominally contained but heading at the z wall. The dQ/dx band is very scattered on this track - the plateau over s = 25-100 cm runs 4.5-6e4 with excursions to 1.1e5 - so I zoomed the last 25 cm at ~7x to read it properly. Reading in from s = 8: 5.3e4, then 6.4-6.5e4 at s = 6-7, then 7.2, 7.4, 7.9, 8.4e4 over s = 5 down to 3, which does sit on the muon reference curve there; but the last three centimetres go the wrong way - 6.1e4, 6.0e4, 5.7e4 at s = 2-1 where the curve demands 9.5e4-1.1e5, and the final two points at s = 0 are 4.2e4, the lowest values anywhere in the terminal 25 cm and below the tracks own MIP plateau. The whole last 5 cm averages about 6.3e4, i.e. 1.15x MIP, where a real stop needs 2-3x and the rubric notes real stoppers here top out at 1.2-1.35e5; the segment means say the same thing, 62942 over the last 24 cm against 55570 over the 264 cm before it, a 13 percent elevation that is far short of a stopping muon. Nothing sits past the fit end at all - flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma, and no object row has a forward cos_fwd. The only unassigned piece, 18007, is 8 points over 4.2 cm at 44343 e/cm sitting 24.2-26.5 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, right on the muon body line at the junction of the two chain segments and typed pdg 11 by the chain: a delta ray on the body, so delta / other. Under the THRU convention the two fitted chain segments are muon and it is the only other row.

notes: Deep fit end (148.7 cm from the nearest face) but the profile falls monotonically to 0.45 of MIP over the last 8 cm with no rise, and the dead-channel pattern at the end in U, V and W is a plausible exit route, so this is a through-goer whose imaging ended at the dead wires. Chain agrees (no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0). The one thing I had to overrule is the chains own capture-gamma tag on 82023: under the THRU rule gamma is undefined without a stop, and a 2-point 0.71 MeV speck 30 cm out would otherwise force michel_kind detached dots and assert decay charge past a stop that is not there.
evidence: 312 cm of chain entering in a corner - 0.5 cm from the z face, 12.7 cm from the y face and essentially on the cathode at x = -3.2 - and running diagonally across the volume to a fit end that is nominally deep: 148.7 cm from the z wall, 196.7 cm from the anode, 222.7 cm from the y wall. The dQ/dx profile kills the stopping reading outright. Zoomed at ~7x the last 8 cm fall monotonically off the tracks own 5.5e4 plateau: about 5.8, 5.2, 4.8, 4.5, 4.3, 3.7, 3.0 and finally 2.5e4 at s = 0, i.e. 0.45 of MIP at the last point, with no elevated region anywhere before it to peak from - s = 8-25 cm sits at 5-6e4, flat on the plateau, while the muon reference curve is already at 6.5e4 by s = 10 and 1.6e5 at s = 0. That is a decline into the fit end, not a Bragg rise, so the overshoot pin-move does not apply either: there is no peak to move the pin back to. The f_meas panels explain the decline: dead channels sit exactly at the fit end in all three planes - two thin dead lines at U ~1065 and ~1072, a wide dead band at V ~4975-4982, and dead lines at W ~9045 and ~9070 - and the track terminates right on them, so the charge is being lost to unresponsive wires and the imaging runs out there rather than the muon stopping. Nothing is attached past the end (flow: n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0). The chains capture-gamma candidate 82023 is 2 points over 0.3 cm carrying 0.71 MeV at 30.2 cm out, and the rest of the near-stop rows are 2-4 point survey specks 35-56 cm out at cos_fwd from -0.93 to +0.99, i.e. scattered in unrelated directions; the larger unassigned pieces (20009, 20012, 20015, 20019, 20021, 20022) all sit at cos_fwd -1.0 on the muon body 53-270 cm back, most of them around the shower at the entry end. Under the THRU convention the seven fitted chain segments are muon and every other row, the capture-gamma candidate included, is delta / other with kind none.

notes: Chain calls this is_stm 0 on shape_flat alone (it does not raise no_bragg), but the profile plainly climbs from 5.3e4 to 1.06e5 over the last 20 cm and the attached 11 cm arm is a textbook Michel topology, which the rubric says is sufficient on its own. The one call I had to weigh is the undershoot: rejected on the charge clause, since the tip averages MIP and falls outward. A block of near-zero fit points at s = 38-43 is the gap between chain segments 30005 and 30011 and is ignored as unmeasured charge.
evidence: 130 cm of chain entering 4.3 cm below the top y face and curving down to a fit end 56.6 cm from the anode, 84.4 cm from the y wall and 69.9 cm from the z wall - properly contained. The profile is a real Bragg: 5.3e4 plateau over s = 60-100 cm, 6-7e4 through s = 20-40, then 8-9.3e4 over the last 8 cm and a terminal chain point at 1.06e5 right at s = 0, tracking the muon reference curve the whole way in (curve 6.2e4 at s = 20, 7e4 at s = 10, 9e4 at s = 3). The segment means agree: 68557 e/cm over the last 39 cm against 53839 over the 42-121 cm stretch. Past the stop a two-piece arm leaves the vertex at a 48 deg kink and runs 11.3 cm: 30003 is 12 points over 6.3 cm at 50335 e/cm and 30001 is 5 more over the next 6.3 cm at 30920, so the arm departs at MIP and its charge falls as it goes out. A muon that just peaked at 1.06e5 cannot carry on at MIP, and 11-12 cm is the right range for the ~24 MeV the chain assigns, so the arm is the Michel. I checked the undershoot explicitly because the arms first two points sit at 1.15e5 and 8.9e4: it does not apply, because the chains own last point is already at the Bragg peak (1.06e5, so the peak is AT the fit end, not past it) and because 30003 averages 50335 e/cm, i.e. 0.93 of this tracks MIP, where the undershoot requires several times MIP over the whole tip. Those two high junction points are vertex charge shared with the muons last centimetre. Four detached 2-point specks sit past the stop with no charge bridging them to it: 119016 at 20.8 cm, 255017 at 27.2 cm and 117014 at 25.8 cm all lie 18-31 deg off the Michel arms own direction (the -x side of the stop), and 118015 at 38.8 cm is still on the forward hemisphere (cos_fwd 0.76) though 53 deg off the arm - all four are on the decay side rather than scattered around the ring, so gamma rather than delta, and none is on the muon body, which runs the other way. The four fitted chain segments are the muon.

181 cm, enters at the anode face, stops 33.8 cm from the y wall. Bragg rise 5e4 -> 9e4 on the muon curve. A 12.8 cm arm at 4.8e4 e/cm leaves the stop sideways (cos_fwd -0.07) -- range and charge of a ~25 MeV Michel. Two isolated dots: 139007 sits 14 cm out, just past the arm's tip and ~15 deg off its axis; 138006 is 50 cm out on the same side, clear of the muon body in the wide view. Both tagged gamma; the 50 cm one is the weakest call in this row.

notes: FRAG because the cluster is the cathode-side half of a much longer cosmic: the context trail is exactly anti-parallel to the chain through the entry point and the entry x is 4.4 cm, i.e. at the cathode. Verdict describes the full object, which is flat-profile and exits the top y face 2.3 cm past the fit end. The 1.0-1.6e4 dip at s = 64-70 is the V-plane dead band, not a physics feature. Past that the profile FALLS into the fit end: 4.3-9.2e4 for 10 cm, then 3.6e4, 2.5e4, 1.5e4, 0.6e4 over 2 cm, then an 8 cm hole with no points, then 1.0-2.5e4 for the last 1.4 cm. What clinches it is 92006, the 8-point 4.4 cm piece the chain offers as a capture gamma: taking its centroid against the entry-to-stop chord it lies at cos 0.966, i.e. 20.8 cm straight ahead of the fit end and only 5.4 cm off the track's own line, carrying 4.7e4 which is MIP - that is charge continuing past the fit end on the track's line, which the rubric makes THRU by itself. I first read the thick-to-thin transition at the 26001/26002 boundary as a muon ending and a Michel leaving, and moved the pin 21.7 cm; that was the amber selection band ending, which display trap 2 warns about, not a change in the object, and the charge argument does not support it either. Verdict revised. On a through-goer there is no stop, so both fitted chain segments are muon and 92006 takes delta / other; the chain's own rejection, shape_flat plus profile_sparse, says the same thing about the fit end.

notes: Flat-profile THRU: no visible continuation, nearest face 21.9 cm from the fit end, no dead-region exit - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Over the last ~3 cm the profile then collapses to 4.4e4, 4.2e4, 3.6e4, 2.4e4, 2.4e4 while the muon curve is at 1.2-1.6e5 there: a sustained collapse over several cm, the overshoot signature, so the true stop is at the junction at s~3 and the last 3 cm of row 69004 is the Michel. The label schema has only one chain row, so 69004 is tagged muon for what most of it is; the row is split, s>3 muon and s<3 michel. Past the stop sit seven compact specks 16.6-27.8 cm out (0.2-2.9 cm, 2-6 points, 1.4-6.1e4) spread over cos_fwd 0.17-0.99 on the forward side, which read as capture gammas. The 621-point 64.6 cm cluster C71 at d_min 25.5 is not a continuation: for a continuation d_max would be near 25.5+64.6=90, but d_max is 45.8, so the cloud lies across the line of flight, and it is far too large for Michel or gamma - a different object, delta/other. Two specks at 22-41 cm (152006, 156007) and the zero-charge pair 163014 go the same way. No dead channels at the stop in U, V or W.

notes: The only soft call is the lone 46.9 cm speck 165012: it decides attached vs both on its own. Taken as gamma on the rubric's faint-far-speck rule because its direction from the stop is essentially the Michel arm's direction (cos 0.99 with 246016), not a random point on the 60 cm ring. Its 1.05e5 e/cm over 2 points is not used as a criterion. No pin move; the terminal ease-off from 9.2e4 to 5.6e4 over 5 cm is neither an undershoot nor an overshoot signature.
evidence: 129.9 cm chain in two fitted rows, enters right on the x face (d_face 0.0) and the fit ends 45.8 cm from the nearest active face, well contained. The profile sits on a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau all the way out to s=100 and climbs from about 7e4 at s=12 onto the muon reference curve, peaking at 9.0-9.2e4 at s=5-6; over the last 5 cm it eases back to 7.3e4, 6.4e4 and 5.6e4 at the fit's last point. That terminal easing ends at about 1.15 of the plateau, nowhere near the far-below-plateau collapse that would say the fit overshot, so the pin stays where the fit put it and I read the ease-off as the last centimetres already sharing charge with the electron that starts 1 cm away. Three michel-group pieces sit at d_min 1.05, 2.12 and 8.77 cm carrying 1.6-3.6e4 e/cm, i.e. at or below MIP - a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so these are the second particle - and the three azimuths show them as one curled hook about 10 cm long leaving the stop and folding back, the textbook Michel shape; all three are michel. One 2-point 0.1 cm speck (165012) sits 46.9 cm out; its direction from the stop is cos 0.99 with the michel piece 246016 and 0.76-0.86 with the other two, so it lies squarely along the Michel arm's own line rather than scattered in an unrelated direction, and there is a clean charge-free gap between it and the stop, which by the attachment tie-break makes it a detached dot: gamma, hence kind both. The V plane has dense dead-channel bands running through this region but U and W show the stop and the hook cleanly and the measured-minus-predicted panels are flat there.

notes: Called THRU on the flat-to-falling last 7 cm, but this is the hardest kind of call: the competing reading is that the s=8-9 maximum is a real Bragg peak and the last 7-8 cm are an overshoot, which would make it STM_ONLY with pin-rr about 8. I rejected that because the rubric's overshoot signature needs the terminal segment to fall FAR BELOW the muon's own plateau, and here it lands at 5.3-6.2e4, i.e. at or slightly above the level the same track carries at s=10-14. Neither undershoot nor overshoot counted. Dead channels cover the track in U and V, so every dQ/dx number on this item is suspect; medium confidence for that reason too.
evidence: A short, lonely, smoothly curved 24.9 cm chain of 42 points and absolutely nothing else drawn - one object row, no arms, no dots, no gamma ring.
