There is no rise at the fit end, which is the operative test, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Two things say the same: the maximum of 8.3e4 is only about 1.5 times the local level and nowhere near the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches, and the far end's 1.1e4 is a fifth of MIP, far too low for muon body charge, so the profile's overall slope is an artefact of the reconstruction rather than a Bragg curve. f_meas shows why: hatched dead-channel bands cover essentially the whole track in V and clip it in U, with only W clean, so the charge on this object is under-measured over its length. Nothing at all lies past the fit end in any of the three azimuths, so there is no decay activity to judge and kind is none.

notes: Chain agrees (is_stm 0, reject no_bragg + shape_flat) but the call is made on the picture: 88 cm of unbroken MIP plateau. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 87.7 cm straight chain in two fitted rows, entering 1.5 cm from the z face and ending 72.1 cm from the nearest active face - deeply contained, and containment is exactly the trap here, because the profile is flat. dQ/dx sits on a 5.0-6.5e4 band from s=88 all the way in to s=3 with no upward trend whatsoever; the scattered 1.0-1.4e5 points are spread over s=13, 19, 33, 40, 57, 67, 72 and 80, i.e. delta activity along the whole body, not a terminal rise. notes: Flat-profile THRU with no visible continuation and no face - exactly the case the rubric says to call THRU rather than UNCLEAR. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.

evidence: 85.6 cm single-row chain entering 0.1 cm from the x face - i.e. right on the anode - and ending 30.3 cm from the nearest z face, with not one other object drawn anywhere in the frame: no arms, no dots, no gamma ring, nothing at the star in any of the three azimuths. notes: Textbook flat-profile THRU 120 cm from any face and with no visible continuation, no face and no dead-region exit - the exact configuration the rubric tells scanners not to hedge into UNCLEAR. All four rows muon, kind none.

notes: The chain calls this an STM (is_stm 1, reject STM) and I am overruling it on the flat profile. Neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 295.8 cm of chain in three fitted rows, 496 points, entering 0.1 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 58.1 cm from the nearest z wall - contained, but the profile decides and the profile never rises. dQ/dx holds a 3.5-6.5e4 band the whole 296 cm; over the last 15 cm the values run 6.0-7.9e4 on the upper branch and 4.0-5.5e4 on the lower, and the fit's own last points are 7.6e4, 6.2e4, 4.5e4, 4.4e4 and 4.0e4. Compared with the far body at s=60-100, where the same two branches sit at 5.5-6.5e4 and 4.5-5.5e4, the last 15 cm are perhaps 10-15 per cent higher - nothing like the factor of two to three the muon reference curve demands, and the curve itself is at 1.6e5 at s=0, three to four times above the data. There is no peak-then-collapse anywhere in the last 40 cm either, so this is not an overshoot with a mislaid pin; it is a flat MIP profile to the last point, which a stopping muon cannot produce, and at 681 MeV range-equivalent that is what one expects. The three azimuths show the star bare with a clean gap in every direction: the nearest drawn objects are the pair 158009/159010 about 19-22 cm out (cos 0.99 with each other, 66 degrees off the body) and the pair 160011/160012 at 29-33 cm sitting about 17 cm off the body line on the backward side, with 157008 a lone 2-point speck 53 cm out. Under the THRU convention all five, plus the two chain-typed pdg 11 showers 62003 and 62007 that lie on the body at cos_fwd -1.00, are delta / other and kind is none.

notes: f_meas is worth recording: the fit end lands at time slice ~0, the very start of the drawn readout window, which is a plausible mechanism for where the rest of the track went, though the rubric does not require one. The competing reading is an overshoot with pin-rr about 3 (peak 8.0e4 at s=3, collapse to 1.95e4 = 0.39 of MIP, inside the quoted 0.15-0.5 band) - rejected because the 8e4 pair is indistinguishable from the delta outliers scattered along the whole body. Counted as neither undershoot nor overshoot.
evidence: 244.6 cm chain in six fitted rows, 414 points, entering 4.8 cm from the y face and ending 39.9 cm from the anode x face - contained on the numbers. The profile is a flat 4.5-5.5e4 MIP band from s=245 in to s=5, decorated all along its length by 8-12.5e4 delta points at s=24, 28, 50-52, 58, 73-75, 80-82 and 88-95, and it never turns up towards the muon reference curve, which sits at 1.6e5 at s=0 while the data end below 6e4. Over the last 5 cm the values are 6.0-6.3e4 at s=5-10, a two-point excursion to 7.5-8.0e4 at s=2-4, and then 5.6e4, 4.2e4, 2.7e4 and 1.95e4 at the fit's own last centimetre. I looked hard at that as a possible overshoot - a peak followed by a collapse to 0.4 of MIP is the right shape - but the peak is two points at 1.6 times the plateau in a track that carries a dozen larger excursions along its body, with no sustained rise leading into it, so there is no Bragg peak for the pin to be moved back to. Flat to the last point means through-goer. The three azimuths back this up completely: the star is bare, and the only large neighbour, C55, is a 350-point 299.6 cm cluster whose d_min 40.9 and d_max 59.9 span just 19 cm - a 300 cm object seen almost edge-on across the line of flight, and the wide 3-D views show it plainly as a second, roughly parallel cosmic track well below this one. The chain-typed pdg 11 shower 75014 sits on the body at 81-84 cm, cos_fwd -1.00. All chain rows muon, the other two delta / other, kind none.

notes: OVERSHOOT: the fit runs about 6 cm past the true stop; pin-rr 6.1 at the 40001/40002 junction. Called medium because the terminal segment sits at 6.5e4, i.e. 1.3 times the 5e4 body plateau, whereas the rubric's overshoot examples run 0.15-0.5 of MIP - it is far below what a post-Bragg muon would carry but NOT below the track's own plateau, which is how the rubric words the test. Competing readings: (a) STM_ONLY with the pin left alone, which I rejected because the profile is falling, not rising, at the fit's last point, so there is no Bragg rise there to justify a stop; (b) THRU, rejected because the factor-two rise over s=6-20 is real and a through-goer cannot produce it. Also note the 1.28-1.30e5 pair at s=7.5-7.8 sits ABOVE the muon reference curve, which the rubric says never happens for real Bragg charge, so I treated those two as delta points and read the trend from the medians instead.
evidence: 328.9 cm chain, 549 points, entering 0.2 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 141.2 cm from the nearest z wall - as contained as it gets. The body plateau is 4.5-5.5e4 out to s=100 and beyond, and from about s=20 the profile lifts off it: median 7e4 at s=15-20, 8.3e4 at s=11-14, and 9.6e4 over s=6-13 (individual points 7.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.25, 8.7, 9.5, 9.6, 9.65, 9.7, 10.3, 12.8, 13.0 e4). That is a genuine ragged Bragg rise of about a factor two over the last 15 cm, and a through-goer cannot make it. Then over the fit's last 6.8 cm the ten points read 3.96, 4.0, 5.42, 5.46, 6.06, 6.4, 6.4, 7.3, 9.36 and 10.78 e4, mean 6.5e4 - a 32 per cent drop from the segment in front of it, at a place where a muon carrying on from a Bragg peak would be at 1.2-1.6e5. Pin moved back to the S78010/S78013 junction at rr 4.8; S78013 tagged michel.  225015, the chain's own 0.3 cm pdg-11 seed, sits 3.9-4.1 cm from the old end and so ~0.7-0.9 cm from the NEW stop -- inside the radius where direction does not discriminate -- so it is michel too, and the kind is both rather than attached because it is drawn as its own piece.  224014 stays gamma: 53 cm out, forward, clear of the body line.

notes: Clean short stopper, pin unmoved. Peak 1.0e5, a little below the usual band, and the upstream end is at 0.4 MIP - both consistent with the drift-parallel topology degrading the dQ/dx scale; the shape of the rise is not in doubt. No overshoot, no undershoot.
evidence: Short isolated 44.3 cm chain, nothing else in the event at all - 303 image points and zero thinned context points - running almost purely along the drift axis, from x -202.8 to -245.3 with z fixed at 287-288 and only 7 cm of y. Both ends stand off the z wall, the entry by 10.2 cm and the stop by 11.2 cm, so neither end is at a face. The profile rises monotonically the whole way in and follows the muon reference curve: 2-3.5e4 at s=35-44, 4-5e4 at s=20-30, 5.5-6.5e4 at s=10-18, 7-8e4 at s=4-8, 8.4-9.2e4 at s=1-3 and 9.7e4-1.02e5 on the last points. That is a factor of four rise into the fit end with no collapse after it, so the pin stays where the fit put it and the chain agrees, accepting it as an STM. The peak tops out at 1.0e5 rather than the 1.2-1.35e5 usual for stoppers here and the far end sits at 0.4 of MIP, which is lower than a 44 cm-range muon should be that early - I read both as a scale effect of the drift-parallel geometry, where the charge lands on one or two wires and the path-length assignment is poor, rather than as evidence against the stop, since the rubric asks for shape off the plateau and not an absolute number and the shape is unambiguous. The three azimuths show a clean single track with the star at one end, the green entry triangle at the other and absolutely nothing past the stop; f_meas shows a near-vertical track in time at fixed channel in U, V and W with the dead bands standing clear of it and no charge beyond the end. The object table has exactly one row, the muon chain itself, and n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no unfitted dot clusters and no capture gamma in the ring, so there is no decay activity to attribute: STM_ONLY with kind none.

notes: THRU on a flat-to-falling profile with no Bragg rise; deeply contained fit end (113 cm from the nearest face) with no visible continuation, which the rubric explicitly allows - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Dead-region confound checked and excluded: V and W are both live at the stop in f_meas. Undershoot signature EXCLUDED - no short high-charge forward tip; the only forward object, 102017, is 20-28 cm out at 0.63 MIP, not a couple of cm at 1e5. Overshoot/pin-move EXCLUDED - no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 242.7 cm chain entering 0.4 cm from the anode x face at z=82 and ending deep inside the volume at z=114, 113 cm from the nearest face and 115 cm from the cathode, so this is a containment-irrelevant case and the profile has to decide it. It decides it flatly: the far body sits around 5.2e4 with the track plateau line drawn at 6.7e4, and over the last 20 cm the points scatter 3.0-7.1e4 with no organised climb - the closest points run 6.05e4, 5.5e4, 5.2e4, 4.6e4, 3.7e4, 3.0e4 at s under 3 cm, and the local plateau reference actually dips to 5.2e4 near the origin, i.e. the profile is if anything falling inward while the muon reference curve is climbing through 8e4 to 1.6e5. Nothing resembling a Bragg rise, ragged or otherwise, and the chain agrees twice over with reject flags no_bragg and shape_flat; the range/MCS split (561 MeV by range against 1488 MeV by MCS, ambiguity 0.75) is the same story from the kinematics side. f_meas shows only the U plane partly dead at the fit end, with V and W both clean there, so the missing Bragg is not a dead-wire artefact - this is the flat-profile through-goer whose cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Past the fit end there is one real object, 102017: 17 points, 9.9 cm, 4.2e4 e/cm, 19.8-28.1 cm out at cos_fwd +0.25, which the three azimuths show sitting well off the muon line and separately oriented rather than collinear with it - a distinct object, and on a through-goer there is no stop to be gamma or michel relative to, so it takes delta / other along with the two small pdg-11 shower pieces on the body at 31-33 and 124-127 cm.

notes: THRU on a profile that bumps to 8.6e4 at s=5-11 cm and then falls back to MIP over the last 4 cm instead of continuing up the muon curve. Competing reading: a ragged Bragg whose tip is lost - rejected because all three planes are live at the stop in f_meas. Pin NOT moved: the terminal fall is to 0.9 of the plateau, not the far-below-plateau sustained collapse the pin rule requires (0.15-0.5 MIP), and there is no Michel past the end for the fit to have bridged to. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing at all past the fit end in any azimuth, so no short high-charge forward tip.
evidence: 341.6 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode x face at y=179, z=198 and ending at (-70, 17, 262), 36 cm from the z wall and 67 cm from the cathode, so containment does not settle it. The profile runs on a 6.0-6.5e4 body with the plateau line at 6.7e4, and the interesting feature is a modest bump at s = 5-11 cm reaching 7.4-8.6e4, which does sit on the muon reference curve where that curve passes 8-8.5e4. But it does not continue: over the last 4 cm the points fall back to 5.7-6.2e4 with a single 7.1e4 at s = 0.5, exactly where the reference curve is climbing through 1.0-1.6e5 and where a real stopper here should be reading 1.2-1.35e5. So the profile turns away from the curve at the steepest part of the Bragg, and the chain flags it twice, no_bragg and shape_flat. I checked the obvious alibi and it is not available: f_meas puts the stop end (time slice 1595) at U 1470, V 5325 and W 9585, all of them between dead bands rather than inside one, so the missing last centimetres of charge are not a dead-wire artefact. All three stop azimuths show a completely bare end - the amber is the particle-flow selection band, not charge - and the flow block confirms n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no gamma in the ring. All eleven unassigned pieces are pdg-11 shower fragments strung along the body at cos_fwd -1.0 between 101 and 205 cm back, i.e. body activity around the two kinks, not stop activity. The hard part is that 8.6e4 bump: read generously it is the start of a ragged Bragg that then loses its last few centimetres, which is why this is medium and not high - but the fall-back to MIP over the final 4 cm with all three planes live is what a through-goer looks like and not what a stopper looks like.

notes: THRU on a flat MIP profile to the last point. No continuation visible and the fit end is 139 cm from every face; per the rubric that is still THRU, the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out. Stop is live in all three planes in f_meas so no dead-region alibi. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing past the fit end at all. Overshoot/pin-move EXCLUDED: no peak and no collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 331 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the anode x face at y=-260, z=200 and ending at (59, -115, 159) - 139 cm from the nearest wall, 56 cm from the cathode, about as deeply contained as a fit end gets, so the picture cannot help and the profile has to decide. notes: THRU on a flat profile that never leaves its own 6.5e4 plateau in the last 15 cm. The two 1.0-1.2e5 singletons near the stop are the only thing that could be read as a Bragg tip; I read them as deltas because they are isolated points with plateau-level neighbours on both sides and the same pattern recurs at s=27, 32, 86 along the body. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing sits past the fit end except a 3-point speck 39 cm out at cos_fwd -0.62, i.e. backward, not a forward high-charge tip. Overshoot EXCLUDED: no peak-then-collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 330 cm chain entering 0.1 cm from the anode x face at (-340, -281, 95) and ending at (-79, -266, 271), 28 cm from the z wall and 76 cm from the cathode, so the end is inside the volume and the profile decides it. Two isolated orange points at 1.17e5 (s=4) and 1.03-1.09e5 (s=8-9) stand well clear of their neighbours and read as deltas on the body, not as a Bragg tip; there are matching orange singletons at s=27, 32 and 86 along the plateau, which is what deltas look like on this plot. So no rise off plateau, and the chain agrees with no_bragg and shape_flat; the range and MCS momenta (860 against 1062 MeV/c, ambiguity 0.53) do not close either. f_meas puts the stop at U 580, V 4440 and W 8435, with the U dead bank ending near 555 and the V bank near 4370, so the last centimetres are measured, not lost - only a thin W line sits close, and one plane cannot erase a Bragg the other two would show. All three azimuths show a bare end with nothing leaving it and the flow block reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma. The four unassigned pdg-11 pieces sit on the body at cos_fwd -1.0 between 114 and 179 cm back, clustered at the two chain kinks, and 72017 is a 3-point 1.0 cm survey speck 39 cm out at cos_fwd -0.62, backward and clear of any stop - all body and ambient activity, delta / other under the THRU rule.

notes: STM_MICHEL. The Bragg is unambiguous; the judgement is whether 56006 is the Michel or a delta. I took Michel on physics: the muon has ~13 MeV KE at the vertex where the arm attaches, whose kinematic delta maximum is a few hundred keV, so a 13.6 cm arm cannot be body activity from that muon, and cos_fwd -0.81 does not reach the -0.85 body-line threshold. The competing reading is STM_ONLY / detached dots with 56006 as delta-other, which the ~5 cm gap between the stop and the arm attachment would support. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing forward of the fit end except a 2-point speck 25 cm out; the terminal high charge is on the chain itself, not in a separate tip. Overshoot EXCLUDED: the profile rises monotonically to the last point with no collapse, so no --pin-rr. Note also that dead bands sit across the stop in all three planes, which may be why the arm reconstructs sparse (13.6 cm carrying only ~7 MeV of visible charge).
evidence: 113.8 cm chain entering 2.2 cm from the anode x face at (338, 80, 145) and ending at (234, 83, 158), 106 cm from the nearest face and 231 cm from the cathode - a deeply contained end. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the body sits at 2-4e4 far out, climbs through 5-6e4 over s = 6-12 cm, reaches 6.8e4 at s = 4-6, then 8.15e4, 8.5e4, 9.4e4, 1.02e5, 1.065e5, 1.07e5 and 1.13e5 at the last point, tracking the muon reference curve the whole way up and topping out squarely in the 1.2-1.35e5 band real stoppers reach here. The chain accepts it as STM with no reject flags. It is worth noting that f_meas shows dead bands straddling the stop in all three planes (U 3415-3435, V 7310-7325, W 11695-11705 and 11720-11730), which can only remove charge, so the measured Bragg is if anything an underestimate. What makes the item interesting is 56006: 21 points, 13.6 cm, 1.35e4 e/cm, d_min 4.7 to d_max 12.5 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.81, which the chain types pdg 11 shower but leaves unassigned (flow says no daughter, n_stop_arms 0). Zooming the c and d azimuths shows it leaving the brown vertex square at the far end of the 6.3 cm terminal Bragg segment and curving away from the muon line, clearly clear of the body rather than hugging it. It cannot be a delta: at that vertex the muon has 6.3 cm of range left, i.e. about 13 MeV of kinetic energy, whose maximum delta is a few hundred keV with a sub-millimetre range, so a 13.6 cm electron-like arm there is physically impossible as body activity. Within the michel rule ten-centimetre radius direction does not discriminate, and the only physical source of a 13 cm electron beside a demonstrated muon stop is the decay, so 56006 is the Michel. Past the stop, 161015 is a 2-point 0.1 cm speck 25.2 cm out at cos_fwd +0.58, isolated, compact and clear of the body, which the chain itself considered as a capture-gamma candidate and rejected only on its energy window: gamma by the plain rule, so the kind is both. What keeps this medium is the roughly 5 cm offset between the stop and the arm attachment point - a Michel should leave the stop itself, and this one leaves the vertex just before it.

notes: THRU on a flat profile whose last two centimetres are zero-charge fit points. Medium because the three-point 12.5e4 bump at s=3.4 is a real competing Bragg reading; I rejected it because identical isolated 1.1-1.3e5 bumps recur at s=41-43, 48, 62, 67-68 and 96 along the same plateau, so it is this track own delta signature. Mechanism named: the fit end is 17.6 cm from the cathode with the track heading into it, i.e. maximum drift and worst S/N, which is where a cluster fades out; f_meas rules out a dead-wire exit. Undershoot EXCLUDED: the only thing past the fit end is a 1.1 cm 3-point speck at 3.2e4 across an 8.5 cm gap, not a 2 cm tip at 1e5. Pin NOT moved: the collapse is only ~2 cm of near-zero fit points, which the rubric tells me to ignore rather than to bridge from, and there is nothing at the fit end for the fit to have bridged to.
evidence: 383 cm chain entering 8.9 cm from the anode x face at (-331, 230, 192) and ending at (-21, 102, 57), 56 cm from the z wall but only 17.6 cm from the cathode - and it is travelling toward the cathode, x running -331 to -21, so the fit end sits at maximum drift where the imaging signal-to-noise is worst. The profile is flat: the body holds 5.5-6.5e4 the whole way and s = 4 to 20 cm is indistinguishable from s = 40 to 100. Reading the last centimetres off a 10x crop gives 6.0e4 at s=4.3, 8.5e4 at s=4.1, 12.5e4 at s=3.4, 7.4e4 at s=2.7, 3.4e4 at s=2.05, then 1.9e4, 0.9e4 and 0.1e4 at s below 1.3. The last three are effectively zero-charge fit points and the rubric says to ignore them, and once they go the only feature left is a three-point bump centred at s=3.4. I do not read that bump as a Bragg tip, because this track carries exactly that pattern all along its body: isolated 1.07-1.31e5 clusters sit at s = 41-43, 48, 62, 67-68 and 96 on the same plateau, so a 1.25e5 excursion at s=3.4 is the same delta signature landing near the end. A real Bragg has to be a rise following the reference curve over the last 10-20 cm, and over that stretch this profile does not move off 6e4 while the curve climbs from 6.6e4 to 1.6e5. The chain agrees with no_bragg and shape_flat, and the kinematics do not close either - 884 MeV by range against 1713 by MCS, ambiguity 0.57, i.e. the track is straighter than a stopper of that range. f_meas shows the stop end live in all three planes (U 1130, V 4910, W 8895) with the dead banks 30-150 channels away, so the fade is not a dead-wire effect - it is the cluster running out of signal 17.6 cm short of the cathode. All three azimuths show a bare end. The chain does offer a Michel: 115010, 3 points, 1.1 cm, 3.2e4 e/cm, 2.7 MeV, sitting 8.5-9.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.19 - but it says itself that it bridged that across 8.54 cm of empty space by proximity rather than by a graph edge, and a 1.1 cm three-point speck across a 9 cm charge-free gap is the rubric own example of a detached dot, not a 35 MeV electron. With no stop it cannot be gamma either, so it and the two survey specks 52-58 cm out take delta / other under the THRU rule.

notes: OVERSHOOT (the pin-move case), pin moved back to rr 5.9 cm. Peak 1.36e5 at s=9, collapse to 0.7-1.9e4 (0.12-0.32 MIP) sustained over the last 6 cm, then a diffuse EM cloud the fit bridged to. The pin position carries about 3 cm of uncertainty because the profile declines from the peak at s=9 to plateau at s=6.1 before collapsing, so the true stop could be argued anywhere in 6-9 cm; I put it at the collapse boundary. Row split recorded: 4008 spans 2.59-200 cm and its innermost ~3 cm lie on the Michel side of the moved pin, but the tag alphabet cannot split a row so it stays muon. Undershoot EXCLUDED: this is the opposite failure. Competing reading is THRU, supported by the range/MCS split (487 against 1128 MeV, ambiguity 0.81) and the chain rejects shape_flat + profile_sparse - which is why this is medium.
evidence: 209 cm chain entering 0.8 cm from the z face at (-96, -319, 2) and ending at (-208, -177, 93), 92 cm from the nearest wall and 205 cm from the cathode, so the end is well inside the volume. This is the overshoot case in its textbook form. The body runs at 5.5-6.5e4; measured off a 9x crop the profile climbs from 5.7e4 at s=15 through 6.8e4 at s=11.4 and 8.3e4 at s=10.3 to a peak of 1.28-1.36e5 at s=8.5-9.8, falls back through 9.8e4 at s=7.3, 7.5e4 at s=6.8 and 5.6e4 at s=6.1, and then COLLAPSES: every point below s=5.6 sits between 0.67e4 and 1.91e4, i.e. 0.12-0.32 of the plateau, over the last six centimetres. That is the peak-several-cm-before-the-fit-end-then-collapse signature, and it is sustained over 6 cm rather than being one low last point. The zoomed c azimuth shows the same thing in colour: the turbo track runs green, then orange, then RED at the peak, then a couple of plateau points, then blue, and then a diffuse pink and yellow cloud of flow segments spreading out to the star - the fit bridged the muon own stop to that cloud. f_meas puts the stop end at U 215, V 4045 and W 7795, all live with the dead banks 50-150 channels away, and its measured-minus-predicted panels show a real brown residual blob at time slices 550-580, i.e. measured charge at the end that the muon fit does not account for. So I moved the pin to rr 5.9 cm, the junction between the last real muon charge (5.6e4 at s=6.1) and the collapsed stretch. The collapse falls inside chain segment 4008, which has no separate row for its last 3 cm, so 4008 keeps the muon tag for what most of its 206 cm is and the split is recorded here. Past the moved stop, 4011 (6 points, 2.8 cm, 1.03e4 e/cm, the collapsed terminal chain segment) and the two unassigned pdg-11 shower pieces 4009 (15 points, 8.5 cm, 1.34e4) and 4010 (15 points, 8.6 cm, 2.2e4) all lie inside the bridged 0-6.8 cm stretch and together form that diffuse sub-MIP cloud: they are the Michel, and their cos_fwd of -0.93 to -0.95 is measured from the fit last point rather than from the true stop, so it does not read as body activity once the stop moves. 4006, a 6.1 cm pdg-11 shower fragment 200-203 cm back at the entry end, is body activity: delta / other. No gamma anywhere in the ring, so the kind is attached.

notes: THRU, and the clearest one in my chunk - the profile is flat on its own 5.2e4 plateau to the last point with no rise of any kind, on a fit end 90 cm from the nearest face and 89 cm from the cathode. No visible continuation; per the rubric that is still THRU and I say so rather than reaching for UNCLEAR. Dead-region exit EXCLUDED by f_meas in all three planes. Undershoot EXCLUDED: nothing forward of the fit end at all, only a 2-point speck 15.8 cm out at cos_fwd -0.55. Overshoot EXCLUDED: no peak and no collapse, so no --pin-rr.
evidence: 252.8 cm chain entering 0.6 cm from the z face at (314, 32, 1) and ending at (92, 33, 91), 90 cm from the z wall and 89 cm from the cathode, so the end is comfortably inside the volume and the profile has to decide it. Meanwhile the muon reference curve climbs from 5.5e4 at s = 40 through 6.6e4 at s = 13 to 1.6e5 at the origin, and the data never follow it up by so much as one point: there is not even a ragged rise to argue about, and the highest points anywhere near the stop (8.4e4 at s = 11, 8.55e4 at s = 17) are the same isolated excursions this track shows at s = 36, 38, 40 and 48.
