notes: No undershoot candidate: the only non-chain row is 23.5 cm away at the entry end, and no row sits at dstop 1-3 cm forward at ~1e5. No overshoot: the peak is at the last point, not several cm before it. Pin left at the fit's last point.
evidence: Short 23.9 cm single-segment chain, 84.4 MeV by range, entering 0.6 cm from the z face and ending 13.9 cm from the nearest (y) face, in_fv 1, so it stops inside the volume. Upscaled 6x on the terminal region the profile is unambiguous: a flat ~4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s = 24 in to s = 3, then three points at 1.06-1.09e5 over the last ~1.5 cm sitting exactly on the muon reference curve where it turns up, i.e. a factor 2.1 rise off the track's own plateau with the right shape. One green point at 6.9e4 sits at s = 0 itself; that is the ordinary single partial-charge last point the rubric tells you to leave alone, not a sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit's last point. Two mid-track points at 7.5e4 and 9.8e4 near s = 8-10 are scatter above the plateau and do not change the shape. Past the stop there is nothing at all: the flow reports n_stop_arms 0 and n_dots 0, and all three azimuths show clean white space beyond the star with no speck, arm or bridged piece. The only other drawn object is 237001, a 4-point 1.5 cm speck at 23.5-24.8 cm from the stop, i.e. down at the entry end, at cos_fwd -0.93 on the muon body line and carrying only 8372 e/cm, so it is body activity beside the entry, delta / other. f_meas shows the track solidly imaged in all three planes with dead bands 18 wires away in V and about 10 wires beyond the end in W but U and V clean past the end, so it is not a track leaving through a dead region. Nothing that reads as an electron anywhere, so STM_ONLY with kind none; the chain's shape_flat rejection is the disagreement, and I think it is wrong because the rise is only 1.5 cm long on a 24 cm track and a flatness statistic over the whole segment will wash it out.

58 cm, enters 1.1 cm from the z face, stops 15.7 cm inside. Bragg to 1.25e5 at the last point on the muon curve. An 8.4 cm two-piece arm leaves the stop forward (cos_fwd 0.20/0.25) with profile charge to -8 cm; its 1.8e4 e/cm is low for an electron, which is why this is medium and not high. 246011 sits 56 cm out at 1.1e4 e/cm (0.2 MIP) -- too far and too faint to attribute -- but see below.  [REVISED at the end of the pass: 246011 is tagged **gamma**, not delta / other. The rule settled on charge NOT being a criterion -- any isolated object past the stop and clear of the muon body line is a gamma, however faint. The reasoning above is left as written so the change is visible.]

notes: Flat-to-declining profile THRU at 109.9 cm from every face with no continuation drawn. The verdict itself is not in doubt - the rubric's operative test is the profile and the profile falls into the fit end - but the mechanism is unaccounted for: no face, no dead-region exit in U, and no charge past the star, so where the muon went is not visible in these frames. That is the rubric's stated 'the cluster simply ended where the imaging ran out' case, not a reason to weaken the call. No undershoot: no row carries dstop of a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 with chain pdg 11; the only forward-ish rows are C15 and 93014 at 39-50 cm and 41-43 cm off-axis. No overshoot: no terminal peak to collapse from, so the pin stays put.
evidence: 139.7 cm chain in five fitted segments, entering 0.6 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 109.9 cm from the nearest face, so this is a deeply contained fit end and containment cannot decide it. The profile is the operative test and it says through-goer: the plateau sits at 5.0-6.0e4 for the whole 140 cm, and over the last 4 cm the points fall to 4.0e4, 3.6e4, 3.5e4, 2.9e4 and 2.3e4 with two near-zero fit points mixed in, i.e. the charge goes down into the fit end rather than up, and it never approaches the muon reference curve which is at 9e4 to 1.6e5 over that same span. The five chain segments carry medians 54318, 57303, 55145, 58213 and 41951 from the stop backwards - the terminal segment is indistinguishable from the rest, so there is no rise anywhere near the end. I checked for the overshoot and it is not there: a peak-then-collapse needs a peak several cm before the last point, and the only high points (1.25e5 at s = 15, and others at s = 57, 80, 85, 95) are isolated delta spikes scattered along the whole track, not a terminal maximum. All three azimuths show clean white space past the star with no arm, speck or bridged piece, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. f_meas shows the track cleanly imaged in all three planes; the U projection is near vertical at channel ~1750 with the nearest dead band 50-78 channels away, so a continuation would have been seen in U and this is not a dead-region exit. The large object C15 (298 pts, 62.9 cm, no PR segment) and the speck 93014 sit 41-43 cm off the muon line at 44-50 cm and are visibly a separate diffuse streak in every azimuth, so they belong to a different object; 20009 and 20012 are pdg-11 shower pieces at cos_fwd -1.0 sitting 3.0-3.4 cm off the body at 59 and 126 cm back, i.e. deltas on the body. Deep containment with no visible continuation is the uncomfortable part, but the rubric is explicit that a flat profile to the last point is enough on its own.

notes: THRU on the flat profile alone; the U+V dead bands immediately past the fit end give it a mechanism as well, so this is not the rubric's "ended where the imaging ran out" case but an ordinary dead-region exit. No undershoot and no overshoot: the muon chain is the only drawn object, so there is no forward piece to mistake for a Michel, and the profile has no terminal peak.
evidence: 69.9 cm single-object chain, 187.3 MeV by range, entering 0.5 cm from the y face and ending 30.9 cm from that same nearest face; it is the only object drawn, so there is nothing to attribute except the muon itself. The profile is flat to the last point: a 4.3-5.5e4 plateau all the way in, with the final points at 5.2e4, 5.1e4, 5.3e4 and a single 7.05e4 at s = 0, against a muon reference curve that is at 8e4 by s = 5 and 1.6e5 at s = 0 - the data never approaches it and never turns up. The only excursions are a bump of 7.4-9.9e4 at s = 6-11 and two isolated spikes at 1.32e5 and 1.49e5 at s = 49, all of them delta-ray scatter well away from the end, and the segment median is 51766 for the whole 70 cm. So there is no Bragg rise, no terminal peak to collapse from, and no reason to move the pin. All three azimuths show a single clean isolated track with nothing whatsoever past the star - no arm, no dot, no second object anywhere in the frame - and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, so STM_MICHEL is not on the table either. f_meas adds the mechanism: the fit end sits at U channel 3710, V 7548, W 12108, and the track's own direction carries it to lower channel in U and V, where U has a dead line at ~3705 and V's end is already inside a hatched dead band at 7540-7558; only W is clean there, and one live plane cannot make 3-D points, so a continuation past the end would simply not be imaged. MCS 604.8 MeV against 187.3 MeV by range (amb 0.82) points the same way - the track is far stiffer than a muon with 70 cm left to live. Through-goer leaving through a two-plane dead region.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is high-confidence; the medium is about detached dots vs none. The three pieces at 41-56 cm are at the outer edge of the gamma rule's ~60 cm and the chain never offered them to either stage (survey only), so if the owner reads them as belonging to a different object the kind flips to none. No undershoot: no row at dstop 1-3 cm forward at ~1e5. No overshoot: the peak is the last point, pin left alone.
evidence: 391.4 cm chain in six fitted segments, 903 MeV by range with MCS 821.7 MeV at amb 0.00, entering 0.5 cm from the x face and ending 97.8 cm from the nearest face - deeply contained. The Bragg is the best I have seen in this chunk: the data tracks the muon reference curve point for point from the plateau inwards, 5.2e4 out at s = 40-90, 6.5e4 at s = 12-20, 7.0-7.5e4 at s = 6-11, 8.5-8.7e4 at s = 2-5, 1.10e5 at s = 1.5 and a final point at 1.475e5 at s = 0, which is the 1.2-1.35e5 top-out band and above. The chain agrees, is_stm 1. No pin move: the peak is the last point, there is no collapse behind it, and the only high outliers (1.0-1.17e5 at s = 24, 53-56, 70) are delta spikes far from the end. Nothing is attached at the stop - all three azimuths show the star capping a clean track end with no arm and no bridged piece, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - so this is not STM_MICHEL. Past the stop there are three detached pieces, 144024 (7 pts, 3.7 cm, 72372) at 40.9 cm, 145025 (2 pts, 0.1 cm, 56106) at 43.1 cm and 146026 (10 pts, 5.1 cm, 61303) at 56.4 cm, all at cos_fwd +0.17 to +0.41, i.e. on the forward side of the stop and not back along the body, and all visibly clear of the track in every azimuth. They are not one object: 145025 sits 9.6 cm from 144024 in the same direction from the stop (cos 0.98) but 146026 is about 45 deg away and its offset from 144024 is nearly perpendicular to the 144024-145025 axis, so they are three separate compact deposits rather than a broken second track. Isolated, past the stop, clear of the body and inside 60 cm is the gamma rule, and they are not scattered in unrelated directions around the ring, so I tagged all three gamma and the kind is detached dots - which by the rubric does not promote the verdict. The chord-based transverse offsets I computed (40-55 cm) are unreliable here because the track makes almost a right-angle bend near the end, so I judged the separation from the three azimuths instead, as trap 5 requires. f_meas shows dead bands close to the fit end in U (3040 against the end at 3070) and V (6815-6825 against the end at 6825), which would matter for a flat profile, but a track exiting through a dead region does not first climb to 1.475e5.

notes: FRAG_THRU rather than plain THRU because the drawn cluster is visibly broken - a 25 cm piece, 22 cm of nothing, then the two-point blob the pin sits on - and the main piece is clipped at time slice 0, the readout-window edge, so more of the object exists outside what is drawn. MESSY was the other reading I weighed and rejected: there is a coherent straight spine, it is just short and under-charged, not an EM blob in many pieces. Marked medium because with 41 image points and a heavily dead U plane there is very little to go on, and because FRAG versus plain THRU turns on reading time slice 0 as a truncation. Deliberately did not tag 135001 gamma even though the chain names it one - the rubric forbids gamma on a THRU. No undershoot and no overshoot: there is no terminal peak and no forward high-charge tip, only a bridged gap.
evidence: This is a broken, boundary-clipped cluster rather than a track with a stop. The chain is quoted as 41.0 cm over 30 points but the whole event has only 41 image points at full density, and the 3-D frames show why: there is a single coherent amber piece about 25 cm long, then roughly 22 cm of completely empty space, then an isolated two-point blob which is where the pin sits. The dQ/dx panel shows the same hole - chain points at s = 25-41 and at s = 0-2 and nothing at all between s = 3 and s = 24 - so the fit bridged two disconnected pieces and its last point is essentially fictitious. Both ends hug the same wall: the entry is 1.3 cm from the y face and the fit end 0.8 cm from it, in_fv 0, so the object runs along the top y boundary about a centimetre inside it for its whole visible length. There is no Bragg anywhere: the five points at s = 0-2 carry 1.5-2.9e4, the main piece is mostly 0.4-1.5e4 with a handful up to 7.8e4, and the segment value is 13916, about 0.28 of MIP - far under the plateau, let alone the reference curve which is at 1.6e5 at s = 0. f_meas explains the missing charge: the U plane is heavily hatched with dead bands right across this channel range, and the main piece runs down into time slice 0, the edge of the readout window, so the object is cut there rather than ending there. That is what makes me call it a fragment: the drawn cluster is one broken piece of something that continues out of the imaged window, and whatever the full object is, it is not a stopping muon - no rise, no plateau even, and both ends on the boundary. The only other row is 135001, two points at 0.2 cm and 22177 which the chain offers as a capture gamma 29.3 cm out at cos_fwd +0.67; on a THRU-family item gamma is not available because it would assert decay charge past a stop that does not exist, so it is delta / other.

notes: Flat-profile THRU with a deeply contained fit end (68 cm), no continuation drawn and no dead band immediately past the end. No undershoot: no row carries dstop of a couple of cm at 0.9-1.2e5 with chain pdg 11 - the nearest object of any kind is 38 cm away and 38 cm off-axis. No overshoot: no terminal peak. Note that the five perpendicular survey specks at 38-60 cm are exactly the population I called gamma on 039349_7/65 and 039349_70/56; here the THRU verdict forecloses that tag, which is the rubric working as intended but does mean the same physical configuration gets different tags depending on the verdict.
evidence: 264.8 cm chain in three fitted segments, 610.9 MeV by range, entering 0.2 cm from the x (anode) face and ending 68.0 cm from the nearest face, so the fit end is well inside and containment cannot decide it. The profile is flat to the last point: the plateau sits at 5.0-6.0e4 for the whole 265 cm and the last few centimetres carry 5.5-6.3e4, which is a couple of thousand electrons above the plateau and nowhere near the muon reference curve, which is at 8e4 by s = 5 and 1.6e5 at s = 0. The terminal segment's own value is 55776 against 56006 and 40744 for the two behind it, so the end is indistinguishable from the body. A small group of 6.6-7.2e4 points sits at s = 11-16 and single spikes of 1.16e5 and 9.2e4 at s = 24-26 and 9.9e4 at s = 94, but those are delta scatter mid-track, not a terminal maximum, so there is no peak for a collapse to follow and the pin stays at the fit's last point. All three azimuths show the star capping a clean, straight, continuous track with nothing attached and nothing drawn past it, and the flow reports n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The five remaining rows are all survey-only pieces the chain never offered to either stage, sitting 38-60 cm out with transverse offsets of 38-57 cm, i.e. essentially perpendicular to the muon and scattered in several different directions in the azimuths rather than collimated on one side; the largest, 137009, is 23 points over 13.2 cm at 50442 e/cm, which is a small track segment of its own rather than a compact dot. On a through-goer none of them can be gamma anyway - gamma and michel are defined relative to a stop - so they are all delta / other. f_meas shows the fit end 20-22 channels clear of the nearest dead bands in U and V, so this is not a dead-region exit either; the cluster simply ends where the imaging ran out, which the rubric says is still THRU.

notes: The hard call is 43003: 7.2 cm and chain-typed pdg 11 is Michel-scale, but it is 1.3 cm off the muon line, backward, and at 0.2 of MIP, so both the hugging-the-body clause and the close-backward-body-excluded clause send it to delta / other. If that piece is really the Michel the item becomes STM_MICHEL / both, which is why the confidence is medium.
evidence: 101 cm of chain, enters 2.7 cm from the anode x face and stops 55.2 cm from the nearest wall (z), so containment is not in question. The profile sits on a 5.5e4 plateau from s=100 in to about s=20, then climbs steadily through 7e4-9e4 over the last 15 cm and finishes at 1.22e5 and 1.63e5 on the final two points, tracking the shape of the muon reference curve; the rise is ragged with several 6e4 points mixed in but it is a genuine rise off the plateau and there is no terminal collapse, so the pin stays on the fit last point. The one piece at the stop, segment 43003, is 13 points over 7.2 cm at only 1.18e4 e/cm, sitting 1.9-4.4 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.95; projecting its centroid onto the entry-to-stop line puts it 1.3 cm off that line and 2.7 cm back along it, and all three azimuths show it as a small blob lying alongside the amber last-segment band rather than an arm leaving the stop, so it is hugging the muon body and goes delta / other even though the chain types it pdg 11 shower, which is also what the chain itself did by reporting n_stop_arms 0. Past the stop there is one isolated 4-point 1.7 cm speck, 149007, at 25.2 cm and 25 cm clear of the body line with cos_fwd 0.25, drawn with a clean charge-free gap to the track end in all three measured planes: a detached capture gamma, which does not promote the item. The 2-point survey speck 148006 at 47.8 cm projects 35 cm back along the muon axis, so it is behind the stop rather than past it and is delta / other. No dead channels touch the stop in U, V or W.

notes: Low confidence and the owner should look at this one. Three readings are live. (1) THRU as recorded: no Bragg rise at the fit end, and the rubric says a flat or non-rising profile is enough on its own even with no visible continuation and no face. (2) MESSY: plateau at 0.4 of MIP, six pdg 11 shower segments interleaved along the body, a four-way fan at the fit end, 26 drawn objects in a 60 cm box, and chain KE of 236 MeV by range against 114 by dQ/dx and 123 by MCS with amb 0.66 all say this is not one muon; I did not use MESSY only because a coherent spine is visible end to end in all three azimuths, which the MESSY definition excludes. (3) STM_ONLY with an overshooting fit, pin near rr 2.5, reading the three points at s = 2-3 as a real Bragg peak that the fit then bridges for its last 2 cm; I rejected it because the points immediately before the spike (s = 3-5) are also low, so there is no rise leading into the peak, and the same spike height recurs three times near the entry. Dead-channel bands crossing the track in U and V mean the profile itself is partly untrustworthy, which is the main reason I did not go higher than low.
evidence: 93 cm of chain over a 61 cm chord, entering 3.5 cm from the z face and ending 42.9 cm from the nearest wall, so the fit end is nowhere near a face. The profile never establishes a MIP plateau: after ignoring four multi-centimetre runs sitting at 3e3-6e3 (s = 20-30, 41-47, 58-63, 80-84, which line up with grey dead-channel bands crossing the track at U 3040 and V 6890 in f_meas) the surviving points oscillate between 1.2e4 and 5e4, i.e. around half of the 5.5e4 that a clean muon plateau reads on comparable items, which is also the chain own rejection, plateau_off_mip. Over the last 20 cm there is no climb: s = 20 to 5 wanders 5.2e4, 2.5e4, 4.0e4, 1.6e4, 1.9e4, and the final two centimetres sit at 2.4-2.9e4, no higher than the body. The only elevated points anywhere near the end are three at s = 2-3 (8.0e4, 8.2e4, 1.06e5) with low points on both sides of them, so they read as a spike rather than a Bragg peak, and identical spikes to 1.05e5, 1.01e5 and 9.6e4 occur at s = 65-92 near the entry end where the charge is highest. Charge highest at the entry and lowest at the fit end is the wrong way round for a stopper. The stop itself sits at the tip of a short segment past a vertex from which three further segments fan out in the c, d and e azimuths, and six of the fitted segments along the body are typed pdg 11 shower; twelve of the eighteen unassigned rows are 2-4 point survey specks scattered 7-56 cm off the body line in unrelated directions, including the four-point 178031 that the chain offers as a capture gamma 21.9 cm past the stop. With no rise at the fit end the object is a through-goer or is not a single muon at all, and either way there is no stop to hang a michel or gamma on, so every non-chain row is delta / other.
Michel is aligned with muon track, still a bit segment after dQ/dx

notes: THRU off a flat-core profile to the last point, no continuation drawn, 113.5 cm from any face and no dead region at the stop; per the rubric the flat profile alone settles it and the cluster simply ran out of imaged charge. No pin move - there is no peak to collapse from.
evidence: 447 cm chain, enters 0.5 cm from the x anode face and the fit ends 113.5 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. The dQ/dx profile is flat on a 5.0-6.5e4 core from s=100 right down to the last point, with the usual factor-of-two scatter and a handful of isolated high points (1.14e5 and 1.09e5 at s=10, 1.26e5 and 1.20e5 at s=44, 9.7e4 and 9.3e4 at s=54) spread all along the track rather than bunched at the end, plus a mid-track dip to 1.4-3.0e4 around s=86. Over the last 10-20 cm the core does not move at all: it sits at 5-6.7e4 with the single point at s=0 at 8.3e4, against a muon reference curve that asymptotes at 5.4e4 and climbs to 1.6e5 at the origin. A stopping muon core would have to reach 1.2-1.35e5 over that stretch, so there is no Bragg rise and no peak-then-collapse either. All three 3-D azimuths show one clean straight spine terminating at the star with nothing attached and nothing past it; the flow block agrees, reporting n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. The two non-chain rows are both back on the muon body and neither is at the end: 109020 is a 0.4 cm two-point survey speck 53.8 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, sitting on the body line in the d azimuth and offered to neither stage, and 19017 is a 1.8 cm four-point piece the chain calls pdg 11 shower but which lies 319 cm back up the track at cos_fwd -1.00, so both are delta / other. The measured panels show the track ending cleanly at the pin with the nearest dead-channel bands roughly 60-110 channels away in U and V and about 45 away in W, so there is no dead-region exit at the stop.

notes: Cleanest Bragg in my chunk; chain also calls it STM. STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL purely because there is no drawn object past the stop at all - not a faint one, none.
evidence: 119 cm single-segment chain, enters 3.1 cm from the z face and the fit ends 42.3 cm from the nearest wall, so it is comfortably inside the volume. The dQ/dx profile is the textbook stopper: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau out at s=60-100, a slow lift through the 6-8e4 band over s=15-30, then a clean climb that hugs the shape of the muon reference curve from s=15 inwards and finishes at 1.02e5 at s=1.5, 1.39e5 at s=0.7 and 1.52e5 at s=0.3. The rise is smooth rather than ragged and the last three points sit right on the muon curve, which is as good as this sample gets, so there is no question about the Bragg. Nothing at all sits past the end: the object table has a single row, the fitted chain segment itself, and the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. All three 3-D azimuths show the amber flow band running out at the star with no arm, no dot and no off-axis speck anywhere near it; I read the amber only as the selection band per the colour warning, not as charge. There is no terminal collapse either - the profile is still rising at the final point - so the pin stays on the fit last point and neither fit-failure mode applies. The measured panels show the amber band terminating at time slice about 1515 in all three planes with only two or three near-zero-charge tip points beyond it and the nearest dead-channel bands 60-100 channels away in U, 50 away in V and 60 away in W, so the muon did not leave through a dead region.

notes: THRU off a flat-to-declining MIP profile at the fit end. The bright 1.0-1.5e5 clump on the panel is at s=22-26, back up the body, not at the stop - reading it as a Bragg peak would be the trap here. Dead-channel bands sit within about 15 V channels of the stop, so a dead-region exit is plausible but not needed for the verdict. No pin move.
evidence: 323 cm chain, enters 0.4 cm from the x anode face and the fit ends 62.7 cm from the nearest z wall. The dQ/dx core is a flat 4.0-5.0e4 band from s=100 all the way in, and over the last 10-20 cm it does not lift at all - if anything it sags, the final five points reading 4.5e4, 4.1e4, 3.9e4, 3.0e4 and 2.9e4 against a muon reference curve that asymptotes at 5.4e4 and would have to be climbing through 1.2e5 by now. The one dramatic feature on the plot, a seven-point clump running 9.5e4 to 1.48e5, sits at s=22-26, twenty-odd centimetres back up the body, so it is a delta or a hard knock-on and not a terminal rise; a second clump of the same height sits at s=95-100. That is a MIP plateau carried to the last point, which a stopping muon cannot do, so this is a through-goer whose cluster ran out. The two survey specks are the only things anywhere near the end and they are not near it: 183010 is a 0.5 cm two-point speck 58.3 cm out and 184011 an 11-point 6.1 cm piece 60.1 cm out, both at cos_fwd around -0.3, and the c and d azimuths show them as a small detached group well off the muon line and well beyond any decay radius - on a through-goer there is no stop for a gamma tag to refer to, so both are delta / other, as are 51008 and 51009 (a two-point pdg 211 and a seven-point pdg 11 shower) which sit 309 cm back at the far entry end. The flow block agrees that there is nothing at the stop: no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. In the measured panels the track runs off the top of the window at the pin with dead-channel bands about 15 channels either side of it in V, which is a plausible continuation route, while U and W are clean for 60+ channels.

notes: Hardest call in my chunk. No Bragg rise at the fit end - the charge is far below its own plateau there - so THRU by the operative test, but the terminal decay to about 1e4 over 12 cm is not what a clean through-goer looks like either, hence medium. Competing reading was pin_rr about 12 with 54001 as an attached Michel; rejected because the s=12-14 maximum is only 8e4, within this track own plateau scatter, and because the lowest points sit inside the body segment rather than at the 5.6 cm segment junction. No pin move recorded.
evidence: 90.7 cm chain running almost parallel to the cathode - x moves only from 310.2 to 306.2 against a cathode plane at 303.2 - entering 0.9 cm from the y face and ending 33.7 cm from the anode face, so it is contained. Reading the panel off the gridlines, the plateau from s=20 out to s=100 is a 4-6e4 core, there is a local maximum of 7.3-8.0e4 at s=12-14, and then the charge falls away over the last 12 cm: 4.3e4 at s=8.6, then 2.59e4, 1.42e4, 0.80e4, 1.69e4, 2.81e4 through s=8 to s=5, then 3.9e4 near s=4 and down through 3.08e4, 2.46e4, 1.69e4, 1.04e4 to a final near-zero fit point at s=0.1. I weighed moving the pin back to the s=12-14 maximum and calling this an overshoot with the terminal stretch as a Michel, and rejected it. The maximum is only 1.5x the plateau, and 8e4 is a value this same track reaches in ordinary scatter out at s=80, whereas the rubric anchor is that real stoppers here top out at 1.2-1.35e5; the collapse rule relaxes how deep the collapse must be, not the requirement that there be a Bragg peak to collapse from. The segment geometry argues the same way: the low stretch runs s=0 to about 9 and straddles the 54001/54002 boundary at s=5.6, and the two lowest points of all (0.80e4 at s=6.5 and 1.42e4 at s=7.4) fall inside the body segment 54002 rather than in the terminal piece, so the discontinuity is not at a junction. The honest competing reading is that 54001 is a 5.6 cm terminal segment at 0.59 of the body dQ/dx that kinks off the body and hooks - its arc length is 5.6 cm but its far point is only 2.58 cm from the stop in 3-D - which is the right shape for a short attached Michel; what beats it is that no Bragg peak precedes it. The W and V measured panels show real if weak charge continuing right up to the stop marker, dark purple at the end, so the fit is not running into empty space either; the nearest dead channels are about 30 W channels and 85 V channels away. The only other drawn object, 193003, is a two-point 0.4 cm speck 34.3 cm back at cos_fwd -0.81, on the body line, so delta / other.

267 cm, enters 0.1 cm from the z face, stops 54.2 cm inside. Bragg to 1.25e5 on the muon curve, MCS amb 0.00. A 13.3 cm arm at 3.5e4 e/cm leaves the stop sideways with profile charge to -12 cm; the 0.3 cm piece 7.6 cm out lies inside that arm's own extent, so it is the same object rather than a separate dot.

notes: THRU off a flat profile to the last point. Worth flagging that BOTH ends are deep inside - 127.5 cm from a face at the far end, 113.5 cm at the fit end - so the drawn cluster is almost certainly a piece of a longer track; I did not use a FRAG verdict because no larger object is visibly drawn that this is part of (C35 crosses at a different angle and is not a continuation), and the rubric explicitly allows a plain THRU with no visible continuation. No pin move.
evidence: 121.6 cm chain floating in the middle of the volume: the far end is 127.5 cm from the nearest z face and the fit end is 113.5 cm from the anode, so neither end touches anything. The dQ/dx core is a flat 4-8e4 band over the whole 100 cm the panel shows, and at the fit end it does not rise - the last five points read 5.2e4, 3.8e4, 3.7e4, 3.0e4 and 2.8e4, i.e. slightly below the track own core, against a muon reference that would have to be climbing through 1.2e5. The only excursions are isolated high points at s=10-14 (1.28e5, 1.15e5, 1.10e5) and a second clump at s=60-65 (1.55e5, 1.44e5, 1.35e5), both well back from the end and both matched by dips to 0.6-2e4 nearby, which is the ordinary scatter this sample shows. Flat to the last point means through-goer, and the fit end being 113 cm from any face does not change that - the cluster ended where the imaging ran out. Nothing is attached at the stop in any azimuth: the star sits at the clean tip of the spine with no arm, no dot and no speck, and the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The two non-chain rows sit well away and neither is at the end: 123009 is a two-point 0.3 cm survey speck 54.5 cm out, and C35 is a large 417-point unfitted cluster 42-60 cm from the stop which the 3-D azimuths show as a faint V-shaped object crossing the fitted track at a quite different angle around the middle of its length, not a continuation of it; on a through-goer both are delta / other in any case. The measured panels put the stop at time slice 1213 with a dead channel running through the track W range near 9390 and a dense field of dead U channels 15-45 channels away, so the imaging here is patchy, which fits a cluster that simply stops being reconstructable.

notes: THRU off a flat MIP profile to the last point, corroborated by a dead-region exit: the fit end lands on a wide dead V band (7535-7555) and a dead U channel (3700) simultaneously. No pin move.
evidence: 145.6 cm single-segment chain, enters 0.1 cm from the x anode face and the fit ends 41.9 cm from the nearest y wall. The dQ/dx core is a tight flat 4.0-5.5e4 band from s=100 straight through to the origin with almost no structure - the only excursions are two isolated points at 1.15e5 (s=13) and 1.10e5 (s=35) and a short dip to 0.5-2e4 around s=87-90, all far from the end. Over the last 10-20 cm nothing lifts: the final points read 5.6e4, 5.1e4, 4.7e4 and then 4.0-4.3e4, sitting on the same plateau as the rest of the track and nowhere near the muon reference curve, which asymptotes at 5.4e4 and would be climbing through 1.2e5 by the last centimetres. That is a MIP plateau carried to the last point, which a stopping muon cannot do. The object table has a single row, the chain segment itself, and all three 3-D azimuths show one straight spine that terminates at the star with nothing attached, no arm, no dot, no off-axis speck; the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 and no capture gamma in the ring. What makes the through-goer reading concrete here is the measured panels: the track runs up to time slice 1592 and dies exactly into dead channels - a wide hatched dead band sits at V 7535-7555 immediately against the track V 7530-7540, and a dead U channel sits at 3700-3705 right where the U track ends at 3700 - so the muon almost certainly carried on through an unreadable region rather than stopping. W is the only plane that is locally clean, with its nearest dead channels 30 away at 12070 and 110 away at 12210.

notes: Verdict STM_ONLY is solid - clean Bragg shape into the fit end, nothing attached. Medium because the michel_kind rides entirely on one two-point speck: 132002 at 31.2 cm, cos_fwd -0.72. I called it gamma on off-axis separation (about 22 cm off a 23 cm body) plus detachment; the competing reading is delta / other, which would make the kind none, and it is supported by the e azimuth where the speck looks collinear with the track extended past its far end and by trap 5 (this track is visibly curved near its far end, so cos_fwd against the local tangent at the stop is only advisory). No pin move.
evidence: Short 26.4 cm chain, 90 MeV of muon KE by range, entering 0.4 cm from the x anode face and stopping 18.6 cm inside it - the whole object lives in the corner of the volume but the fit end is clear of every face. The dQ/dx profile rises monotonically into the end and does it with the right shape: the far end at s=20-26 sits at 1-3.5e4, the middle at s=10-20 runs 4-6e4, s=3-10 runs 6-9e4, and the last two centimetres give 9.8e4 and 1.04e5, tracking the muon reference curve closely (curve 6.3e4 at s=10 against data 5-9e4, curve 8.3e4 at s=3 against data 8-10e4, curve 1.15e5 at s=0.5 against data 1.0e5). It never crosses the curve, which the rubric says it should not, and it tops out a little under the 1.2-1.35e5 band, but the shape is a clean Bragg and the chain independently tags it STM. Nothing is attached at the stop - no arm, no bridged piece, no dot within 10 cm - so this is not STM_MICHEL. The single non-chain object, 132002, is a two-point 0.9 cm speck 31.2 cm from the stop carrying 7539 e/cm, which the chain labels gamma body exclusion. It sits at cos_fwd -0.72, i.e. about 44 degrees off the backward body direction, which at 31.2 cm puts it roughly 22 cm off the muon body line - and the body is only 23 cm long end to end, so the speck is not lying on the body. The c and d azimuths both show it well clear of the spine and of the spine extended backwards, though the e azimuth foreshortens the track and makes it look almost collinear beyond the far end, which is exactly the projection accident the frames are supposed to guard against. Detached across a 31 cm charge-free gap, compact, well off the body line and inside 60 cm, so by the attachment rule it is a gamma rather than a delta, and charge is explicitly not a criterion for that call. That makes the kind detached dots on an otherwise plain STM_ONLY.

notes: Cleanest STM_MICHEL in my chunk: Bragg rise into the stop, a 12.3 cm MIP arm at a 56 degree kink, chain agrees. The only judgement is 137003, which sets both versus attached; I called gamma on forward hemisphere, same side as the arm, and a clean 8 cm charge-free gap from the arm end. No pin move.
evidence: 115.9 cm muon chain, enters 0.7 cm from the y face and stops 45.9 cm from the nearest wall. The dQ/dx profile is a proper Bragg: a 4-6e4 plateau from s=100 down to s=20, 6-7e4 through s=10-20, 7-8.5e4 over s=5-10, and 9.0e4 to 1.04e5 in the last four centimetres, following the shape of the muon curve without crossing it, exactly as the rubric says a real stopper behaves. There is no terminal collapse - the highest points are the last ones - so the pin stays on the fit last point. Leaving that stop is a 12.3 cm 21-point arm, 62001, at a 56 degree kink, whose points scatter over 2-9e4 with a mean of 5.24e4, i.e. at MIP. That is the load-bearing discrimination: a muon at its own Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so the arm is a second particle, and 12 cm at MIP is the right size for a 33.5 MeV electron. I explicitly checked the undershoot case and it does not apply - the undershoot needs a two-centimetre tip at 0.9-1.2e5, four to six times MIP, whereas this piece is long and sits at MIP, which the rubric names as the ordinary STM_MICHEL case. The three stop azimuths all show the blue arm leaving the star at a clear angle to the amber muon body and running off to one side, so this is not the muon carrying on. Beyond the arm sits 137003, a two-point 0.3 cm speck 17.0 cm from the stop at cos_fwd +0.18 carrying 1.88e4: it is in the forward hemisphere, the same side of the stop as the decay (the arm is at cos_fwd +0.55), nowhere near the muon body line, and separated from the arm far end at 8.6 cm by a charge-free gap of more than 8 cm. Isolated, compact, detached and inside 60 cm makes it a capture gamma rather than a delta by the attachment rule, and charge is not a criterion for that call. In the c and d azimuths it sits beyond the arm roughly along its direction; in e it projects off to the side, which is the usual azimuth accident. Michel plus gamma gives kind both. The W measured panel shows a wide dead band at 10085-10095 crossing the arm region, which is worth noting as a reason the arm charge may be understated.

notes: THRU off a flat-to-sagging profile at the fit end, with a dead V channel and a dead W band right at the stop as the likely exit. The mid-track dip at s=11-16 is the same depth as the terminal one, which is what convinced me the terminal dip is this track ordinary behaviour and not a collapse. No pin move.
evidence: 114.7 cm single-segment chain, enters 5.7 cm from the y face and the fit ends 44.5 cm from the nearest z wall. The dQ/dx core is a flat 4-6e4 band the whole way from s=100 to the origin, and at the end it does not rise but sags: the last points read 3.1e4 and 2.7e4 followed by a tight clump at 1.5-1.8e4, i.e. well under the track own plateau, while the muon reference curve would be climbing through 1.2e5 there. There is no local maximum anywhere near the end to make this a peak-then-collapse either - the core over s=3-10 is the same 4-6e4 as at s=90 - and a second identical dip to 0.9-1.8e4 sits mid-track at s=11-16, which shows this track drops points like that in the middle as well as at the end. The isolated high points (1.29e5 and 1.15e5 at s=26-27, 1.10e5 and 1.01e5 at s=52-53) are all well back up the body. Flat to the last point means through-goer. Nothing is attached at the end: the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the azimuths show the amber spine terminating at the star with clear space around it. The four non-chain rows are all two-point specks strung out down one side of the body at 12.6, 22.4, 28.0 and 41.9 cm from the stop with cos_fwd -0.56, -0.86, -0.86 and -0.96, and the b, d and e azimuths show them as a spray flanking the muon body rather than a decay cone at the end; on a through-goer there is no stop for a gamma tag to refer to, so all four are delta / other. The measured panels put the fit end at time slice 1277 sitting essentially on a dead V channel near 7045 with a dead W band at 11465-11475 immediately beside the track, so a dead-region exit is the natural continuation.

notes: THRU off a flat-relative-to-attenuation profile at the fit end. The apparent 1.26e5 peak at s=30-38 followed by a long decline is drift attenuation plus a delta ray - object 28010, a pdg 11 piece on the body line at 33-35 cm, sits exactly under the spike - not a Bragg peak, and 30 cm of following charge is far too long for a Michel. This track needs its charge read against its own local level because it runs along the drift and loses more than half its dQ/dx end to end. No pin move.
evidence: 242.4 cm chain running almost along the drift axis - x goes from -339.2 at the entry, 0.7 cm off the anode face, to -114.3 at the fit end, which is 71.6 cm from the nearest y wall - and the measured panels confirm it, showing the whole track inside about twenty channels in each plane while spanning 140 time slices. That geometry explains the profile: the segment means fall monotonically from 4.10e4 at the far, near-anode end through 2.62e4 in the middle to 1.94e4 and 1.80e4 in the last 22 cm, which is drift attenuation along 225 cm of extra drift, and it is why the chain also flags plateau_off_mip. Read against the track own local level rather than an absolute number, the last 20 cm at 1.0-3.5e4 is exactly what the body 40-100 cm back is doing (1.0-4.5e4), so there is no rise and no relative collapse at the fit end - the profile is flat to the last point. I did weigh the moved-pin reading, because there is a genuine spike at s=30-38 reaching 1.26e5, 1.07e5 and 9.8e4 and falling gradually backwards to 5.6e4, which has the shape of a peak followed by a 30 cm collapse. It is not one. Thirty centimetres is far too long for a Michel, the post-spike level equals the rest of the body once attenuation is accounted for, and decisively the spike sits exactly where object 28010 lies - a five-point 2.7 cm piece the chain types pdg 11, at d_min 33.2 to d_max 34.6 cm and cos_fwd -1.00, i.e. sitting on the muon body line - so the spike is a knock-on delta depositing extra charge on the body, not a Bragg peak. Nothing is attached at the fit end in any azimuth; the flow block reports no daughter, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0. The other unassigned rows are all on or beside the body far from the end - 28013, 28014 and 28015 are pdg 11 shower pieces at 135-140 cm back at cos_fwd -1.00, 76016 is a four-point 2.0 cm piece 25.9 cm back at cos_fwd -0.85 and 77017 a two-point speck 51.5 cm back at cos_fwd -0.95 - so all six non-chain rows are delta / other, which is also what the THRU convention requires. The nearest dead channels to the stop are a U band about 10 channels away at 90-100, with V and W clear for 30 and 60 channels.

notes: THRU on a flat profile alone: no visible continuation, no face within 114 cm, and no dead-region exit at the end - the profile is simply flat on the MIP plateau to its last point, which a stopping muon cannot do. Undershoot checked: there is no forward high-charge tip past the fit end (single object row, nothing drawn past the star), so the fit end is not short.
evidence: 162.9 cm single-object chain, 272 points; enters 2.4 cm from the z face at Z=296 and the fit ends deep inside the volume, 114.5 cm from the nearest face (cathode/anode both far). The dQ/dx profile is flat on its own MIP plateau all the way in: the far body sits at 5.0-5.5e4 and the last 15 cm before the origin sit at 4.5-5.2e4, i.e. slightly BELOW the plateau, with no climb of any kind toward the muon reference curve, which asymptotes to 1.6e5 at s=0 and is never approached. The scattered near-zero points at s=8-12 and s=38-41 are zero-charge fit points and are ignored. A stopping muon cannot end at MIP, so this is a through-goer whose cluster simply ran out. All three 3-D azimuths show a clean terminated line with nothing past the star - no arm, no dots, no specks in the ring - and the object table lists exactly one row, the muon chain itself, so there is nothing to attribute. f_meas shows the drawn segment ending cleanly in U, V and W with no measured charge continuing past the last point and no dead band straddling the end in U; the V plane has dead channel bands but they lie beyond the end, not across it. Chain agrees (reject no_bragg, shape_flat, is_stm 0) but the flat profile is the call on its own.

notes: THRU on the flat profile alone: no visible continuation past the last point, no face within 63 cm, and no dead band across the end in any plane - the profile is simply on the MIP plateau to the last point. Undershoot checked and absent: nothing is drawn forward of the fit end at all, let alone a short high-charge tip. Chain also rejects (no_bragg, shape_flat) but the call is made from the profile. 26003 is tagged delta / other under the THRU convention (and would be body activity anyway at 144 cm back, cos_fwd -1.0).
evidence: 387 chain points over 247 cm in two chain segments; enters 0.6 cm from the x (anode) face at X=-339 with a brown vertex square there, and the fit ends 63.5 cm from the nearest z wall, deep enough that containment is not the question. The dQ/dx profile is flat on its own plateau the whole way: the body sits at 5.0-6.0e4 from s=100 in to s=10, and the last points before the origin are 6.4e4, 6.1e4 and 6.3e4 with three low points of 4.3e4, 3.0e4 and 2.5e4 mixed among them at s=3-5. That is scatter about the same plateau, not a climb - the muon reference curve is already at 8e4 by s=20 and 1.6e5 at s=0 and the data never turns up toward it, and there is no peak-then-collapse anywhere in the last 20 cm either. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot end at MIP, so this reads as a through-goer whose cluster ran out. All three 3-D azimuths show a clean line terminating at the star with nothing past it - no arm, no dot, no speck in the 60 cm ring - and every drawn object sits 144-234 cm back toward the entry: 26004 and 26005 are the chain own segments and 26003 is a 5.2 cm 10-point pdg-11 shower speck 144-148 cm back at the kink between the two chain segments, far outside any Michel or capture-gamma radius. f_meas puts the stop circle at the top of the drawn strip in U, V and W with no measured charge beyond it; the dead-channel bands in U near 1015-1030 and in V near 4760-4790 are crossed well before the end, not at it.

notes: THRU: no Bragg rise, and the fit end is 4.6 cm from the z wall (in_fv 0), so the track leaves the volume - this is the easy kind of THRU, not the flat-profile-in-the-middle kind. Undershoot checked and absent: nothing is drawn forward of the fit end, and the last points are BELOW MIP rather than several times it. All three unassigned pdg-11 rows are on the body line 85-161 cm back and are delta / other on their own merits as well as by the THRU convention.
evidence: 298 chain points over 177 cm broken into seven fitted chain segments; enters 1.2 cm from the x (anode) face at X=339 and runs almost straight across in drift with Z pinned near 288-294, so the whole object hugs the top-back corner of the volume. The fit ends 4.6 cm from the z wall and 35 cm from the y wall, in_fv 0 - i.e. essentially at a face. The dQ/dx profile never rises: the body plateau is a low 3.0-4.0e4 with green excursions to 5e4, and the last 5 cm actually fall to 2.2-2.6e4 with one 1.2e4 point, so the profile is flat-to-falling right into the origin with nothing approaching the muon reference curve, which is at 8e4 by s=6. The one visible bump in the whole panel is at s=45-48 (7.2e4 up to 1.15e5), in the middle of the body, not at the end. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot end below MIP, and here the track walks out of the detector: no Bragg plus a stop 4.6 cm from the wall is a plain through-goer. All three azimuths show a straight line ending at the star with nothing past it - no arm, no dot, nothing in the 60 cm ring - and every non-chain row is far back: the pdg-11 shower specks 73027 (6.8 cm, 126-128 cm back), 73030 (6.7 cm, 85 cm back) and 73033 (3.4 cm, 159-161 cm back) all sit at cos_fwd -0.99, on the muon body line, so they are body activity. f_meas shows the track as a near-vertical strip in all three planes ending at time slice 1592 with the stop circle on it and no measured charge beyond; the V plane has a wide dead band at 7540-7560 well clear of the stop at 7480.

notes: THRU on the profile shape. The competing reading is a weak Bragg: the last 6 cm do sit about 20 percent above the plateau. I went against it because the maximum is at s=11-13, not at the end, and the profile falls away from the muon curve over the last 6 cm instead of tracking it - a stopper cannot put its peak twelve centimetres before its last point and then decline. Confidence medium for that end elevation. Pin left alone: the s=12 to s=0 decline is 30 percent to 1.2x MIP, not the collapse to 0.15-0.5 MIP the bridge signature needs. Undershoot checked and absent: nothing at all is drawn forward of the fit end. 27006 is on the body line 112 cm back and is delta / other on its own merits as well as by the THRU convention.
evidence: 326 chain points over 195 cm in three fitted segments, a straight line at essentially constant Z=104 running from the anode face (entry 0.1 cm from the x face at X=-340) to X=-230; the fit ends deep inside the volume, 103.6 cm from the nearest face, so this is a profile call not a containment call. Calibrating the dQ/dx panel by pixel: the body plateau is 5.0-6.2e4 through s=20-50; there is a bump at s=11-13 reaching 8.4-9.4e4; and in the last 6 cm the points run 8.46, 8.32, 8.04, 8.04, 7.27, 6.5, 6.46, 6.43, 6.22, 5.52, 4.76, 4.06 and 3.94e4, median about 6.5e4. So the last centimetres are about 20 percent above the plateau on the median but they are LOWER than the s=11-13 bump, i.e. the profile is not peaked at the end, and it falls away from the muon reference curve as s goes to zero - the curve is at 9.5e4 by s=6 and 1.3e5 by s=2 while the data is at 8e4 and 6.5e4. A stopping muon has its maximum in its last centimetre, not twelve centimetres back, and 9.4e4 is well short of the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches here. The decline from the s=12 bump is only about 30 percent and lands at 1.2x MIP, nowhere near the 0.15-0.5 of MIP that the fit-bridging collapse looks like, so the pin stays where it is. Nothing is drawn past the star in any of the three azimuths - no arm, no dot, no speck in the ring, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - and the single unassigned row 27006 is a 4.2 cm 8-point pdg-11 shower speck 112-114 cm back at cos_fwd -1.0, on the muon body line, so it is body activity. f_meas shows the stop at the top of the strip in U, V and W with no measured charge beyond; U has a dead band at channels 140-150 about ten channels past the stop at 157, which would give a dead-region exit, but V and W have no dead channel on the continuing side. Corroborating: MCS 1586 MeV against 455 MeV from range at amb 0.97, which is what a non-stopping track looks like.

notes: THRU on the flat-to-falling profile alone: no visible continuation, no face at the end (16.4 cm from the anode), and no dead band across it - the profile simply never rises and the last 6 cm sit below the body median. That is the rubric case where the cluster ended where the imaging ran out, and I am saying so rather than reaching for UNCLEAR. Confidence medium because the last 3 cm collapse to about 0.3 of MIP after a modest 7.6e4 local maximum at s=5.9, which is the shape of the fit-bridging signature; I did not move the pin because that signature also needs something past the gap for the fit to bridge to, and this item has nothing at all drawn past the star. It also needs a peak, and 7.6e4 against a 5.5e4 plateau is far short of the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches. Undershoot checked and absent: no forward piece past the fit end at any charge.
evidence: 284 chain points over 169 cm in three fitted segments; enters 0.5 cm from the z face at Z=298 and the fit ends 16.4 cm from the anode face, in_fv 1 but not deeply contained. Calibrating the dQ/dx panel by pixel: the body plateau runs 5.0-6.5e4 through s=20-50 with green/yellow excursions to 8-9e4 and two points near 1.2e5, so the body is noisy. Toward the end the profile does not climb - it falls. The last six centimetres read 7.62e4 at s=5.9, then 6.08, 6.01, 5.66e4 at s=3.0-4.3, then 4.45e4 at s=2.9, 3.24 and 2.69e4 at s=2.1, and 2.03, 1.85, 1.75e4 in the last centimetre; the median of that stretch is about 4.05e4, BELOW the body median of 5.5e4, and the data falls away from the muon reference curve (9.5e4 at s=6, 1.3e5 at s=2) rather than tracking it. So there is no Bragg rise at the fit end, which is the operative test. The last 3 cm do collapse to about 0.3 of MIP, and I considered calling that the fit bridging a gap, but the bridge mechanism needs a Michel on the far side to bridge TO and there is nothing there: all three azimuths show the spine terminating at the star with no arm, no dot and no speck anywhere in the ring, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, and the nearest drawn object is 37.5 cm back. The three unassigned rows are all on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.99 or -1.0 and far behind - 75010 a 1.5 cm 3-point survey speck at 37.5-38.4 cm, 20009 a 7.0 cm 13-point pdg-11 shower at 65-70 cm, 20006 a 7.8 cm 14-point pdg-11 shower at 85-91 cm - so body activity. f_meas puts the stop at time slice 1073 at the end of the strip in U, V and W with no measured charge beyond, and the dead bands (U 850-880 and 920, V 4655-4680, W 8420-8450) are all far from the stop channels, so there is no dead-region exit to appeal to. Corroborating: MCS 652 MeV against 400 MeV from range at amb 0.64.

notes: THRU on profile shape: the last centimetres are elevated about 30 percent over a low plateau but the rise is nothing like the muon curve, which climbs 2.4x over the same stretch, and it never approaches the 1.2-1.35e5 a real stopper reaches here. Confidence medium - this is the closest of my THRU calls to STM_ONLY. Arguing against me: the chain did NOT flag no_bragg (its rejects are shape_flat and plateau_off_mip), the end is deep in the volume, and MCS (752 MeV) and range (694 MeV) agree at amb 0.33, which is stopper-like. Arguing for me: no Bragg shape, and the whole track is charge-depleted so even a scaled-down Bragg should have reached ~8-9e4 and it reaches 5.8e4. Pin left alone; both the s=13-17 bump reading and the terminal-collapse reading were checked and neither matches. Undershoot checked and absent: nothing is drawn forward of the fit end. 92008 was my gamma candidate - isolated, 60 cm out, cos_fwd 0.09, clear of the body - but under the THRU convention gamma is not available and it is tagged delta / other; it is also a single speck in an unrelated direction with no Michel arm to define a side, which the rubric calls delta / other anyway.
evidence: 457 chain points over 301 cm in three fitted segments; enters 0.1 cm from the x (anode) face at X=-340 and the fit ends 78.6 cm from the z wall, 97.9 cm from the y wall and 58 cm from the cathode, so the end is well inside the active volume. The whole track carries low charge - the chain own reject is plateau_off_mip and the dQ/dx-based energy (484 MeV) sits 30 percent under the range energy (694 MeV) - so the body plateau is 3.5-4.5e4 rather than the usual 5.5e4. Calibrating the panel by pixel: s=40-100 runs 3-5.5e4; there is a bump at s=13.6-16.8 reaching 9.7e4, 9.7e4, 9.9e4, 10.9e4 and 11.3e4; then s=10-12 falls back to 4.2-4.5e4; and the last three centimetres sit at 5.3-5.8e4 with one outlined point near 7.0e4 at the origin. So the end is about 30 percent above the local plateau but nowhere near the muon reference curve, which is at 6.8e4 by s=11 and 1.3-1.6e5 at s=0-2: the data rises by a factor 1.35 over the last 11 cm where the curve rises by 2.4, i.e. it does not follow the Bragg shape. I also checked the other reading, that the fit overshot by 13 cm and the s=13-17 bump is the real peak: it fails because after that bump the charge returns to the 4.2-4.5e4 plateau rather than collapsing to the 0.15-0.5 of MIP the fit-bridging signature needs, so the bump is a delta or a fluctuation. Nothing at all is drawn past the star in the three azimuths - no arm, no dot, n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0 - and the drawn objects are 26006 and 26007, 2-3 cm pdg-11 shower specks 107-114 cm back on the body line at cos_fwd -1.0, plus 92008, a 1.7 cm 4-point survey speck exactly 60 cm from the stop at cos_fwd 0.09, i.e. sideways, alone, and at the very edge of the capture-gamma ring. f_meas shows the track as a near-vertical strip ending at time slice 1590 in all three planes with no measured charge past it; the dead bands (U 1850-1890, V 5630, W 9850-9900) are clear of the stop channels.

notes: MESSY, resting on three things rather than one: a 41.1 cm chain whose two ends are 9.75 cm apart; 35 of those 41 cm carrying 0.04-0.3 of MIP; and four fitted segments totalling 38 cm of length packed into a 4 cm shell 7-11 cm behind the stop. The competing reading is the chain own tidy story - STM_MICHEL / both, with 52014 the attached Michel (4.2 cm, 4.4e4, 43 deg kink) and 179011 a capture gamma 18.5 cm past the stop - and if the owner reads the curved band as a real spine that is the call. I went MESSY because there is no coherent spine to hang a stop on. Under the MESSY convention every row is tagged delta / other and michel_kind is none, which is why this record does NOT count a michel or a gamma even though I believe 52014 is electron-like. Undershoot checked and NOT applicable: 52014 is at MIP, not several times MIP, so it is a Michel-shaped piece rather than a muon tip. Confidence medium.
evidence: Three independent things say this is not one track. First the geometry: the chain is quoted as 41.1 cm over 70 points, but its entry [252.2,127.8,11.8] and its stop [245.0,123.0,16.3] are only 9.75 cm apart, so the fit doubles back on itself over most of its length. Second the charge: the dQ/dx panel puts the chain points from s=8 out to s=45 at 0.1-2.2e4, i.e. 0.04-0.3 of MIP, in a smooth wave, with only the last seven centimetres carrying real charge at 3.0-6.3e4; the chain own dQ/dx energy is 28.4 MeV against 124.4 MeV from range and its reject is plateau_off_mip. No muon deposits a tenth of MIP over 35 cm - that stretch of the fit is running through empty space. Third the object table: four fitted rows - 52006 (8.4 cm), 52009 (13.3 cm), 52010 (9.1 cm) and the unassigned shower 52007 (7.2 cm) - all have d_min 6.98-7.11 and d_max 9.24-10.87, so four pieces totalling 38 cm of length are packed into a 4 cm shell behind the stop at cos_fwd -0.66 to -0.99, overlapping each other. (I note the panel shows chain points out to s=45 while every d_max in the table is under 11 cm; those are arc length and 3-D distance respectively, which is consistent with a curling fit but is not something the table asserts, so I rest the call on the entry-to-stop distance and the charge rather than on a bounding radius.) The 3-D azimuths match: a compact tangle about 25 cm across with half a dozen vertex squares, a curved band, a closed loop of dots enclosing another segment, a short piece at the star and a diffuse halo of image points around all of it; f_meas shows the entire object as one small blob spanning about ten channels and fifty time slices in each of U, V and W. There is an attached 4.2 cm piece at the stop (52014) carrying 4.4e4 at a 43 degree kink, which is what an ordinary Michel looks like and is not the undershoot case (its charge is at MIP, not several times it), and a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 18.5 cm out at cos_fwd 0.5 which the chain calls a capture gamma; but the tag vocabulary presupposes an identified stop and this object does not have one, so under the rubric every row is delta / other.

notes: STM_MICHEL / both - the cleanest item in my chunk. Bragg peak unambiguous (11.2-12.8e4 on the muon curve over the last 5 cm), Michel unambiguous (11.6 cm arm at MIP and falling, 70 deg kink), gamma decided on attachment (2-point 0.2 cm speck 6.4 cm beyond the arm tip across a charge-free gap, 22 deg off the arm direction so it is on the Michel side, not a random-direction speck). Undershoot checked and absent for the reason stated in the evidence. Pin left alone: the two chain points in the last centimetre are 4.1e4 and 6.4e4 after the 11.2-12.8e4 peak at s=2-5, which is a one-centimetre dip with one point still above MIP - the rubric asks for a SUSTAINED collapse over several cm before moving the pin, and one low point at the very end is ordinary scatter. Flagging it here because it is the only place a reader might want the pin at about 1.5 cm; it would not change the verdict, the kind or any tag.
evidence: 259 chain points over 154.5 cm in one clean fitted segment; enters exactly at the x (anode) face, d_face 0.0, at X=340 and the fit ends 24.4 cm from the z wall and 151.5 cm from the y wall, in_fv 1. This is the textbook profile of the twelve I scanned.
